docs.t: About Dlonem — a one-person studio in Virginia
docs.x: About One person, one made-up word Dlonem is a one-person studio. The apps, the mods, the videos and the Discord servers are all built and supported by the same person. Home › About Who this is I’m Thomas. Dlonem LLC is my studio, and for most practical purposes Dlonem LLC is me. I write the code, draw the icons, record the videos, and answer the support email. If you send a bug report, it lands in front of the person who caused the bug. The name is a made-up word with no meaning behind it. It came out of a random name generator years ago and stuck, which is a much less interesting origin than people expect. The full story of how I got there (by way of a Roblox account called Carlman622, a World of Warcraft warlock, and a decade as Mr.Potato) is on the Legacy page , if you want the long version. What I make Four phone apps. Three of them are Break Buddy apps, one each for cannabis, caffeine and nicotine, and they all do the same job: help you take a break from a habit and show you plainly what is happening while you do. The fourth, Tiny Dragon Hoard , is a cozy idle game about a dragon who collects things. All four are here . Two Crusader Kings III mods. The Long Night & Azor Ahai builds the Long Night out as a real endgame for the A Game of Thrones total conversion, and Supernatural adds vampires, werewolves, witches and hunters to the base game. Both are free, both are on the Steam Workshop, and both can be installed by hand without Steam . Five Discord communities and a YouTube channel. The oldest community has been running since 2016, and the newest is a guild for World of Warcraft: Forever . The channel is where all of this started, and it is still the reason most people find anything else I make. Both are linked from the Community page . How I build things A few rules I hold to, because they are the reason I started making my own apps rather than using someone else’s: Your data stays on your device. The Break Buddy apps store what you enter (your history, your notes, your reminders) locally. I do not collect it and I cannot read it. The privacy policy is short because there is not much to disclose. No accounts. You should not need to sign up for anything to track your own coffee. No subscriptions. Where an app has a paid unlock, it is a one-time purchase. I am not going to charge you every month for a habit tracker. Estimates are labelled as estimates. The apps show you timelines drawn from published research, and where a number is a projection rather than a fact, it says so. These are wellness tools. They are not medical advice, and they do not claim to be. Getting in touch The fastest route depends on what you need. Each app has its own support address, listed on its policy page . For anything else, whether a bug, a question, a feature idea, or business, contact@dlonem.com reaches me. There is more detail, including what to put in a bug report so I can fix it, on the support page . For the mods specifically, the Discord servers are faster than email, because the rest of the community is there too and someone has usually hit your problem already.

docs.t: Caffeine Break Buddy — Caffeine Tracker & Withdrawal Timeline
docs.x: Caffeine Break Buddy Get the magic of your morning cup back A free caffeine tracker, and an honest guide to what happens when you cut back. It won't shame you about your coffee habit or ask for a willpower marathon, and nothing you enter ever leaves your phone. Get it on Google Play App Store — coming soon Android 1.0.21 , updated 30 September 2026 Home › Apps › Caffeine Break Buddy 12–24h After your last dose, before withdrawal starts 50% Of people get a headache in controlled studies 2–9 Days it takes, start to finish The mechanism What caffeine tolerance is Adenosine is the molecule that makes you feel sleepy. It builds up across the day and settles onto receptors that dial your alertness down. Caffeine works by blocking those receptors . It doesn't add energy so much as hide the tiredness. With daily use your body adapts. In humans, a week of 250 mg three times a day raised the density of adenosine A2A receptors on blood platelets by about 31% , and made them measurably more sensitive. In rodent brain, chronic caffeine raises A1 receptor binding by roughly 17–20% . More receptors, or more sensitive ones, means the same coffee blocks a smaller share of them. That is tolerance, and it's a physical adaptation rather than a failure of discipline. Three things most guides get wrong Nobody has measured caffeine receptor density in a living human brain. So when a site tells you your receptors reset in exactly 7, 14 or 30 days, that number is invented. The figures above come from human blood cells and from rodent brains. What has been measured in people is symptoms, and those resolve in two to nine days. Tolerance is specific to each effect. It's essentially complete for caffeine's effects on blood pressure and adrenaline within one to four days of daily use, and complete for the subjective buzz within about three weeks. But the effect on physical performance is stubborn: cyclists still got a ~4–5% power boost after 15 straight days of daily dosing. "Caffeine does nothing for regular drinkers" overstates a finding that is still contested. You don't have to be a heavy drinker. Withdrawal has been produced from as little as 100 mg a day , and after only three days of regular use. In one study of people averaging 235 mg (about two and a half cups), 52% reported moderate or severe headache when it was swapped for placebo. Hour by hour What the timeline looks like Timings vary with dose and metabolism, but the shape is consistent enough that researchers can put hours on it. 0–12 HOURS Nothing much. Caffeine's half-life is roughly three to five hours in most adults, so levels are falling but you're not empty yet. Individual values run from about two hours to ten; pregnancy and oestrogen-containing contraceptives lengthen it substantially, and smoking shortens it. 12–24 HOURS Onset. This is when it starts, and if you drink your coffee in the morning that lands squarely on the following afternoon. Headache comes first for about half of people, typically bilateral and throbbing, then fatigue and a sense of being foggy rather than tired. 20–51 HOURS The peak, and the hard part. Headache, real fatigue, low alertness, drowsiness, depressed or irritable mood, difficulty concentrating. Some people also get flu-like symptoms, nausea, or muscle stiffness. About 13% of people in controlled studies hit distress or impairment significant enough to matter at work. DAYS 3–5 It lifts. The headache is usually the first thing to go. Energy is still flat and concentration still annoying, but the trend is clearly downward. DAYS 5–9 Done, for almost everyone. The systematic review puts total duration at two to nine days, with the long tail belonging to people who were on high daily doses. AFTER If you go back, you need far less than you used to. Tolerance to the subjective effects is what fades fastest, so your old four-cup habit will hit like six. This is the part people enjoy, and the part they overshoot. Practical What helps, and what's a waste of money What helps Taper rather than stop dead. Standard clinical advice is cutting intake 25–50% every few days. Withdrawal severity tracks the dose you stop from , so a smaller last step means a smaller landing. Don't start the day before something that matters. The peak is 20–51 hours out. Friday morning means a wrecked Saturday. Expect the headache instead of diagnosing yourself. Half of people get one. Knowing it's on the schedule is most of the battle. If you get migraines, talk to someone first. In a small randomised trial of episodic migraine sufferers, abrupt caffeine withdrawal triggered severe attacks in seven of nine people. Move the ritual, not just the drug. Most restarts are the 3pm walk to the machine rather than a craving. Track the days. A visible number is harder to abandon than a vague intention. Doesn't work "Detox" teas and cleanses. Tolerance is receptor adaptation, not residue. There's nothing to flush. Quitting to fix your hydration. Coffee doesn't dehydrate you: in 50 habitual drinkers it hydrated as well as an equal volume of water. Bracing for anxiety. Anxiety is an effect of taking caffeine. There's little evidence it's a withdrawal symptom, and the validated list points the other way: drowsiness and fatigue. Expecting insomnia. Also not on the validated list, and polysomnography during withdrawal found no change in sleep time, latency, or architecture. Assuming it's psychological. A balanced placebo study in 87 coffee drinkers found the pharmacology, not the expectation, drove the symptoms. Any promise of a "receptor reset" on a fixed date. That measurement has never been made in a human brain. Ready to cut back? The caffeine guide has a caffeine table for common drinks, a cup-by-cup taper, and what to do about the headache. It's short, because there isn't much to disclose. Get it on Google Play App Store — coming soon Common questions Caffeine withdrawal FAQ How long does caffeine withdrawal last? Two to nine days. The systematic review that settled this looked at 57 experimental and 9 survey studies: symptoms typically start 12 to 24 hours after the last dose, peak between 20 and 51 hours, and run two to nine days in total. Higher daily doses mean longer and rougher. How much coffee is enough to get withdrawal? Less than you'd think. Symptoms have been produced by stopping doses as low as 100 mg a day (one small coffee), and three days of daily use is enough for them to appear. In a group averaging 235 mg a day, 52% reported moderate or severe headache when their caffeine was secretly swapped for placebo. How long until my tolerance resets? Nobody knows, and that's the useful answer. Caffeine receptor density has never been measured in a living human brain, so every confident "reset in N days" figure online is made up. What's measured: symptoms clear in two to nine days, and human blood-cell receptor markers return to baseline within roughly 48 hours. Tolerance to the alertness effect is what you care about, and most people notice a real difference within a week or two. Should I taper or quit cold turkey? Taper, probably. Cutting 25–50% every few days is the standard clinical recommendation, and it's mechanistically sound because withdrawal severity scales with the dose you stop from. But be aware no trial has ever directly compared tapering against stopping abruptly for caffeine, so the size of the advantage is unknown. There's also an odd finding worth knowing: people told exactly when their dose was being cut reported more withdrawal than people who weren't told. Is caffeine withdrawal a real diagnosis? Yes. It's in DSM-5 as 292.0 (F15.93) and in ICD-11 as 6C48.3, requiring at least three symptoms within 24 hours plus significant distress or impairment. Caffeine addiction , on the other hand, is not a diagnosis: DSM-5 explicitly declined to include caffeine use disorder and parked it in the section for conditions needing further study. Will quitting help me sleep? Timing matters more than quitting. A meta-analysis of 24 studies found caffeine cut total sleep time by about 45 minutes and sleep efficiency by 7%, but the same work found 107 mg needs

docs.t: Apps
docs.x: The apps Simple tools, no accounts, no clutter Everything you enter stays on your device. THC Break Buddy is on Google Play and the App Store; the rest are on Google Play, with iOS on the way. T THC Break Buddy Habit tracker A mindful tracker for cutting back on cannabis at your own pace. Log your breaks, watch your streaks grow, and see what you're saving. All of it is stored privately on your device. Get it on Google Play Download on the App Store Learn more about a tolerance break → C Caffeine Break Buddy Habit tracker The same approach, pointed at your coffee habit. Track cups skipped, money saved, and how long you've kept it up, without the app passing judgment. Get it on Google Play App Store: coming soon Learn more about cutting back on caffeine → N Nicotine Break Buddy Habit tracker The Break Buddy approach for quitting or cutting back on nicotine, whether that is cigarettes, vapes, pouches or dip. Real milestones, clear timelines, and a plan that adjusts to how your week went. Get it on Google Play App Store: coming soon Learn more about quitting nicotine → D Tiny Dragon Hoard Cozy idle game Every flight fills your hoard. Every dragon flies differently. Raise a roost of one-of-a-kind dragons, torch castle walls, and build a treasury of legend. Free to play, with no sign-up. Get it on Google Play App Store: coming soon Learn more about the game → The promise Privacy-friendly means it No accounts required. Your tracking data never leaves your device. The full details are in the privacy policy . It's short, because there isn't much to disclose. The obvious question Why three apps and not one Three of these do the same job for different substances, and the reasonable question is why they are not one app with a dropdown at the top. The first reason is that the timelines are not the same shape. Caffeine clears in hours and the hard part is a few days of headaches. Nicotine's worst stretch is measured in days and the cravings outlast it by months. A cannabis tolerance break is measured in weeks, and how long it takes depends on how much was in your system to begin with. An app that tried to be all three at once would end up vague about all three, and vague is the one thing a countdown cannot afford to be. The second reason is more practical. Someone cutting back on coffee should not have to install something with a cannabis leaf on the icon, and someone quitting vapes should not have to scroll past features that have nothing to do with them. Separate apps mean each one can say exactly what it is on the home screen and nothing else. They do share an engine underneath. A fix to how a streak survives a bad day, or to how the recovery curve handles a slip, gets made once and rolls out to all three. That is why they tend to update within days of each other. The same four rules What every one of them does the same way No account, ever. There is no sign-up screen, no email field and no password. You open the app and start. This is not a feature I am saving for later; there is nothing to sign into because there is no server to sign into. Your data stays on the phone. What you log is written to your device and read back from your device. It is not uploaded, synced or analysed, which is also why losing the phone loses the history — an honest trade I would rather state plainly than hide. They work with no signal. On a plane, in a basement, with the phone in airplane mode: the timers still run and the history still opens. Nothing is a subscription. Where there is something to buy it is a one-time unlock that stays unlocked. I am not going to charge you every year to keep looking at your own data. The privacy policies spell out the specifics for each app, and they are short, because there is not much to disclose. Not sure which Pick by what you are actually cutting back on Coffee, energy drinks or pre-workout, and you want to know when the headaches stop: Caffeine Break Buddy . Cigarettes, vapes, pouches or dip: Nicotine Break Buddy . A cannabis tolerance break, especially one with a date you need to be clear by: THC Break Buddy . And if you are not cutting back on anything and just want something to poke at on a break, Tiny Dragon Hoard is a cozy idle game about dragons filling a treasury, which is a different kind of useful. Guides Before you start a break Each app page explains the timeline for its habit. These guides cover the rest: getting ready, getting through the hard days, and what to do afterwards. How much is in what you drink, a cup-by-cup taper, and handling the headache. Quitting nicotine . A plan for cigarettes, vapes and pouches, with free quitlines and text programs.

docs.t: Nicotine Break Buddy — Quit Tracker & Withdrawal Timeline
docs.x: Nicotine Break Buddy Watch your body heal, day by day One calm quit app for cigarettes, vapes, pouches and dip. An honest timeline of what withdrawal does, no shame about slips, and nothing you enter ever leaves your phone. Get it on Google Play App Store — coming soon Android 1.0.12 , updated 30 September 2026 Free. Optional $9.99 one-time unlock, never a subscription Home › Apps › Nicotine Break Buddy 8 days Where most unaided quit attempts fail 2–4 Weeks until most symptoms are gone 6–12 Weeks for brain receptors to reach non-smoker levels The mechanism What nicotine did to your brain, and what undoes it Nicotine binds nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (chiefly the α4β2 subtype) and leaves them desensitised. Your brain compensates by building more of them . Imaging studies find smokers carry roughly 26–36% more of these receptors in the cortex and about 27% more in the striatum than non-smokers. That's why the first cigarette of the day lands so hard and why the tenth barely registers. PET work found that one or two puffs occupies half of those receptors for about three hours, and a whole cigarette occupies 88% . Smoking to satiety hits 95%. A daily smoker keeps them saturated essentially all day, so withdrawal is what happens every time the level drops, many times a day. The good news is that this reverses, and it has been measured in living human brains. Receptor levels stay elevated through about a month of abstinence and return to non-smoker levels by six to twelve weeks . An earlier, smaller study put it closer to three weeks. Either way it's a matter of weeks rather than years, and it's a physical repair, measured directly. One caveat Recovery isn't uniform. The occipital cortex was the last region still measurably elevated at four weeks in the best-designed study, and cerebellar levels at that point tracked with how strongly people were still craving. Feeling fine on paper and still getting hit by urges at week five is normal. It isn't a relapse warning. Every kind of nicotine Built for every product Most quit apps were built for smoking and bolt everything else on afterwards. This one starts from what you use. Cigarettes Peak nicotine within about three minutes of finishing one Vapes & e-cigs Lower peak than a cigarette, but high-strength liquid gets close Pouches A comparable peak, delivered far more slowly, over roughly an hour Dip & chew Slow release, long contact, heavy total daily load Cigars Tracked by count and session rather than pack maths Nicotine gum Counts too, if it's become the habit rather than the exit Hour by hour, then week by week What the timeline looks like The research puts real numbers on this, and they're more encouraging than the folklore. 0–8 HOURS Nicotine's half-life is about two hours. Blood levels peak as you finish and fall fast, and meaningful levels are gone within six to eight hours. Cravings can start about 30 minutes after the last one. DAY 1–2 Onset. Irritability, anxiety, restlessness, trouble concentrating, appetite up, sleep disrupted. Worth knowing: DSM-5 requires four of seven symptoms within 24 hours, and craving is not one of them, which surprises most people. DAY 2–3 The peak. This is when urges are strongest and mood is worst. If you are going to feel like a different person, it's now. FIRST 8 DAYS The window that decides it. Most relapse among people quitting unaided happens inside these eight days. A rough stretch here doesn't mean you're doing it wrong. It means this is the part to plan support around, rather than relying on willpower. WEEK 2–4 It resolves. docs.s: What nicotine did to your brain, and what undoes it
docs.x: The mechanism Nicotine binds nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (chiefly the α4β2 subtype) and leaves them desensitised. Your brain compensates by building more of them . Imaging studies find smokers carry roughly 26–36% more of these receptors in the cortex and about 27% more in the striatum than non-smokers. That's why the first cigarette of the day lands so hard and why the tenth barely registers. PET work found that one or two puffs occupies half of those receptors for about three hours, and a whole cigarette occupies 88% . Smoking to satiety hits 95%. A daily smoker keeps them saturated essentially all day, so withdrawal is what happens every time the level drops, many times a day. The good news is that this reverses, and it has been measured in living human brains. Receptor levels stay elevated through about a month of abstinence and return to non-smoker levels by six to twelve weeks . An earlier, smaller study put it closer to three weeks. Either way it's a matter of weeks rather than years, and it's a physical repair, measured directly. One caveat Recovery isn't uniform. The occipital cortex was the last region still measurably elevated at four weeks in the best-designed study, and cerebellar levels at that point tracked with how strongly people were still craving. Feeling fine on paper and still getting hit by urges at week five is normal. It isn't a relapse warning.

docs.x: Common questions How long does nicotine withdrawal last? Two to four weeks for most of it. The systematic review of abstinence effects found withdrawal begins in the first one to two days, peaks in the first week, and total scores are back at or near pre-quit levels by two weeks, three to four at the outside. Cravings and increased appetite are the two that can run longer. How long until my receptors go back to normal? Six to twelve weeks, and unusually for this kind of claim, it has been measured in living human brains. Smokers scanned during abstinence still had elevated nicotinic receptor levels at one month; by six to twelve weeks they matched non-smokers. A smaller earlier study using a different tracer put it at around 21 days. Should I quit cold turkey or cut down? The evidence doesn't support cutting down as the easier path. The largest head-to-head randomised trial (697 smokers, everyone getting nicotine replacement and behavioural support) found abrupt quitting beat a two-week taper at both four weeks (49% vs 39%) and six months (22% vs 16%). A Cochrane review of 22 studies found the two approaches equivalent. So: equivalent at best, worse in the biggest single trial. If you do reduce first, the evidence supports using fast-acting NRT or varenicline during the reduction phase. Why is the first week so much harder than I expected? Because that's where the biology is. Urges peak on days two to three, and a review of people quitting without help found most relapse happens within the first eight days. Roughly 3 to 5% of unaided quitters are still abstinent at six to twelve months, which says less about anyone's character than about the value of using the tools that work. How long does a single craving last? A few minutes. To be straight about it, this specific number isn't well established in the research literature, and the official sources disagree: Ireland's HSE says three to five minutes, the NHS says up to fifteen. What is well established is the long arc: urges decline exponentially, about 13% of people still report strong ones at six months, and by twelve months essentially nobody does. Will quitting make my anxiety or depression worse? The evidence points the opposite way. A meta-analysis of 26 longitudinal studies found people who quit scored lower on anxiety, depression, stress and mixed anxiety-depression than people who kept smoking, and higher on positive affect and psychological quality of life. The effect sizes were comparable to antidepressant treatment, and just as large for people with psychiatric diagnoses. These are observational studies, so read it as a strong association rather than proof, but "smoking calms my nerves" does not survive contact with the data. Does vaping help you quit or not? Randomised trials give high-certainty evidence that nicotine vapes beat nicotine replacement therapy for quitting, by about four extra quitters per hundred. But real-world data are less kind: daily vaping was associated with more than double the odds of abstinence, while non-daily vaping showed no benefit at all, and both patterns were linked to higher relapse risk among people who'd already made a month. Fewer receptors means less effect from the same amount. That is tolerance, and it is a physical change rather than a matter of willpower. A PET imaging study of chronic daily cannabis smokers found roughly 20% fewer CB1 receptors in cortical brain regions compared with non-users. Day by day What each stretch feels like Timelines vary, but the shape is consistent from one person to the next. DAY 1 Usually easy, sometimes suspiciously so. Sleep may already be a little off. DAYS 2–6 The peak, and the hard part. Insomnia; vivid, exhausting dreams as REM sleep rebounds; no appetite; irritability well out of proportion to whatever set you off; anxiety, low mood, restlessness; night sweats, chills, headaches. If you are on day four and feel terrible, that is the schedule rather than a personal failure. DAYS 7–14 It lifts. Sleep is still imperfect but improving, appetite returns, mood evens out. Most acute symptoms are done inside this window. DAYS 14–21 This is where it gets pleasant. Dreams settle, sleep gets good (often better than before), and some people report sharper mornings. DAYS 21–30 Tolerance is meaningfully reset. If you go back, you need far less than you think . People overshoot here all the time and have an unpleasant evening. Fighting it makes it worse, and it resolves on its own. Eat on a schedule even without appetite. Skipping meals makes the irritability worse. Track the days. Tolerance is a matter of receptor density rather than residue, so there is nothing to flush. Sweating it out in a sauna. Same problem. It feels productive and does nothing for tolerance. That's a substitution rather than a break, and it lands you back here in a couple of months. Anything promising a reset in three days. The imaging research used four weeks. Planning a break? docs.t: How to Cut Back on Caffeine Without the Headache
docs.x: Caffeine break Cutting back on caffeine Count what you take, taper it without the misery, get through the headache, and keep the benefit afterwards. Start here What this guide covers From Dlonem · Updated 27 September 2026 · General information, not medical advice The Caffeine Break Buddy page explains what caffeine tolerance is and lays out the withdrawal timeline hour by hour. This guide is the practical side: counting what you actually take, building a taper, handling the headache, and coming back to coffee without drifting straight back to where you started. If you are pregnant, get migraines, or take medication that interacts with caffeine, talk to your clinician before you change your intake. Step one Count what you actually take Most people underestimate their intake, mostly because cup sizes and brews vary so much. The US Food and Drug Administration lists a regular 12-ounce brewed coffee at anywhere from 113 to 247 mg. Typical amounts: Source Caffeine Brewed coffee, 8 oz (240 mL) about 96 mg Brewed coffee, 12 oz (FDA range) 113 to 247 mg Espresso, one 1 oz shot about 63 mg Instant coffee, 8 oz about 62 mg Decaf coffee, 8 oz (FDA) 2 to 15 mg Black tea, 8 oz about 48 mg Green tea, 8 oz about 29 mg Caffeinated soda, 12 oz (FDA range) 23 to 83 mg Energy drink, 12 oz (FDA range) 41 to 246 mg Energy shot, 2 oz about 200 mg Dark chocolate (60 to 69%), 1 oz about 24 mg Excedrin Migraine or Extra Strength, per caplet 65 mg Figures are Mayo Clinic's unless marked FDA. The chocolate figure is USDA's and the Excedrin figure is from its label. Two sources are easy to miss. Some over-the-counter headache pills contain caffeine, and the Excedrin label itself warns that its recommended dose contains about as much caffeine as a cup of coffee. Supplements and pre-workout are harder: in a study of 53 caffeine-containing supplements, only 28 listed an amount, and daily doses ranged from 1 to 829 mg. Guarana, yerba mate, kola nut and green tea extract are all caffeine under another name. Add up a normal day. For reference, the FDA cites 400 mg a day as an amount not generally associated with negative effects for most adults, while noting that people vary widely in how sensitive they are and how fast they clear it. Step two Build the taper The standard clinical advice is to cut intake by 25 to 50% every few days, because withdrawal is milder when the step you stop from is smaller. The easiest way to do that without thinking about milligrams is to keep the number of cups the same and change what is in them, one cup at a time. Swapping in decaf usually does not change the taste much, and brewing tea for less time cuts its caffeine. An example for someone on three 8-ounce mugs of brewed coffee a day, about 290 mg. Each step lasts three or four days: Step The three mugs About Start Regular, regular, regular 290 mg 1 Regular, regular, half-caf 240 mg 2 Regular, half-caf, half-caf 195 mg 3 Half-caf, half-caf, half-caf 150 mg 4 Half-caf, half-caf, decaf 105 mg 5 Half-caf, decaf, decaf 65 mg 6 Decaf, decaf, decaf under 45 mg The amounts assume about 96 mg for a regular mug, half that for half-caf, and decaf at the FDA's 2 to 15 mg. The whole plan takes two to three weeks. The early steps are smaller than the published 25 to 50% and grow toward it; the last one is a big share of a small amount. If a step gives you a headache, stay on it a few days longer. If you want to go faster, skip every other row. Swap the afternoon cup first, since it is the one most likely to be costing you sleep. Days one to three Handling the headache The withdrawal headache has a formal definition, and two parts of it are useful. It is relieved within an hour by about 100 mg of caffeine, and it resolves within seven days of stopping completely. The clinical reference for caffeine withdrawal suggests ordinary painkillers such as acetaminophen, ibuprofen or aspirin, and water and rest, especially over the first one to three days. Read the painkiller label. A caffeinated tablet quietly puts back the dose you just took out. Using combination painkillers on ten or more days a month for more than three months is also a recognized cause of rebound headaches for people who already get headaches. A small dose is a legitimate fix. The same clinical reference notes that 50 to 100 mg of caffeine gives rapid relief. If the headache is making the day unworkable, a small cup is not failure. Carry on from a smaller step. The weekend headache is the same thing. The diagnostic criteria count caffeine that is "interrupted or delayed," not only stopped. Sleeping in and having your first coffee three hours late can set it off, which is why some people only get headaches on Saturdays. If you get migraines, talk to someone before you start. Caffeine withdrawal is a known migraine trigger, and the app page has the study. Energy Getting through the afternoon A short nap, if you can take one. In a sleep-lab comparison, a 10-minute nap improved alertness straight away and the benefit lasted up to about two and a half hours. A 30-minute nap left people groggy first. CDC guidance for shift workers says the same: under 20 minutes, with an alarm. Move for ten minutes. In a small study of 18 sleep-deprived young women, ten minutes of walking up and down stairs raised their sense of energy more than a 50 mg caffeine capsule did. Get daylight early. Bright light during the day helps set your body clock and supports sleep at night. Whether it directly makes you more alert in the moment is less certain, so count it as an investment in tonight's sleep. Keep the ritual. A lot of what a coffee break gives you is the break. Decaf or herbal tea at the same time, in the same mug, keeps that part intact. Before you change anything Who should check first Pregnancy. The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists says moderate caffeine consumption, under 200 mg a day, does not appear to be a major contributing factor in miscarriage or preterm birth, and that the link with growth restriction remains undetermined. Your own clinician is the one to set a target. Some medications slow caffeine down. Fluvoxamine, an antidepressant, is a strong example: in one study, caffeine's half-life went from about 5 hours to 31. The antibiotic ciprofloxacin stretched it from about 5 to 8 hours, and oral contraceptives from about 5.4 to 7.9. If you start one of these, the same coffee lasts much longer. Your pharmacist can check anything else you take. Quitting smoking changes your coffee. Chemicals in tobacco smoke speed up the enzyme that clears caffeine. When you stop, clearance drops by about a third within days. In one study, four days off cigarettes raised the amount of caffeine in the blood over a day by 46%, and levels can stay higher for months. The same coffee hits harder, and the jitters and poor sleep can pass for nicotine withdrawal. New Zealand's medicines regulator suggests halving caffeine when you quit. This comes from the smoke, not the nicotine: it happens when you stop smoking even if you use patches, and quitting a vape or pouches does not cause it. The nicotine guide has more. Very high doses are dangerous. The FDA says toxic effects such as seizures can occur from rapidly taking around 1,200 mg. Pure powdered caffeine is the real hazard: one teaspoon can hold as much as 28 cups of coffee, and these products have contributed to at least two deaths in the US. Medical experts advise against energy drinks for children and teens. After Going back to coffee If you go back, the goal is to keep what the break bought you. Tolerance to caffeine's lift comes from taking it every day, and it comes back quickly, so these are worth deciding before the last day: A daily ceiling well under where you started. The FDA's 400 mg is an outer limit for most adults, not a target. A cutoff time. Common sleep advice is no caffeine in the six hours before bed. In a sleep-lab study, 400 mg taken six hours before bed still cost more than an hour of sleep. Decaf for the second cup when you want the cup and not the caffeine. A recount now and then. Redo the tally from step one once a month. Creep happens one bigger cup at a time. The app Keep count Caffeine Break Buddy is the tracker I built for this. You log coffee, espresso, tea, energy drinks, soda, pre-workout, pills or chocolate, watch it clear your system between doses, and see your tolerance recover. It needs no account, and nothing you enter leaves your phone. It is free on Android: get it here . Taking a break from something else? There is a guide to cannabis tolerance breaks and one to quitting nicotine . References Sources US FDA. Spilling the Beans: How Much Caffeine is Too Much? Link Mayo Clinic. Caffeine content for coffee, tea, soda and more. Link Mayo Clinic. Caffeine: How much is too much? Link USDA National Agricultural Library. Caffeine content of foods (SR Legacy). Link Excedrin Migraine, Drug Facts label. DailyMed. Link Excedrin Extra Strength caplets, product label

docs.t: CK3 mods not working? Load order, patches and error logs
docs.x: Crusader Kings III When CK3 mods break Load order, checksums, error logs, and how to find the one mod out of forty that is ruining your campaign. Written from years of getting this wrong. Right now · checked 1 October 2026 CK3 1.20 just came out Paradox released Crusader Kings III 1.20, the “Crozier” update, on 30 September 2026, alongside the By God Alone expansion. If your mods stopped working in the last day or two, that is almost certainly why. The game moved, and most mods have not caught up yet. A Game of Thrones is still built for CK3 1.19.0.6. Every AGOT submod depends on it, The Long Night & Azor Ahai included, so an AGOT playset needs the game on 1.19.0.6 until AGOT updates. Staying on an older version below covers how to roll back on Steam. Supernatural is already updated: since 2.36 it runs on 1.20. If you are staying on 1.19 for AGOT, use version 2.35a , the last one built for it. For any other mod, check its Workshop page for a 1.20 update before you report a bug. If the author has not posted one yet, the mod is out of date rather than broken, and the rest of this page still applies. Start here The short version Most broken CK3 setups come down to one of four things, and they are worth ruling out in this order before you do anything more involved. One: load order. Two mods changing the same file, in the wrong order. Two: a game patch. CK3 updated, your mods did not. Three: a leftover. An old version of a mod still sitting in your mod folder, still being read. Four: the descriptor. A hand-installed mod whose .mod file points at the wrong place. The rest of this page is each of those in detail, plus how to read the error log and how to find a bad mod without uninstalling everything. If you are installing one of my mods by hand, the step-by-step lives on the download pages instead: The Long Night and Supernatural . Where things live The three folders that matter Mods you installed by hand, and the .mod files that describe them, live in your CK3 user directory: Windows Documents\Paradox Interactive\Crusader Kings III\mod\ macOS ~/Documents/Paradox Interactive/Crusader Kings III/mod/ Linux ~/.local/share/Paradox Interactive/Crusader Kings III/mod/ Mods you subscribed to on the Steam Workshop do not go there. They land in Steam's own folder, under CK3's app id: Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\1158310\ Each subfolder in there is named after the Workshop item's id, which is the long number at the end of its Workshop URL. That is how you work out which downloaded folder is which mod. The third folder is the one almost nobody opens, and it is where the answers are: Documents\Paradox Interactive\Crusader Kings III\logs\ The launcher never mentions it. It holds error.log , and more on that further down. The one rule Lower wins This is the single most useful thing to understand about CK3 mods, and it is one sentence. When two mods contain the same file, the one lower in the playset overwrites the one above it . That is the whole mechanic. The load order is not a suggestion or a loading sequence; it is a stack of overwrites, resolved top to bottom, file by file. Two consequences follow, and between them they explain most "why is this mod not doing anything" reports. The first: a mod that seems to have no effect is usually not broken. It is being overwritten by something below it that touches the same files. Move it down. The second, which catches people out more: sorting a mod below another one is not the same as disabling it. If two mods ship the same file and you push one to the bottom, the one at the bottom wins that file — but every file the loser has that the winner does not is still loaded. You end up with a mix of both. When two mods are genuinely incompatible, the fix is to untick one, not to reorder it. Compatibility patches exist because of this rule. A patch is a mod that contains the merged version of the files two other mods both changed, which is why a patch always goes last: it has to be the one doing the final overwrite. After an update The patch that broke everything CK3 updates. Your mods do not update at the same moment, because a human has to go and fix each one. This is the most common cause of a save that will not load and a main menu full of red. What actually happens: a mod replaces whole files. When Paradox changes one of those files in a patch, the mod is still handing the game its older copy, which now refers to things that moved or no longer exist. The mod is not corrupt. It is out of date, which looks identical from the outside. The supported_version line in a mod's descriptor is the author saying which game version they last checked it against. The launcher shows a warning when that does not match your game. Take the warning seriously but not literally — plenty of mods keep working across a patch that changed nothing they touch, and an author who has not updated the line yet is common. It is a hint, not a verdict. If a patch just landed and everything is on fire, the honest answer is usually to wait a few days. Big mods get fixed. Starting a fresh campaign on a broken setup is how you lose thirty hours of it later. Finding the culprit Halve it, do not hunt it With forty mods enabled and a crash on load, the instinct is to guess which one it is. Do not guess. Halving finds it in about five or six launches no matter how many mods you have, and guessing can take all evening. Turn off the bottom half of your playset. Launch. If it works, the problem is in the half you turned off; if it still breaks, it is in the half you kept. Either way you have just eliminated half your list. Take the half that contains the problem, cut that in half, and go again. Forty mods becomes twenty, ten, five, three, two, one. Two things make this go wrong. Keep any mod that others depend on switched on the whole time — for a Game of Thrones setup that means AGOT itself, since every submod fails without it and you will get a false result on every round. docs.t: CK3 mods not working? Load order, patches and error logs
docs.x: Start here Most broken CK3 setups come down to one of four things, and they are worth ruling out in this order before you do anything more involved. One: load order. Two mods changing the same file, in the wrong order. Two: a game patch. CK3 updated, your mods did not. Three: a leftover. An old version of a mod still sitting in your mod folder, still being read. Four: the descriptor. A hand-installed mod whose .mod file points at the wrong place. The rest of this page is each of those in detail, plus how to read the error log and how to find a bad mod without uninstalling everything. If you are installing one of my mods by hand, the step-by-step lives on the download pages instead: The Long Night and Supernatural .

docs.t: CK3 mods not working? Load order, patches and error logs
docs.x: Where things live Mods you installed by hand, and the .mod files that describe them, live in your CK3 user directory: Windows Documents\Paradox Interactive\Crusader Kings III\mod\ macOS ~/Documents/Paradox Interactive/Crusader Kings III/mod/ Linux ~/.local/share/Paradox Interactive/Crusader Kings III/mod/ Mods you subscribed to on the Steam Workshop do not go there. They land in Steam's own folder, under CK3's app id: Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\1158310\ Each subfolder in there is named after the Workshop item's id, which is the long number at the end of its Workshop URL. That is how you work out which downloaded folder is which mod. The third folder is the one almost nobody opens, and it is where the answers are: Documents\Paradox Interactive\Crusader Kings III\logs\ The launcher never mentions it. It holds error.log , and more on that further down.

docs.t: CK3 mods not working? Load order, patches and error logs
docs.x: The one rule This is the single most useful thing to understand about CK3 mods, and it is one sentence. When two mods contain the same file, the one lower in the playset overwrites the one above it . That is the whole mechanic. The load order is not a suggestion or a loading sequence; it is a stack of overwrites, resolved top to bottom, file by file. Two consequences follow, and between them they explain most "why is this mod not doing anything" reports. The first: a mod that seems to have no effect is usually not broken. It is being overwritten by something below it that touches the same files. Move it down. The second, which catches people out more: sorting a mod below another one is not the same as disabling it. If two mods ship the same file and you push one to the bottom, the one at the bottom wins that file — but every file the loser has that the winner does not is still loaded. You end up with a mix of both. When two mods are genuinely incompatible, the fix is to untick one, not to reorder it. Compatibility patches exist because of this rule. A patch is a mod that contains the merged version of the files two other mods both changed, which is why a patch always goes last: it has to be the one doing the final overwrite.

docs.t: CK3 mods not working? Load order, patches and error logs
docs.x: After an update CK3 updates. Your mods do not update at the same moment, because a human has to go and fix each one. This is the most common cause of a save that will not load and a main menu full of red. What actually happens: a mod replaces whole files. When Paradox changes one of those files in a patch, the mod is still handing the game its older copy, which now refers to things that moved or no longer exist. The mod is not corrupt. It is out of date, which looks identical from the outside. The supported_version line in a mod's descriptor is the author saying which game version they last checked it against. The launcher shows a warning when that does not match your game. Take the warning seriously but not literally — plenty of mods keep working across a patch that changed nothing they touch, and an author who has not updated the line yet is common. It is a hint, not a verdict. If a patch just landed and everything is on fire, the honest answer is usually to wait a few days. Big mods get fixed. Starting a fresh campaign on a broken setup is how you lose thirty hours of it later.

docs.s: Halve it, do not hunt it
docs.x: Finding the culprit With forty mods enabled and a crash on load, the instinct is to guess which one it is. Do not guess. Halving finds it in about five or six launches no matter how many mods you have, and guessing can take all evening. Turn off the bottom half of your playset. Launch. If it works, the problem is in the half you turned off; if it still breaks, it is in the half you kept. Either way you have just eliminated half your list. Take the half that contains the problem, cut that in half, and go again. Forty mods becomes twenty, ten, five, three, two, one. Two things make this go wrong. docs.s: Four things that save the evening
docs.x: Habits Keep a playset you do not touch. Make a second playset with the handful of mods you know work together and leave it alone. When something breaks, launching that one tells you in thirty seconds whether the problem is a mod or the game itself. Delete old versions properly. Unsubscribing on the Workshop usually removes the files; a hand-installed mod never does. Both the folder and its .mod file have to go, and a leftover .mod file pointing at a folder that is gone is its own flavour of confusing. Add mods one at a time when a campaign is running. Mid-save changes are not automatically dangerous, but six at once means you cannot tell which one caused the thing you noticed two hours later. Back up the save folder before a big change. It is in the same user directory, under save games . Copy it somewhere. It costs nothing and it has saved more campaigns than any of the advice above.

docs.t: CK3 mods not working? Load order, patches and error logs
docs.s: The ones that come up most
docs.x: Common questions A mod is in my folder but the launcher does not list it. Hand-installed mods need a .mod file sitting next to the folder, not the descriptor.mod inside it. The launcher only reads the outer one. The launcher says "descriptor file error". The path= line in that .mod file is wrong. Use forward slashes even on Windows, and match the folder name exactly, capital letters included. My save will not load after an update. Check whether a mod in the playset updated or was removed. A save remembers the mods it was made with, and one going missing is more likely to break it than one going out of date. Everything is in English except a few bits of nonsense text. Missing localization. Cosmetic, usually a mod overwriting a file whose keys moved in a patch. It is safe to keep playing. Do I need to start a new game after adding a mod? Depends entirely on the mod. Ones that add events, traits or decisions are usually fine mid-save. Ones that change the map, the starting setup or existing characters are usually not. The mod's own page should say, and if it does not, ask.

docs.t: Community
docs.x: Community Five servers, one host I've been building Discord communities since Discord was the new kid. Pick the room that fits. 1,700+ combined members across the five servers The Grey Company Est. Sep 2026, the newest A guild for World of Warcraft: Forever. Alliance, on the Normal ruleset, leveling and social, with every time zone welcome. The Discord is where the guild plans its runs and lives between sessions. Join the Grey Company About the guild → The Game Center Est. May 2016, the original Started in May 2016 as a Skype replacement for my friend group. I'd found Discord before most people had heard of it and made us a server with a plain controller icon. It was never meant to be a "community project"; it kept growing into one anyway. Holiday merch giveaways, game nights, years of running jokes, and eventually its own website. The icon has changed with every season, and the same people are still talking to each other. Join The Game Center Read the full story → Dlonem's Den Est. 2019, the home base The server that goes with the YouTube channel. Video drops, behind-the-scenes on the apps, and whatever I'm currently obsessed with. If you found me through a video, this is your room. Join the Den The Long Night & Azor Ahai Est. 2026, for the mod The server for the Long Night & Azor Ahai mod for A Game of Thrones. Patch notes go up here first, bug reports get answered, and load-order questions get sorted out before they ruin anyone's campaign. It's filling fast. Join the Long Night server Supernatural For the mod The official server for the Crusader Kings III Supernatural mod . Report bugs, pitch ideas, ask questions, and have a say in where the mod goes next. Player input has driven a lot of what's in it already. Join the Supernatural server Five doors Which one you actually want Five servers sounds like more than it is. They are not five versions of the same room, and joining all of them is usually the wrong move. If you play one of the mods and something is broken , go straight to that mod's server — The Long Night or Supernatural . That is where patch notes land first and where load-order problems get sorted out, usually by another player before I have even seen the message. It is the fastest help available anywhere, including email. If you found me through a video , the Den is the one. It is the server attached to the YouTube channel: uploads, what I am building, and whatever I am currently obsessed with. If you just want somewhere to hang out , The Game Center is the oldest room and the least on-topic one. It has been running since 2016 and it is mostly people who have known each other for years talking nonsense. The whole story is here if you want it. If you are playing World of Warcraft: Forever , The Grey Company is the guild: Alliance, Normal ruleset, leveling and social. The Discord is the way in, and in game you can send people to dlonem.com/grey instead of reading out an invite code. If your problem is with an app , Discord is the slowest route. Use the support page instead — app problems need details like your device and version that are easier to send by email. Before you knock How these rooms are run I have been moderating Discord servers since 2016 and I have landed on a fairly boring philosophy about it, which I think is the correct one. Bug reports are welcome and blunt ones are the most useful. "It crashes when I press the button" is worth more than a polite paragraph that avoids saying what broke. If you are annoyed at something I made, say so — I would rather hear it than have you leave quietly. Nobody has to be interesting to belong there. I wrote messages years ago for people who join a server and then never speak, because sitting in a room where everyone already knows each other is genuinely hard and that should not be the thing that stops you. Lurking indefinitely is a completely acceptable way to use all five of these. What I do not run is a hype server. There is no engagement bot, no levelling system, and nothing that pings everyone. If I have shipped something you will see it once. The Grey Company works a little differently because it is a guild: it has officers, and its event nights are posted as Discord events you can mark yourself interested in.

docs.t: The Grey Company: an Alliance guild for WoW Forever
docs.x: A World of Warcraft: Forever guild The Grey Company Alliance, Normal ruleset, NA servers. A leveling and social guild for people who plan to stick around. WoW Forever's release date is 4 November 2026, and the Discord is the way in. Join the Grey Company Discord What WoW Forever is Telling someone in game? Type dlonem.com/grey Alliance faction Normal ruleset NA North American servers Nov 4 launch day The plan What we're building A guild for leveling, grouping up and hanging out on the North American (NA) servers, with players from every time zone welcome. The end game is still open; we'll pick it together once we see what Forever becomes. Some of us ran together on The Burning Crusade Anniversary. We left those names there. Forever is where we're staying. The Discord is where the guild lives between sessions: who's playing what, who needs a group, and what we're running next. House rules Everything within reason That's our unofficial motto, and it covers most of the rules. Everyone's welcome. Who you are is your business, and nobody here gives anyone grief for it. Politics and sexuality stay out of guild chat. That's not a judgment of anyone. Neither has anything to do with WoW, and they're the fastest way to split a guild. You get one friendly warning. After that, you'll need to find another guild. A little chaos is fine. Drama isn't. We're building for the people who stay. The name Why the Grey Company It's Tolkien's. In The Lord of the Rings, the Grey Company are the Rangers of the North who ride south to join Aragorn and follow him through the Paths of the Dead. The Star Wars fans in the Discord heard Grey Jedi instead. Both work. Grey with an e. Spell it gray and dlonem.com/gray still finds us. Inside What's in the Discord Guild intentions and rules, so you know what you're joining. Class, race and role tags: tank, healer or damage. Looking for group, professions, and a PvP call to arms. Mechanics worth knowing and addons worth installing. Guild stats, and a channel for the iconic moments. Event nights, posted as Discord events with reminders. No beta, upgrade or Classic experience needed. Join, grab your roles, and say hello. Before you join Quick answers Is it a raiding guild? Not to start. We're leveling and social. Once people hit 60 and the new raids open, we'll decide together how far to take it. Which region and time zone? NA, the North American servers. I'm on US Eastern time, but if you play on NA you're welcome from any time zone. Can I join if I play Horde? The guild is Alliance. On the Normal ruleset you can make characters on both factions, so a Horde alt is fine; you just can't group with us on it. Do I need to buy anything extra? No. Forever is included with a WoW subscription or Game Time. The upgrades are optional; one only matters if you want to reserve your name early, 27 October to 3 November. What about Hardcore? We're on Normal. Hardcore is its own ruleset, which Blizzard said would open after the others. Characters can't move between rulesets, except that a Hardcore character who dies can transfer to another one. The game WoW Forever, the short version What Blizzard has announced, checked against its own posts on 8 October 2026. Blizzard can change details, and its posts linked below are the final word. New to Forever? Read the beginner's guide , pick a class with the class guide , and take your first dungeon with the Hall of Thanes guide . Launch: 4 November 2026 at 3:00 p.m. PST (6:00 p.m. Eastern). What it is: a new, permanent version of WoW alongside the modern game and Classic. It's set before Molten Core and starts on the original continents with a level cap of 60. Cost: included with a WoW subscription or Game Time. Upgrade packs are optional. Name reservation: 27 October to 3 November 2026 (PST), with any upgrade. Up to three characters, first come, first served. No realm list: you pick a ruleset instead: Normal, PvP, Roleplaying, or Hardcore (Blizzard said Hardcore would open after the others). Switching means a new character. We're on Normal. Two names: every character has a first and a second name, and the full name has to be unique in your region. Factions: Horde and Alliance still can't group together. Sources, all Blizzard: launch, cost and name reservation , rulesets and factions , character names , and what Forever is . The game's own page is worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com/forever . World of Warcraft is a trademark of Blizzard Entertainment; this is a player guild, not an official Blizzard page. Meanwhile, on YouTube WoW Forever, in short Short videos from the channel, newest first. New ones show up here on their own; the rest are on the channel . Healers Watching the Warlock Life Tap Again Tanks Watching the Hunter Pet Pull Again No Wonder It's Taking Me So Long to Level Streamers Explaining Where the Gold Came From Tank and Healer Deciding Which DPS to Kick The Tank Going to Find the Hunter Blizzard Trying to Throw In Retail for Free Undead Paladins Looking for Whoever Reported the Bubble Undead Paladins Reading the Cannibalize Patch Note Undead Paladins After Waiting Since 2004 Alliance Players Seeing Orgrimmar for the First Time POV: Questing in WoW Forever Every WoW veteran in the starting zone on November 4th Every WoW player's November plans Rallying the boys for WoW Forever (6th time's the charm) My Steam backlog watching me reinstall WoW again Who's behind it My last stop in Azeroth WoW is where my name comes from. Dlonem is what the game's random name generator gave me for a death knight in sixth grade, give or take a few letters I changed. Before that I was Noaha, a warlock who joined Icecrown Citadel raids he had no business being in. The full story is on the Legacy page. I'm not going back to the modern game, and the only thing that would pull me back to Anniversary is Wrath. Blizzard calls Forever a permanent home it plans to keep building, starting on the original continents at level 60. If it lives up to that, it's the last version of WoW I need, and The Grey Company is built to last as long as it does. I've run Discord servers since 2016, and the rooms that last are the ones where people can relax. My first website existed to solve the can't-paste-an-invite problem for The Game Center . dlonem.com/grey is the same fix, years later. Getting in One link to remember You can't paste a Discord invite into WoW chat, so inviting someone means spelling out random characters and hoping. In game, tell people dlonem.com/grey instead. It lands here, one click from the server. dlonem.com/grey/join skips this page and opens the invite. Join the Grey Company Discord Or open the invite directly: discord.gg/UcJmm4XQVZ

docs.t: Recommended games — and how to buy keys safely
docs.x: The backlog speaks Games worth your hoard 270 games owned, 57 played last year. Here's the heavy rotation, the ones worth your coin, and the honest backlog. Heads up: the store links on this page are affiliate links through my G2A creator account. If you buy through them, I earn a small commission at no extra cost to you, which is one of the ways this whole operation stays funded. I only link G2A where a proper Steam key or gift is sold. If you're new to G2A: it's a key marketplace, and buying smart there is a skill. I walked through the whole thing on camera: how to buy cheap games safely , and separately what buying and activating a Steam gift looks like . Worth ten minutes before your first order. Watch: How to buy cheap games safely on G2A · Buying and activating a Steam gift Read this first Buying keys without getting burned The cheap price is real. So are the four ways it goes wrong. None of this is complicated, but all of it is on you rather than the store. A marketplace is not a shop G2A doesn't sell keys. Third-party sellers do, and the marketplace sits in the middle taking a cut. That's the whole thing in one sentence, and every other point below follows from it: you're buying from a stranger with a rating rather than from a storefront holding stock. Check the region before you pay A key can be locked to accounts registered in a particular country. Very often the reason a key is unusually cheap is the region lock. Listings say which region they're for. A key you can't activate where you live is worth exactly nothing, and finding out afterwards is the most common way people get stung. "Key" doesn't mean Steam The same game turns up as a Steam key, a Steam gift, an EA App key, a Ubisoft Connect key or a GOG key, and they land in different launchers. Battlefront II below is the clearest example: the marketplace stock is usually EA App, so if you want it sitting in your Steam library, you want a Steam sale instead. Buy the key, not the account Some listings sell you an account with the game on it rather than a key for your own. Don't. The game lives on someone else's login forever, you can't move it to your library, and you're one password reset away from owning nothing. The only time it makes any sense is a bulk library with thousands of titles on it, and that isn't what you're here for. If the listing doesn't clearly say key , close it. The seller rating is what you are paying for Sort by rating and sales volume, not by price alone. The few dollars between the cheapest listing and a seller with thousands of clean sales is the cheapest insurance you will ever buy. If the only thing a listing has going for it is the number, close the tab. And the part most affiliate pages leave out: a resold key doesn't pay a developer the way a first-hand sale does. For a small studio (Manor Lords is one person's studio, Bellwright is a small team), buy it direct and let them have the money. Marketplaces make sense for big-publisher back catalogue, deep discounts on games that have already made their money, and picking up something you'd otherwise never have bought at all. That's the honest line, and it's how I use them myself. When to skip all of this: brand-new releases (marketplace pricing isn't better yet, and the risk is highest), anything under about ten dollars (the savings don't cover the hassle), and any game where a regular Steam sale gets you within a few dollars, since Steam's own refund window is worth more than the difference. Tier one In heavy rotation What's getting played right now: game nights, solo grinds, and the forever games. Grand strategy Crusader Kings III The game I've modded for years and played for over a quarter of my Steam time. Worth knowing: read the listing title carefully on this one. Sometimes you're buying the base game alone; sometimes it's bundled with a DLC like Roads to Power , and the price barely moves. You're already saving ten or twenty dollars, so two more minutes on the description is the best-paid reading you'll do all week. And mods close a lot of the DLC gap for free: I make two of them, Supernatural and The Long Night & Azor Ahai . ~$13 on G2A $49.99 retail Find it on G2A Empire sim Schedule I Yes, the guy who ships a THC tracker also runs a fictional empire on the side. It's called balance. Absurd, addictive, and even better in co-op. ~$5 on G2A $19.99 retail Find it on G2A Pirate survival Windrose The pirate game I've been waiting for: sail a procedural open world, build, plunder, repeat. Scratches the Black Flag itch, and it's even better with a crew. Keys run under retail $29.99 retail Find it on G2A Co-op horror The Mound: Omen of Cthulhu The big recent one. Descend into cosmic horror with friends and succumb to madness in good company. Best played with the lights off and the mics on. ~$13 on G2A $23.99 retail Find it on G2A Large-scale battles Star Wars Battlefront II Still one of the best-feeling Star Wars games ever made, and it goes on sale for pocket change. G2A only carries EA App keys for this one, so for the Steam version, catch a sale. If you want it at its best, I made a guide on installing Kyber , the mod that adds custom multiplayer servers. ~$3 in Steam sales $39.99 retail Watch it on Steam Co-op chaos Helldivers 2 What game nights are made of. Managed democracy doesn't spread itself, so grab three friends and deliver it personally. A regular in my videos. ~$20 on G2A $39.99 retail Find it on G2A Tier two Worth your coin Not always in the rotation, but every one of these earned its spot in the hoard. Strategy trilogy Total War: Warhammer I–III Never pay full price for the trilogy. Each entry routinely drops under $15, so all three together can cost less than one at retail. The definitive fantasy strategy sandbox. Worth knowing: owning I and II folds their races and maps into Warhammer III ’s Immortal Empires campaign. So the trilogy isn’t three games you play in turn so much as one very large game you unlock in pieces. Buy III last. ~$9 each on key sites $59.99 retail Find it on G2A RPG Baldur's Gate 3 The RPG of a generation, with a hundred-plus hours of choices that matter. If it's not in your library yet, fix that. Worth knowing: mod support is built into the game itself rather than bolted on, so you do not need a third-party manager to start tinkering. It also almost never discounts hard, so this is one where a marketplace key beats waiting. Routinely under retail $59.99 retail Find it on G2A Medieval liberation Bellwright Build villages, train a people's army, and liberate the realm one town at a time. A survival-strategy hybrid I kept coming back to well past bedtime. ~$7 on G2A $29.99 retail Find it on G2A Co-op bullet heaven The Spell Brigade Survivors-style wizard chaos built for playing with friends. Got mine for about ten bucks. It's usually only a couple dollars off retail, but retail is cheap anyway. ~$10 on G2A $12.99 retail Find it on G2A City builder Manor Lords Grabbed it at a good discount, sank a stretch into laying out the perfect medieval village, and haven't been back since. I will be; city builders always get me back. ~$20 on G2A $39.99 retail Find it on G2A Tier three The honest backlog 270 owned, 57 played. The math demands a confession section. Cozy · unopened Disney Dreamlight Valley Grabbed it on G2A at a serious discount off retail and it's been sitting in the hoard ever since. One rainy weekend, I'll get to it. ~$22 on G2A $39.99 retail Find it on G2A Common questions Before you spend anything Is buying game keys from a marketplace safe? It can be, but a marketplace is not a store. G2A doesn't sell keys itself. Third-party sellers do, and the marketplace sits in the middle. Seller reputation, region lock and key type are all things you check yourself; the platform doesn't guarantee them for you. For a brand-new release or a small indie game, buying direct from Steam or the developer is usually the better call. What is a region-locked key? A key that will only activate on an account registered in a particular country or region. Listings state the region, and very often a key is cheap precisely because it's locked somewhere you aren't. Check it before you pay. A key you can't activate is worth nothing, and this is the single most common way people lose money here. Will a cheap key always end up in my Steam library? No. The same game can be sold as a Steam key, a Steam gift, an EA App key, a Ubisoft Connect key or a GOG key, and they land in different launchers. Star Wars Battlefront II above is the clean example: the marketplace stock is usually EA App, so I point at a Steam sale for that one instead of taking the commission. Should I buy an account instead of a key? No. An account listing hands you someone else's login with the game sitting on it. It never becomes yours, it can't move to your library, and a password reset ends it. Keys only. The single exception is a bulk library of thousands of games, which is a different hobby entirely. docs.t: Legacy — how Dlonem became Dlonem
docs.x: The legacy One made-up word, earned slowly Nobody sets out to be called Dlonem. It took a random name generator, a decade as a potato, and one rebrand to get here. Watch the moon fill in. 2008 – 2010 · ROBLOX Carlman622 Every online life starts with a first username you can't explain. Mine was Carlman622, on Roblox. The account is still out there, frozen in a striped hoodie and a Roblox cap it's been wearing since January 2010. Nobody, me included, has ever worked out what the name was supposed to mean. The dream project back then was an authentic Hunger Games map. This was before Discord, and before Skype was a given, so my cousin Randy and I would fire up Roblox and call each other on our families' landlines , staying on for hours while we played. Unlimited phone plans had not reached either of our houses yet. Randy's mom eventually opened a phone bill with hours upon hours of our calls itemized on it, easily a couple hundred dollars' worth. The Hunger Games map was never finished. The bill is the real legacy. 2009 – 2011 · WRATH OF THE LICH KING Noaha the Warlock Middle school, World of Warcraft. A warlock named Noaha carried me through the Lich King era, including a proud stretch of joining Icecrown Citadel raids I had no business being in. I'd get kicked for having no idea what I was doing, queue back up, and try again. I never made it past the second boss. Damn, I would try. ~2010 · THE GENERATOR A death knight needs a name Sixth grade, going on seventh. It was time to roll a death knight, and I couldn't think of a name, so I hit WoW's random name generator over and over, never quite liking any of it. Then I took one result, removed a couple letters, swapped another, and landed on a word that didn't exist anywhere: Dlonem . I named the character and moved on. It would be sixteen years before the word had a real job. 2011 – 2017 · STEAM The Mr.Potato years On Steam I became Mr.Potato, and to basically everyone who knew me, just Potato . (One guy insisted on "Tater." There's always one.) Old friends from that era still call me Potato today, so I would say it stuck. Right up to the rebrand, my profile picture wasn't even a potato. For a while it was a turtle in a baseball cap. I didn't have my own thing going yet, and getting one is what everything after this is about. the pre-brand aesthetic, preserved MAY 2016 · DISCORD The Game Center Back then the friend group lived on Skype, because it was simpler than Steam voice: always on, and you could call anybody. Then I stumbled onto Discord before most people had heard of it, and moved us over. It started as a group server with a plain little game controller for an icon. There was no "TGC" and no grand plan, just "wouldn't it be cool to meet more people to game with?" It blew up into something bigger anyway: holiday merch giveaways, game nights every couple months, seasonal icons for every holiday, and me playing the designated adult in a server full of teenagers. ("You probably shouldn't be saying that" was the moderation policy.) It even got its own website. Ten years later the server still exists, and so do all forty-something versions of that controller icon. TGC, est. may 2016 LATE 2019 · THE REBRAND The word comes back A potato is hard to build a brand on. Looking for a name that was mine , I remembered the death knight. Dlonem was unique, unclaimed everywhere, and already had history. The YouTube channel launched under it in 2019, and the letter D started showing up in profile pictures, first in a ghostly Danny Phantom style, later sharpened into the crescent-and-scythe mark it is now. the danny phantom era, july 2019 JULY 1, 2026 · NOW Dlonem LLC Today the word covers a YouTube channel, five Discord communities, two Crusader Kings III mods with thousands of subscribers, and a small studio shipping privacy-friendly mobile apps, officially incorporated as Dlonem LLC on July 1, 2026. Sixteen years from name generator to legal entity. Full moon. Still building. docs.t: CK3 Mods — Crusader Kings III mods by Dlonem
docs.x: Crusader Kings III Two mods, one obsession I've been modding CK3 for years. One mod adds the monsters to the base game; the other finishes the story the show fumbled. Both are free on the Steam Workshop, and both have their own Discord where players shape what gets built next. 25,900+ subscribers across both mods 81,100+ unique Workshop visitors 2,600+ favorites 2022 first mod published Pick your apocalypse The mods A Game of Thrones submod The Long Night & Azor Ahai NEW The Long Night as a full endgame. The dead get back up wearing their own faces and ruling their own realms. The Wall comes down on camera. You can lay down your lands and serve on the Wall for real, holding a castle or riding out with a ranging company. The Night King is fought on foot, in the snow, and only a bane destroys him. Azor Ahai is a working prophecy that the world resolves on its own, rather than a trait you tick at the start. 14,200+ subscribers 27,400+ visitors 700+ favorites Read the full breakdown Watch the showcase Wiki Steam Workshop Discord Non-Steam download Base-game overhaul Supernatural Vampires, werewolves, hybrids, witches, demons and hunters in the base game. Six lifestyles with ten perk trees, supernatural regiments, artifacts, twenty-two game rules, and since 2.35 a hunt where every monster is a real character who left a trail. You can play the hunter, or rule as something far older. 11,600+ subscribers 53,700+ visitors 1,900+ favorites Read the full breakdown Wiki Steam Workshop Non-Steam download Discord Running both at once The compatibility patch This is for running vampires and the army of the dead in the same campaign. Both mods rewrite some of the same files, and whichever loads second erases the other's version without warning. The patch fixes that. AGOT: Supernatural & The Long Night Compatibility Patch needs all three mods It does nothing on its own, and it has to load last. Twenty-two entries that both mods define. Each one is a three-way merge against the base game's own version, so neither mod's changes are guessed at. Marriage acceptance. AGOT's full 1,000-line house and legitimacy logic, plus Supernatural's fertility exemptions. Without the patch one of the two is gone; this entry alone was behind multiplayer desyncs in testing. Births. AGOT's entire birth pipeline (house looks, Valyrian genetics, dragon dreams) and Supernatural's, in one file. Both ship it at the same path, so the later one was deleting the other wholesale. The Originals. Supernatural's founding vampire family is written for the vanilla map, with a Norse culture and faith that don't exist in Westeros. Under the patch they become First Men of the North: northman culture, Old Gods faith. Plus disinheritance, the witch ritual, secrets, schemes, abductions, artifact demands, traits, imprisonment and resurrection rules. Latest patch update · from the Steam change notes 1.1.3a — Re-checked against today's A Game of Thrones update 4 September 2026 A hotfix for the A Game of Thrones 0.5.2 hotfix (4 September). Every file this patch merges from AGOT and Supernatural was regenerated against the new build and compared with what shipped; the child-birth, disinherit and marriage merges came out identical, so nothing there changes. Every change note on Steam → 1,579 running it right now 22 merged entries v1.0 current release Load order: drag the patch to the very bottom A Game of Thrones AGOT submods (AGOT+, Valyrian Steel, Submod Core, Nobility…) AGOT: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Supernatural The Compatibility Patch (this one, last) Every fix works by defining the entry the two mods fight over. Anything loaded after it wins instead, and the patch does nothing at all. View on Steam Workshop New to this If you have never installed a CK3 mod On Steam it is genuinely one click. Open the Workshop page, hit Subscribe, and the next time you open the Paradox launcher the mod is in your list waiting to be added to a playset. Nothing to unzip and nothing to configure. Off Steam — GOG, Epic, Game Pass — it is about five minutes of copying a folder and writing one small text file by hand. Both of my mods have a page that walks the whole thing: The Long Night and Supernatural . The part that trips up almost everyone is not installing a mod. It is the load order. CK3 resolves conflicts by letting the mod lower in your playset overwrite the one above it, which means a mod that appears to do nothing is usually being overwritten rather than being broken, and sorting two incompatible mods rather than disabling one of them leaves you running a mixture of both. I wrote up the whole thing — load order, what a game patch does to a mod, finding the one bad mod out of forty, and how to read the error log — on a separate page: when CK3 mods break . It applies to any mod, not just mine. Running both Why there is a third thing in the list The compatibility patch confuses people until the load-order rule explains it, and then it is obvious. Supernatural and The Long Night both change some of the same underlying files. Loaded together without anything else, whichever one sits lower wins those files outright and the other one quietly loses whatever it had put there. Neither mod is at fault; that is just what overwriting means. The patch is a small third mod that contains the merged version of exactly those files — the pieces of both, reconciled. It has to load last , because its entire job is to be the final overwrite. Put it anywhere else and something else overwrites the merge, which puts you back where you started. You only need it if you are running both mods in the same campaign. One mod on its own does not need a patch for anything.
