docs.x: The activity header the mod ships for Magical Research. Magical Research is how a mage gets stronger on purpose. You pick a project, work at it for five months, and if you collect enough breakthroughs you are rewarded with what the project promised: a new spell, a permanent power, a regiment, an artifact, or years of life. It is open to a true mage who holds at least a county and is an adult. A Mage on the Gnostic Council's Keeper of the Reliquary seat can run it every five years instead of ten, and a reminder appears in your alerts when it is ready. Magical Research. At home, where you stand. No travel. Research Expedition. A journey to a place of power you know about. There are two kinds. Magical Research happens where you are standing. A Research Expedition travels to one of the world's three places of power, and plays out as a story at that place instead of a project; see Research Expeditions . The budget and the three specialist intents are for the first kind only. Research Budget Extra cost Starting progress Needs Economy Variant None None — Increased Funding 100 gold +5 — Exhaustive Funding 200 gold +10 Ambitious, or any learning education Your intent decides which projects you are offered, which events can find you, and what kind of experience the good outcomes pay: Intent Projects about Experience it pays General Research Spells, the mind, other worlds, necromancy, nature, the Ultimate Spell Secret Knowledge Life Extension Longevity, the body, the soul Alchemy and Demonology Combat Magic War spells and curses Combat Magic Creation and Artifacts Golems, transmutation, rings, the Ancient Singularity, fortifications Alchemy, or Secret Knowledge once Alchemy is full An expedition can only be General Research. You can take one guest, but nothing in the activity rewards the guest except an evening with the books. How a research runs # Extra Support. On arrival you choose an assistant, or work alone for a little prestige. The candidates are witches you trust: a friend or soulmate, your heir, a witch you hold a hook on, a mage courtier, another player. The assistant does not travel or attend; they simply help. They learn that you are a witch, take Assisted in Magical Research for twenty years (+1 learning, +10% magic experience), think better of you, and gain Secret Knowledge if they are a mage below 100, or a permanent +1 learning if not. How much they add to your work depends on how good they are: +5 from a mage past 75 Secret Knowledge, +3 past 25, +2 from any other mage, +1 from a True Witch, a demon or an Erudite, nothing from anyone else. Research Focus. Two days later you pick the project. You may change your mind once, which costs eleven days. Five months of work. Each month one event from the research pool finds you, plus one more scheduled at the start. On top of that, any night there is a chance that someone spends it on the books: a little stress, and +1 progress. The verdict. At five months the game counts your progress against what the project needed. Calibration. Four projects play out a follow-up story here: Time Travel, Design Combat Spell, Artificial Human and Magic Ring. If you finished far ahead, Excess Breakthroughs comes next. Projects and breakthroughs # Every project needs one to four breakthroughs , and a breakthrough is 25 progress, so a four-breakthrough project needs 100. You are offered up to three projects drawn at random from your intent's pool, plus that intent's basic project, which is always there. The third random project is only offered if you have the Erudite perk from the base game's learning tree. A basic project can be repeated; an advanced one can be completed once per character; a unique one once in the whole world. All 28 projects, what they need and what they give Project Kind Breakthro

docs.x: The activity header the mod ships for the Mage Summit. A Mage Summit gathers the world's magic users for a banquet and then a Council of Mages , where a Speaker puts a motion to a vote. With the Order of the Blue Rose off, it is the only way to found the Gnostic Council , and the way its Grand Magus is elected once it exists. With the Order on, which is the default, it does neither: the Order fills the chair. To host you need the Mage trait, a title above baron, a landed or landless administrative government, and one of three things: a full Secret Knowledge track, a prestige level of 4 or more, or a house with the Magic Traditions modifier, which comes from completing a mythical magic legend. It costs 1,000 gold , halved for each of: Magic Traditions, the 50% discount from the Recognition event, and the Knowledge Sharing Arcana legacy. At its cheapest a player pays 125. Then food: the poor option is free, the default Normal food adds the scaled feast price plus 100 gold, and Good food more again. The cheapest summit, on poor food, is 125 gold. The Extraordinary security option adds 300 gold and nothing in the mod reads it. The cooldown is ten years. The summit is held at your capital, your domicile, a place of power, or a Mage's Laboratory or Spire. Up to 30 guests: by default every Mage, Yaga, arcane-focus character or Magical Experiments holder in the world, and every True Witch, wherever they are and without any range limit; you can add court mages and learned witches in range. Anyone excluded from the community as an Outcast is left off. A mage who was missed can invite himself with Join the Mage Summit on anyone already going, once a year, and not through the same person twice inside nine years. There are three intents: Sharing knowledge (the default), Diplomatic affairs (for rulers) and Show superiority (for mages, demons and Yaga). They decide which events find you and which motions you can bring. A member of the Order also has Seek Kindred Minds , which pays standing when another member he knows is there, and a Medicum or higher Speak for My Circle . The banquet and the Council of Mages # The Banquet lasts four weeks, with a weekly event for every attendee: knowledge, perk points and sorcery lessons for the sharers, hooks and supporters for the diplomats, demonstrations and duels for the show-offs, and potions and scrolls for sale. If you have the guards check invitations at the opening, one time in three they catch a witch hunter at the door, which costs the host 100 prestige on the spot. Then the Council of Mages . Every Mage and True Witch scores for the Speaker's chair (legendary, a Mage, learning 20+, prestige level 3+, the host, a Gnostic Council member, owning a magic artifact or the Source), bids for it on a diplomacy duel, and the highest score speaks. The Speaker brings one motion; Mages, True Witches and arcane-focus characters vote, and a hook on a voter buys his vote. It passes on a simple majority. Motion Speaker needs If it passes A joint program of magical research Sharing knowledge Everyone: Research Cooperation for 10 years (+3 learning, +10% lifestyle experience) and Secret Knowledge A mutual defence pact Diplomatic affairs Every landed attendee but the Speaker joins a pact: when an outsider attacks one, the rest are asked to join the war, pay 100 gold, or leave the pact at the cost of a prestige level "We need a Grand Magus - I nominate myself" Show superiority, a Mage, and no Gnostic Council yet. Not offered with the Order on The Speaker becomes Grand Magus and the Gnostic Council is founded The Gnostic Council needs funds A council member Every attendee pays a fifth of their gold into the council's funds Ban black magic — Curses, powerful curses and domination are forbidden to every attendee Ordinary

docs.x: The activity header the mod ships for the Search for Magical Artifacts. The True Witch's activity. Six months at your capital spent finding out where the world's magical artifacts are, and making a case for one of them. It is held at your capital, costs the game's activity price plus 100 gold, and runs every twelve years. You must hold fewer than eight magical artifacts. Increased Funding costs another 300 gold for a faster start. At the start the game draws up to three magical artifacts you do not own, from anywhere in the world. A few weeks in, Large-scale Search asks how you look: your spies, your books, your contacts or your coven. A little later, Target Selection asks which of the three trails to follow; the first is the easiest. Every month an event moves your progress up or down: paying an informant, putting your spymaster on it, giving up your familiar, a stranger who knows too much, a rival's interference. Progress at the end Result Under 50 Fruitless Search. Stress. 50 to 74 Successful Search. You learn who owns your chosen artifact, and you remember it. 75 to 99 Very Successful Search. As above, and a personal claim on it, but only if a hidden 40% roll during the Large-scale Search went your way. 100 or more Flawless Search. A personal claim on it, every time. The Search never hands you the artifact. The best it gives is a claim ; taking the thing is up to you. Since 2.38 it can hand you a lesser relic : each month on site there is a 10% chance of A Lesser Thing , once a search. Relics do not count toward the eight. The artifacts it can find are the Ancient Singularity (either mark), the Ring of Everlasting, the Black Grimoire, the Darkblade, the Crown of Shadows, the Orb of Truth, the Magic Catalyst, the Dragonscales, Hell's Scepter and the Enchanted Ring.

docs.x: The coven's gathering, and the one activity that the base game also has: Supernatural's version replaces it. Three weeks, up to 30 guests, a ceremony on the seventh day. You host it as a witch whose house is a coven, or as a landless adventurer whose camp has the Portable Chapel (see Secret Seekers ). It costs a small sum of gold, takes three months to gather, and runs every five years, or every two and a half if you hold a Temple of the Horned God. It has the strictest guest rule in the mod: you and each guest must know the other is a witch , and the guest must be within your diplomatic range. And once the ceremony is over, every attendee learns every other attendee's witch secret . A Grand Rite is a room full of people who can now ruin each other. Intent Who What it does Worship the witch god Everyone, the default The base game's rite rewards; a heresiarch also draws one of eight dark gifts Seek True Power Players One of nine outcomes: ancient texts, an amulet, power, a debate that pays a perk point, a rumour of someone's magic artifact, a demon's offer, a sacrifice Nominate Yourself as Grand Master The host, if their house is a coven Gather support for the Grand Master election Shape the Coven's Policy The host, as Grand Master, with the Coven Authority tradition Choose the coven's focus Bring the Coven to the Order The host, if he is a Magistratus of the Order and a member of the coven Every Mage of the coven who could join is sent the Order's note The ceremony asks how you lead it: read from an old scroll, use some tricks, or improvise, each a skill duel; pay an offering for a sure result; or, as a True Witch, tell them about true magic, which always goes well. A good ceremony earns the respect of every participant; a poor one their disappointment. Choosing a Grand Master # Eleven days after the ceremony, if anyone stood, the coven chooses. The score is title rank, plus a point each for being a True Witch or Mage, a heresiarch, the house head, owning a magic artifact and having power to spend, plus three for each round of support gathered at the rite. If the house has no Grand Master the best score wins. If the sitting Grand Master stayed away, he is deposed in his absence . If he came, the winner may challenge him, and he chooses: fight in single combat, which can be fatal , step down for 200 prestige, or, as a player against an AI challenger, refuse at the cost of a prestige level and everyone's regard. The new Grand Master learns the witch secret of every member of the house, and every witch in the house learns his. The five coven policies Policy The coven gets Spreading Witchcraft +1 personal scheme, +10% Convert to Witchcraft, but hostile schemes against you +5% Accumulating Wealth +2 stewardship, +20% tax, −5 general opinion Expanding influence +20% merit, +20% influence, +10 maximum political scheme success, −5% tax Security Prioritization Hostile schemes against you −5 and −5 maximum, +10 travel safety, −5% prestige Seeking of Knowledge +2 learning, +10% lifestyle experience, +5% stress gain Changing a policy you have already set costs 500 prestige. Keeping the current one earns Authority. Two things at a Grand Rite can cost you your life or your soul A demon may appear and offer Gift From Hell (+3 intrigue, +1 stewardship, health) for your soul, which it comes to collect eighteen to twenty years later: die, bargain, or fight a greater demon to the death. You can sell another attendee's soul instead. And a Sacrifice kills one attendee for a great deal of power; the coven may find out who did it.

docs.x: A coven is three things at once: a house modifier , a Grand Master at its head, and a culture tradition that gives the coven authority in the realm. The house modifier alone is worth health, fertility and magic experience to every member; the tradition unlocks a cultists regiment, free disinheritance of non-witches, extra benefits on the witch traits, and the Grand Master's own policy intent at the Rite. You found one with the base game's decision, Found Witch Coven, which Supernatural replaces with an easier one in 2.38: you must be a witch and your house's head, and you need two other adult witches of your house whom you know to be witches , whatever the house's size. The base game wanted four, or three in five adults of a larger house. The AI founds covens too since 2.38, rarely: mostly an ambitious witch, one past fifty, or the head of a house with four or more known witches, never a content one, checked every five years, and never while the world already holds one coven for every 150 counties. The world also makes covens of its own: the Baba Yaga family is one, and a second appears the first time somebody creates the Crown of Shadows. Otherwise you join one by birth or marriage, and rise to lead it at a Grand Rite . The coven's panel. Every coven shows in the Situations window as Coven , owned by its Grand Master, or by the house head if it has none. It lists the members (every adult of the house the owner knows to be a witch), the coven's reliquary and the decisions below, and is redone each year. Other player members see a copy, and a button on the left of the screen, Your Coven , opens the Situations window. Items pledged to the coven give every member The Coven's Reliquary , up to +15% magic lifestyle experience. Leave the Coven : you are no longer counted among its witches, and what you pledged comes back to you. Disband the Coven : the owner ends it. The house is no longer a coven, and every pledge goes back to its owner. A coven also ends when its house loses a War Against the Witch , and its panel ends when fewer than two adult witches are left in the house. Covens and the Order. A witch can belong to a coven and to the Order of the Blue Rose at once. A Grand Rite host who is a Magistratus of the Order can choose Bring the Coven to the Order , and every Mage of the coven who could join is sent a note and a rose. A coven may also ask one of its own what he is ( The Sisters Ask What You Are ): tell them about the Order and lose some standing, or lie and hope they believe you. Until 2.35 there was no way for an outsider to find out that a house was a coven: nothing let anyone outside the house detect it. Supernatural's contribution is the sweep: when a witch hunt's trail ends at a coven house, a seasoned hunter (Witch-Hunting 60, or an established name as a hunter) can go through the house , up to five rounds in one night, each round another member of that house who is standing in that county. From the second round on he takes a wound before the door even opens, and losing a round ends the sweep the honest way, with him on the floor and four of them still upstairs. If he stops while the culprit is still free, the county records a withdrawal and it costs him 25 prestige. When the culprit belongs to the Order, he can sweep her temple the same way. The sweep is one night in one house, not a campaign against a dynasty scattered across three kingdoms. House members who are not in the hunted county are never drawn into it.

docs.x: A Grand Magus and three seats, sitting over the world's magic. Until 2.38 it was Witchcraft's Gnostic Council with an Grand Magus in the chair; 2.38 gave it and its seats the Order's names, and with Supernatural: The Blue Rose on (the default) it belongs to the Order of the Blue Rose . Seat Gives Grand Magus +3 diplomacy, +50% prestige, double diplomatic range. Appoints the other three, and can Call a secret Gnostic Council meeting every four years once all three seats are filled. Keeper of the Reliquary +3 learning, +10% lifestyle experience, and Magical Research every five years instead of ten. Adeptus Major +3 intrigue, +10% scheme discovery, can force a mage duel without losing face, and every Combat Magic project needs one breakthrough fewer. Chancellor +3 stewardship, +1 influence a month, and Manage of Council Funds every two years. With the Order on. Only members of the Order sit on the council. Invite to Gnostic Council , Request Gnostic Council appointment and Witchcraft's yearly offer of a seat all refuse anyone else, and leaving the Order, by any road, loses the seat. The chair is filled by the Order: while fewer than three temples stand, the Temple Magus of the oldest temple takes it; with three or more, a Conclave elects the Grand Magus from the Temple Magi, and fills the seats. Taking the chair forms the council if it never existed. A Mage Summit no longer founds the council or elects its chair. Once the Order owns the council, only members see its window, unless the council has revealed itself to the world. On a save from before 2.38, a Grand Magus who is not a member is dealt with once. A player is asked in The Masks Bow to You to join a temple or give up the chair; an AI who can join is made a Magistratus of a temple, and one who cannot is removed from the chair. A player Grand Magus who is a member can Dissolve the Gnostic Council once every ten years: every seat falls empty, and each holder sent home thinks 15 less of him for ten years. With the Order off, it is Witchcraft's council under the new names. It does not exist when the game starts, it is founded at a Mage Summit when a Mage Speaker with the Show superiority intent nominates himself and the vote passes, and whenever the chair is empty the next summit is an election. The Grand Magus also fills seats with Invite to Gnostic Council (a Mage or Yaga; the invitee gains a lot of prestige), and a mage can ask with Request Gnostic Council appointment . He removes a member with Recall from the Gnostic Council , which needs 5,000 prestige, a hook, or an incapable member. Any member can Quit . A seat also qualifies you for the estate's Gnostic Council Archives and its top two tower levels. The council keeps a treasury. Witches can Make a donation to the Gnostic Council every ten years (50 gold, plus 50 for a count, 100 for a duke, 200 for a king, 250 for an emperor), which makes a non-member a permanent Gnostic Council Supporter (+1 diplomacy). A supporter can Ask for the Gnostic Council's support once the treasury holds 200 gold: three years of protection against plots, research money and +20% magic experience, three years' access to a place of power, a court mage, or help in a war. The Grand Magus decides. With the Order on, members' dues go into the same treasury.

docs.s: Places of power and magic buildings
docs.x: Academy of Magic Temple of the Horned God Hut On The Chicken's Leg Houska Castle Three special buildings are the world's places of power : the Academy of Magic, the Temple of the Horned God and the Hut On The Chicken's Leg. None of them can be built from nothing. Each appears once, through an event, in some ruler's capital; you get one by holding that county. Holding one while landed opens the Arcane focus to a witch, adds 5 to every standard power gain, strengthens the Ultimate Spell, and makes it a summit venue and an expedition destination. Building How you get it What holding it does Academy of Magic Appears with the Ancient Singularity event +3 learning per prestige level, +50% magic experience, the Learn new spell decision, +3 research starting progress Temple of the Horned God Appears in a random AI ruler's capital +2 intrigue per prestige level, +10 life expectancy, +25% Demonic experience, a fort and garrison, the Summon Demonic Army decision, and the Grand Rite every two and a half years Hut On The Chicken's Leg Baba Yaga's family brings it +10% magic experience, +10% county control, plots against you slower and weaker, Claim the Yaga title , and a Yaga can raise the hut itself as a regiment Houska Castle The Crown of Shadows event opens a slot for it in Litoměřice's capital; whoever holds that county can build it for 400 gold +1 learning per prestige level, +25% magic experience, +2 on every Demonology gain. Not a place of power Mage's Study , then Laboratory , then Spire Built in a holding: 300, 600, then 900 gold and 1,000 prestige. Needs the Counter-spells perk or the Mage perk, or the Open-Minded Lords legacy for the upper two; the Laboratory does not accept the Mage perk alone, and the Spire needs the Mage Rulership tradition. One tower each Magic experience +10% / +30% / +40%, wider diplomatic range, county control, development and income, and +3 / +4 / +5 research starting progress. The Study and Laboratory count as a tower for Magic Triangulation; as the files stand, the Spire does not The estate mage tower, level 4. An estate has its own mage tower , four levels at 100 to 400 gold and the same in prestige. An arcane-focus character can build the first level; the rest need a true mage. Every level displays as "Mage's Laboratory". Levels 3 and 4 need you to be independent, under Mage Rulership, or on the Gnostic Council. It is worth +2 to +5 research starting progress and some magic experience, and it holds internal buildings of its own: a Triangulation Device (this is how a mage without a holding tower gets Magic Triangulation, and its second level makes it free), a Rune-Ward Cache and Spellbound Vault against artifact theft, an Affiliates Network , the Gnostic Council Archives for members, and Accursed Tomes if you own the Black Grimoire or a magical elaboration. A landless adventurer gets the craft through a camp purpose, Secret Seekers. It costs 1,000 prestige to adopt, needs a witch, gives +10% magic experience, and is the route to all but one of the magic task contracts. Besides the base game's Scribes, Juicy Rumors and Subdued Gear upgrades, it unlocks two camp buildings: the Fortune Teller's Tent (gold, travel safety, free scrying) and the Cult Caravan , six levels of dread and conversion, which in turn opens the Portable Chapel (the camp can host the Grand Rite, and a better cult priest), Combat Equipment (the cultists regiment), Dark Missionaries (camp conversions and Spread the Cult) and the Cult Archives (+3 learning, +3 research starting progress). Leave the Seekers and the witch buildings are torn down.

docs.x: Witchcraft's dynasty legacy, "Gathering lost knowledge and searching for true power." Five perks, priced like any other legacy: Perk What it does 1. Open-Minded Lords Needs a witch. Your dynasty makes better court mages, imprisoning someone can win you their magical artifact, and you can build the Mage's Laboratory and Spire without the Counter-spells perk. 2. Magic Theorists +5 starting progress on Magical Research, and the Esoteric Training decision. 3. Knowledge Sharing Every expedition destination is open to the whole dynasty, +10% magic experience, and the Mage Summit at half price. 4. docs.x: Magic Domination is a strong hook that never expires. The Domination spell sets it, along with a master and minion relation, ends the victim's plots against you, and can turn their culture and faith to yours. It is what Command your minion uses. An AI mage at war will dominate a neighbouring ruler of his own rank and drag him in, up to four minions. Dark Champion is a court position that opens when you hold the Crown of Shadows or a demon's Deals with Mortals perk. The candidate needs a vice and something dark: a murderer, corrupted, a cannibal, a True Witch, a demon, a Mage, a hunter, or your minion. On the Special Mission task he can be sent to assassinate, plunder, abduct or rescue. Appointing a Priest of the Cult makes him a witch The camp officer that the Cult Caravan opens is made a witch on appointment , and learns your own witch secret. Choose him knowing that. The fifteen magic task contracts (Secret Seekers camps; The Secret Library also under Scholars) Contract Who can take it Pays Inconvenient Witch Anyone Prestige and provisions; failure costs prestige Searching for Ingredients Anyone, for a herbalist or witch employer Gold and prestige Demonic Possession A player Gold and prestige Ruthless Rivalry A player Gold and prestige Task For The Healer A player Gold and prestige; failure costs nothing Magic Anomaly A true mage with room for more power, once per dynasty Prestige and an unknown reward The Secret Scroll A player, while no Ancient Scroll exists The Ancient Scroll Secret Mission A True Witch or true mage, once per dynasty 200 gold and prestige Monster Hunt A player who is not a demon Large gold, prestige and provisions Haunted Manor A player Large gold and prestige Rumors About a Magic Artifact A player without a magic artifact Where the artifact is; on a critical success, a claim on it Lifting the Curse A player Gold and prestige The Secret Library Anyone Prestige and a perk point or skills Evaluation of the Court Mage A witch, Mystic, True Witch, Mage or arcane focus Gold and prestige; on a critical success, the court mage's seat and a fief Carnivorous Plants Anyone Gold, prestige and provisions Most of these also pay provisions on success.

docs.s: The endgame: crises and the two wars
docs.x: Witchcraft has an endgame, timed by the Witchcraft: Ending crises rule. At the default, "At any time", the first crisis can come ten years in; the other settings delay it 50 to 200 years, and Never turns it off. After that, each year there is a chance that a crisis starts, if a player has become powerful enough to provoke one: The Grand Coalition : the world's leading witch hunter raises a coalition against a player Mage who rules an independent empire and has drawn too much attention. It never fires while the Witch Hunters Activity rule is on Low, which is the default . Bael : the demon comes for a player mage past 50 Secret Knowledge who holds two magical artifacts, unless the Bael rule is off. Return of the Grand Magus : Abdul Al-Hazred, author of the Black Grimoire, arrives to reclaim the title from a player who holds the Gnostic Council's Grand Magus seat, has 70 Secret Knowledge and two magical artifacts. He demands your artifacts, then sets out to destroy your dynasty: a summoned assassin, a curse on your heir, a double who sits in your council and spends your money, a bounty on your family. He can be stopped. Its rule's "Cannot appear" setting does not block achievements. There are two casus belli. Demonic Invasion belongs to a Greater Demon with a full Reputation track, costs 2,000 prestige, and on victory takes the titles and every magical artifact, relic and page; a defender who has sold his soul is executed, anyone else goes to the dungeon. Losing it, the demon pays and is imprisoned. War Against the Witch cannot be declared: it comes from the Grand Coalition, or from a witch hunter's Stop The Witch when he chooses to raise a coalition. If the coalition wins, the witch's house loses its coven, every magical artifact, relic and page is taken, the witch is burned, and the witch's adult heir and every adult house member who is not an independent ruler go to the dungeon. A third, Seize Their Relics , came with 2.38: a player can declare it at any distance, and a greedy or ambitious AI Mage against a neighbour.

docs.x: Some characters carry the Mage trait without the power: a secret, False Mage , says they are pretending. A False Mage shows the trait but fails the true-mage check that most mage content uses: no Magical Research, no Teach Sorcery, no research spells, no mage contracts. A few things look only at the trait, among them Mage Duel and a Gnostic Council appointment. A player can choose to become one when an event offers it; one True Witch in ten is offered it six months to three years after the capstone; and two in ten court mages the game generates are frauds. Exposure strips the Mage trait, costs a prestige level and five years of Liar Liar , and a liege who employed them as court mage holds it against them for ten years. Taking the Magical Experiments perk ends the pretence the other way: the secret lapses, and the perk takes the Mage trait away with it.

docs.x: Extra Support. On arrival you choose an assistant, or work alone for a little prestige. The candidates are witches you trust: a friend or soulmate, your heir, a witch you hold a hook on, a mage courtier, another player. The assistant does not travel or attend; they simply help. They learn that you are a witch, take Assisted in Magical Research for twenty years (+1 learning, +10% magic experience), think better of you, and gain Secret Knowledge if they are a mage below 100, or a permanent +1 learning if not. How much they add to your work depends on how good they are: +5 from a mage past 75 Secret Knowledge, +3 past 25, +2 from any other mage, +1 from a True Witch, a demon or an Erudite, nothing from anyone else. Research Focus. Two days later you pick the project. You may change your mind once, which costs eleven days. Five months of work. Each month one event from the research pool finds you, plus one more scheduled at the start. On top of that, any night there is a chance that someone spends it on the books: a little stress, and +1 progress. The verdict. At five months the game counts your progress against what the project needed. Calibration. Four projects play out a follow-up story here: Time Travel, Design Combat Spell, Artificial Human and Magic Ring. If you finished far ahead, Excess Breakthroughs comes next.

docs.x: Every project needs one to four breakthroughs , and a breakthrough is 25 progress, so a four-breakthrough project needs 100. You are offered up to three projects drawn at random from your intent's pool, plus that intent's basic project, which is always there. The third random project is only offered if you have the Erudite perk from the base game's learning tree. A basic project can be repeated; an advanced one can be completed once per character; a unique one once in the whole world. docs.x: Success gives the project's reward and Secret Knowledge by difficulty: +2 for a one-breakthrough project, +3 for two, +5 for three, +10 for four. Failure costs nothing but the time: you get Learning from Mistakes for sixteen years (+1 learning, and +5 starting progress on your next research) and +1 Secret Knowledge. There is no wound, no death and no lost gold for failing. Beat the target by more than one whole breakthrough, and Excess Breakthroughs asks what to do with the surplus: Use it : more track experience, more again if you are a Legendary Mage. Record it in the chronicles : unlocks Write a Magical Elaborate , a decision that costs gold and runs every five years. Spread the word : a great deal of prestige, and a one-in-two chance that witch hunters take an interest in you for ten years. What can go wrong Research is safe unless you choose risk. The one way it can kill you is Risky Experiment 's plain option, 2 in 100. Your witch secret gets out if you take Total Commitment 's quickest option, or answer the Arcane Research nickname event as the Enchanter. A tortured prisoner and your assistant both learn it, and spreading word of your breakthroughs draws hunters.

docs.t: Supernatural CK3 Mod Wiki: Vampires, Werewolves and the Hunt
docs.x: An expedition travels to a place of power : the Academy of Magic, the Temple of the Horned God or the Hut On The Chicken's Leg. You can only plan one to a place you know about: one you hold, one inside your own independent realm, one an event has told you of (Magic Triangulation, Rumors About Magic, a search's Places of power event, the Grand Magus's answer), or all three if your dynasty has the Knowledge Sharing legacy. Each is meant to be visited once in a lifetime. There is no project and no verdict: the place itself is the story, and it pays out as you go. The Academy of Magic The Temple of the Horned God The Hut On The Chicken's Leg The Academy of Magic is the safe one. A guide shows you round; the grand library and the deeper halls pay skills and track experience, sometimes Liquid Aether, and one of the rooms you may find is worth +5 learning outright. You leave with Visited the Academy of Magic for good: +2 learning, +5 starting progress on every research after. The Temple of the Horned God is three trials, and the last can kill you. Fail the first and you limp home wounded, with +1 learning to show for it. Pass all three and the rewards are the biggest an expedition gives: track experience across the board, Source potential, and claws or physical and mental gifts. The Horned God's own favour goes only to a Yaga who asks for more, or to a Shrewd answer at the chalice. The Hut On The Chicken's Leg is Baba Yaga's. If she lives and the hut is not yours, you may be taken in by Sefia and learn from her (once per dynasty), and Baba Yaga will think much less of you when she hears. If no Yaga lives and you hold the hut's county, you can win a learning duel to break in and become the new Yaga . Either way you leave with Visited the Hut On The Chicken's Leg (+1 intrigue, +5 life expectancy). Spoilers: the Temple's trials The first trial is a riddle. The answer is "Fire? You are fire." Any other answer wounds you, and the expedition ends. The second is a demon guardian. Fighting it always wins, and a true mage can open with Power Strike for Combat Magic experience. Running away ends the expedition. The third is a chalice and two basins, green and red. Drinking either one alone kills you, every time. Drink both and the Horned God speaks to you; kneel or refuse him, and either way you are rewarded. A Shrewd character has a third answer: fill the chalice with water from his own waterskin. It earns the Horned God's favour. Walking away is always allowed. Once anyone has won the Horned God's favour, later visitors find the temple open and get a shorter, gentler visit.

docs.s: The banquet and the Council of Mages
docs.x: The Banquet lasts four weeks, with a weekly event for every attendee: knowledge, perk points and sorcery lessons for the sharers, hooks and supporters for the diplomats, demonstrations and duels for the show-offs, and potions and scrolls for sale. If you have the guards check invitations at the opening, one time in three they catch a witch hunter at the door, which costs the host 100 prestige on the spot. Then the Council of Mages . Every Mage and True Witch scores for the Speaker's chair (legendary, a Mage, learning 20+, prestige level 3+, the host, a Gnostic Council member, owning a magic artifact or the Source), bids for it on a diplomacy duel, and the highest score speaks. The Speaker brings one motion; Mages, True Witches and arcane-focus characters vote, and a hook on a voter buys his vote. It passes on a simple majority. Motion Speaker needs If it passes A joint program of magical research Sharing knowledge Everyone: Research Cooperation for 10 years (+3 learning, +10% lifestyle experience) and Secret Knowledge A mutual defence pact Diplomatic affairs Every landed attendee but the Speaker joins a pact: when an outsider attacks one, the rest are asked to join the war, pay 100 gold, or leave the pact at the cost of a prestige level "We need a Grand Magus - I nominate myself" Show superiority, a Mage, and no Gnostic Council yet. Not offered with the Order on The Speaker becomes Grand Magus and the Gnostic Council is founded The Gnostic Council needs funds A council member Every attendee pays a fifth of their gold into the council's funds Ban black magic — Curses, powerful curses and domination are forbidden to every attendee Ordinary rulers will become our puppets Schemer Everyone: Joint spy network for 10 years (+3 intrigue, +10% hostile scheme success) [Someone] is a threat and must be eliminated A target: the Speaker's demon or mage rival, an inquisitor, or a ruler or head of faith who outlaws witchcraft The target gets Death Sentence for 10 years, and every attendee is offered a curse, a murder plot or a duel against them [A rival mage] should be excluded A Mage rival The target becomes an Outcast for 50 years: no more summits, −10 opinion, a prestige level lost Extraordinary privileges for the Grand Magus The Grand Magus The Grand Magus may Demand Submission from witches and mages Seal the Ancient Singularity Another attendee holds an awakened Singularity It is sealed With the Order off, if the Gnostic Council exists but has no Grand Magus, the summit is an election instead: no Speaker and no motions. The host, any Mages who declare and the two AI attendees best placed are ranked, and the top four stand, so a declared Mage can be cut; everyone votes once, and the winner becomes Grand Magus with a great deal of prestige.

docs.x: Eleven days after the ceremony, if anyone stood, the coven chooses. The score is title rank, plus a point each for being a True Witch or Mage, a heresiarch, the house head, owning a magic artifact and having power to spend, plus three for each round of support gathered at the rite. If the house has no Grand Master the best score wins. If the sitting Grand Master stayed away, he is deposed in his absence . If he came, the winner may challenge him, and he chooses: fight in single combat, which can be fatal , step down for 200 prestige, or, as a player against an AI challenger, refuse at the cost of a prestige level and everyone's regard. The new Grand Master learns the witch secret of every member of the house, and every witch in the house learns his. The five coven policies Policy The coven gets Spreading Witchcraft +1 personal scheme, +10% Convert to Witchcraft, but hostile schemes against you +5% Accumulating Wealth +2 stewardship, +20% tax, −5 general opinion Expanding influence +20% merit, +20% influence, +10 maximum political scheme success, −5% tax Security Prioritization Hostile schemes against you −5 and −5 maximum, +10 travel safety, −5% prestige Seeking of Knowledge +2 learning, +10% lifestyle experience, +5% stress gain Changing a policy you have already set costs 500 prestige. Keeping the current one earns Authority. Two things at a Grand Rite can cost you your life or your soul A demon may appear and offer Gift From Hell (+3 intrigue, +1 stewardship, health) for your soul, which it comes to collect eighteen to twenty years later: die, bargain, or fight a greater demon to the death. You can sell another attendee's soul instead. And a Sacrifice kills one attendee for a great deal of power; the coven may find out who did it.

docs.x: The Order wants six temples , far apart. At game start a player who is a Mage is offered one in A Temple Without a Master : I will be its Temple Magus founds it at your capital. The rest are seated around the best-placed AI Mages, scored on learning and title rank, with a lean toward Western Europe on the base game's map. Witchcraft makes no Mages at the start of a game, so on a fresh start there is often nobody to seat. The Order then gathers itself: every year, while fewer than six temples stand, the best-placed AI Mage outside it founds one. That is at most one temple a year, so expect the six to appear over the first years of a campaign rather than on the first day. Size. A temple holds 30 members, 5 more for every 25 years it has stood, up to 60. AI candidates are only called while a temple is under 80% full; the last fifth is kept for players. How many. One temple for every 170 counties in the world. Charters and daughter temples stop there. Petition for a Charter. A landed member who is not a Temple Magus, at standing 75 (60 under More Hands), while someone else sits in the chair, once every ten years. The Grand Magus decides. Granted, you found a temple at your capital and keep your standing. Found a Daughter Chapter. A landed Magistratus who is not the Temple Magus, at standing 75, from a full temple that has not sent out a daughter in fifty years. Up to five AI members who think well enough of you (20 or more) follow you, keeping their ranks. Found the Order Anew. Shown only when no temple stands anywhere. A landed Mage who knows two other Mages who could join (at his court or visiting, his vassals, his liege, or anyone whose witch secret he holds) founds a temple at his capital, and each of them is asked in The Order Again . Succession. A player Temple Magus can Name as Successor in the Temple a Magistratus of his own temple. Otherwise the highest rank, then the highest standing, takes the temple. A player who becomes Temple Magus by any road chooses its way in The Mask of the Temple . A temple with no members left is gone. What its members pledged stays with them.

Anyone in one of these groups can be called: Who What they need Mages, and anyone with the Source Nothing more Members' children Age 12 to 30 and learning 8, with a parent in the Order. A member's death marks each of his children for forty years Witches Adult, learning 12, a moderate fit, and neither callous nor deceitful Scholars Learning 16, age 16 to 40, a learning education of the second tier or better, and a high fit Unlanded scholars Learning 12, age 16 to 50, a learning education of the third tier or better, no land, and a fair fit Never called: hunters, demons, golems, necromancers, anyone Bound to the Book, anyone who turned the note down in the last ten years or failed the tests in the last thirty, and anyone who ever left the Order keeping what he knew. It favours a young heir to a great title: +25 for an unlanded candidate of 30 or under who is heir to a duchy or more. It passes over AI lords: −30 for a landed AI, and −30 more at kingdom rank, so the Order grows through courtiers rather than kings. A player is never marked down for his lands. It decides whether a witch or a scholar is in the Order's reach at all, player or AI, and half of it is added to every candidate's place in the Selection. docs.x: A Name You Have Heard Before. Two scholars arguing over wine, a book merchant, or your confessor. An adult player with learning 12 and a temple in reach has a 20% chance a year, once in a life. Remember the name puts you within the Order's reach whatever your traits and makes the tests easier for ten years. Ask around about it is an intrigue roll; if it works, someone speaks for you. A Rose Among the Things. When a member dies, a player child of his aged 6 or more finds a box with a pressed rose, a rose coin and a page nobody can read. Keep them and the Order can find you for forty years. Seek Out the Order. A decision for a player who is a Mage or has the Source, once every five years, while a temple stands. If a temple in reach has room, you are near the top of its next Selection. If not, a toast says why. Ask About the Blue Rose. A prison interaction on a member whose secret you know. He gives up at most two others of his temple, and has broken the Order's rules. Then you will name me to them lets him go and puts your name forward.

Not for me keeps you off the list for ten years. The Old Chapel , a few weeks later. The masks explain the three words and what failing costs. I will take the tests or I will walk out now . The Coin , a month or two later. Bring back a coin with a rose on it from a tomb, a bell tower, a mill wheel or a cage. I heed the call makes you an Acolyte with a tutor. A Neophyte at a Conclave takes the oath there, in front of every temple. Fail at any step and it is Pulveris Memoria : you wake in your own bed, remember nothing of the Order, and cannot be called again for thirty years. Nobody dies in the pledge. docs.x: Every Acolyte is given a tutor, the Medicum or higher of his temple with the fewest acolytes. While he has one he carries Under a Tutor , +10% monthly magic lifestyle experience, and each year there is a small chance the two become friends or rivals. The teaching takes six years, a year less each for the Source, learning 15 and a Magistratus tutor, and never under three. A player hears The Words in the first year and The Candle That Would Not Go Out in the third. It ends in The First Real Spell : I am a Mage now gives the Mage trait, Witchcraft's own way. A Warlock or True Witch cannot take a second capstone, so she is taught the Order's craft instead ( I have learned what the Order can teach me ), which counts as taught for the rank of Medicum. When a player is tutor or acolyte, the pair has a moment now and then: The First Lesson , The Errand , Two Heads Over One Problem (shared Magical Research needs one breakthrough fewer), The Lesson Returned , and once, Late Lessons , which can make them lovers if both are 18 or older, unrelated and fond of each other. A temple also has moments of its own: An Outsider Asks Questions (often a real witch hunter), The Relic That Would Not Sleep , A Neophyte's Test Gone Wrong and The Tutor's Quarrel . A child born to two members who are both Mages has a 10% chance of the Source ( A Spark in the Cradle ).

docs.s: The rules, leaving, and the Old Law
docs.x: Breaking the Order's rules marks a member for ten years and costs him 40 opinion with his Temple Magus ( Broke Faith ). It covers exposing a brother's secret, talking under Ask About the Blue Rose , sending Zecchia after a member you know is one, being caught paying her from the council's funds, a cruel member binding the Vade Maecum , and bending the Old Law. An AI Temple Magus casts out a marked member at the temple's year. No rule of the Order kills. Leave the Order is a decision any member can take, and being cast out ends the same way. The Order Does Not Let You Walk Away gives two answers: Let them take it : Pulveris Memoria. You forget the Order and lose your magic: the Mage and True Witch traits, the 21 magic perks, your spells, your stored power, the Fors Factorum and any council seat. The Source and the witch trait or secret stay, because you were born with one and other people know the other. You cannot be called for thirty years. I will keep what I know : you keep everything and can never come back. Four times in ten, two to five years later, They Came for What You Know : a learning roll, and if you lose it, Pulveris Memoria anyway. The Old Law. The Order takes no necromancers. A member who becomes one gets The Forbidden Art each year until it is settled: Renounce it (the Necromancer trait, the Master Necromancer modifier and the right to raise Skeleton Warriors go, with major stress and −20 standing), Let them judge me , or Leave before they cast me out . Rule One is "with demons, don't". A demon may still Seek a Compact with the Order ; the master hears it in A Demon at the Temple Door , and wearing the Seal of Solomon he can make it kneel instead. A demon with a Compact can Borrow from the Reliquary , and owes a favour for every loan.

Taking the Temple Magus alive gives him every member's secret. A year later a player hunter gets The Adeptus Major Moves : take 100 gold and forget the house, or refuse and risk Pulveris Memoria on a learning roll. Never a death. Respondeo and Obfuscation Powder are the Order's answer to a trail.

docs.s: Binding the book, and the Contract
docs.x: Bind the Vade Maecum needs a Mage holding all four pages, unsealed, or the whole book, while nobody else has a Contract running. Its tooltip names the son the book will ask for before you start: the eldest living son of your blood, bastards you never knew of included, or for a woman her eldest son. With no such son the book cannot be paid, and the decision says so. The pages become one book, which is protected while the Contract runs (Zecchia and Seize Their Relics leave it alone), and The Book Names Your Son . You then have three years , shown in your Situations as The Contract : Name as Witness a courtier, spouse or vassal who agrees. He carries Bound as Witness (+15% stress gain, −20% magic lifestyle experience, −1 learning) until he breaks it with Break the Witness's Bond or the last page is burned. If he dies or leaves you, the step is undone. A council member who thinks well of a man who is not cruel may offer himself ( A Councilor Offers ). Tear It Apart (a holder who is not bound, with no Contract running): the book becomes four pages again. Scatter them all, or give one to a Champion in reach, whose hide then keeps it. docs.x: A secret society of Mages, new in 2.38. It is organised in temples, each under a Temple Magus , and it keeps three words: Silence, Subservience, Observance. Every year each temple chooses a few people with the gift or the mind for it, and the ones who pass its tests are taught to be Mages. The Gnostic Council is its council. All of it sits behind the Supernatural: The Blue Rose game rule, which is on by default. A save from before 2.38 counts as on. With it off no temple is ever founded, and the Gnostic Council works as Witchcraft ships it. Relics, covens, Zecchia and the Seal of Solomon exist either way. Membership is not a trait, so nothing on your portrait gives you away. It is a secret, Member of the Hermetic Order , which your Temple Magus learns the day you join. A demon you meet may also have been summoned rather than made; that is a different thing (see Summoning ). It is what unlocks the Demonic lifestyle. Under a rite that shuns or criminalises witchcraft it carries a further −30 crime modifier and legal grounds to imprison, execute or banish. It is what the demon tree's capstone grants, and taking it removes Minor Demon. It carries the same −20 general opinion. Demons are opposite to every creature in the mod. Vampire, werewolf and hybrid all list them as incompatible, and a witch hunter is −30 to them. Children Demons can have children. That is governed by its own game rule, Supernatural: Demon Inheritance/Pregnancy , separate from the werewolf one. At its default two demons have a 75 per cent chance of a demon-blooded child, and a demon with a human, a werewolf or a hybrid has 50. A Greater Demon parent adds 15 to either. That child is demon-blooded or human, never a wolf. Turn the rule off and demons rely on adoption, which is what the mod did before the rule existed. Not every pregnancy holds. docs.x: A minor demon who steals for a fee, new in 2.38. She is one woman, a Minor Demon of House Hellion with the Source, greedy and fond of drink, who comes back each time she is called; if she is ever killed, the next summoning makes another. She moves things, never people or titles. There are three ways to reach her: Summon Demon. She is one more entry in the roll (8 of 137 when every entry is open), for a clean binding while she is not already working for someone. The first time, A Thief Answers . Study the Black Grimoire can turn up A Name in the Margin : her name. Summon Zecchia , a decision for anyone who knows her name, every two years: a Mage pays a standard spend of power, and a wearer of the Seal of Solomon pays nothing. Her name passes to your heir when you die. A member of the Order who calls her loses 10 standing (Rule One), unless the Order is treating with the Pit. How Much Will You Take? One to five things; four and five need 400 and 500 gold in hand, and a Chancellor can put it on the Gnostic Council's funds ( The Council will pay ). She asks a personal price as well: a long drink (major stress and some gold), something of yours (your best ordinary artifact, or 100 prestige), or a lock of your hair. Then you have ninety days to point her at someone with Send Zecchia After Their Treasures . Ninety days later, Zecchia Delivers : up to the agreed number of the target's items, the best first, pledged and lent ones included. She will not take a hide, the Seal, the book while a Contract runs, a dynasty or house banner, or anything tied to a title. Her fee is paid then: 100 gold for each thing agreed, plus 50 to 200 for each thing she brought, by its rarity. The same hirer cannot set her on the same victim again for ten years. If you never name anyone, Zecchia Is Getting Bored : name them now, pay half and let her go, or ask for more than you agreed, in which case she robs you instead. A later victim who goes to her while she holds your lock of hair can ask Who hired you against me? , and she tells him. Sending her after a member of your own temple, or one you know is a member, can mark you as having broken the Order's rules.

docs.x: Nearly every demon in the game belongs to one house. The dynasty is displayed as Hell and the house as Hellion , two different words for the same family, which is the single most confusing thing about this content. A second house, Maledictio , belongs to the same dynasty and holds one demon. Both carry a white-and-red snake on black. Sixteen of the seventeen demon templates place their character into House Hellion, which is why the house grows over a long campaign: every summoning, every escaped binding, every demonic courtier adds a member. Fixed in 2.35 (10 September 2026). The invented-witch template used by witch hunts also placed its character in House Hellion, so every woman a hunt turned up joined the demons' house. A live campaign came back with 246 living members , almost all of them invented witches. Witches are now born without a dynasty. Demons keep the house.

docs.x: Seventeen perks in one tree with two arms, one for war and one for guile, meeting at a root that hands out +10 to every skill and +10 prowess , the largest flat stat block anywhere in the mod. The war arm ends at Greater Demon; the guile arm ends at Crossroad Dealmaker and the cyrograph. Two focuses, Manipulation and Destruction, and both carry +30 per cent stress gain . The Demonic lifestyle is the only one in the mod that taxes you for being in it. It is also designed to be finished and abandoned: taking both capstones clears your focus and closes both focuses to you permanently. And because summoned demons are handed all seventeen perks the moment they appear, the lifestyle is in practice only for a mortal who became a demon. A Prince of Hell has already finished it before you meet him.

docs.x: Before 2.35 the mod's only answer to a demon was killing it, and demons are immortal. Upstream's Banish Demon spell does not banish. It kills, and every greater demon is immune to it. Meanwhile a greater demon can recruit another demon into its court every four years, forever. The population compounded and had no drain. Exorcism is that drain, and it is the hunter's verb rather than the mage's: it costs no magical power at all. It sits inside the demon hunt, as one of three things you can do at the confrontation. The numbers: what an exorcism is worth to attempt The chance starts at 40 and is clamped between 5 and 90. Term Value Monster-Hunter track +0.5 each, so up to +50 Witch-Hunter track +0.2 each, so up to +20 Caught mid-feeding +15 One other hunter attending +10 Two or more other hunters +20 in total The demon is a greater demon −25 Its Hell Powers −0.2 each, so down to −20 Its reputation −0.1 each, so down to −10 A career hunter against a plain minor demon is capped at 90 . The same man against a Prince at high powers is about 50 . A green hunter against that same Prince is 8 . The witch-hunting experience, 5 to 12, is paid either way . A man learns the words by saying them at something that did not listen just as surely as at something that did. What success looks like depends on what the demon is. A summoned demon was never a person, and the body it was wearing simply collapses. A made demon, a mortal who was turned, has someone underneath, and the exorcism gives them back. The game answers that question by asking whether the demon has a father and a house of its own, because every summoned template is fatherless and Hellion. Named demons cannot be exorcised. Failing does not kill you. It drops you into an ordinary fight at a 20-point penalty , with the way out still open. After a failed exorcism there are two other ways out. Breaking it off, Hit it hard enough to get out of the doorway , ends the hunt as a withdrawal: you spend a year recovering at −2 prowess, the demon becomes your rival and hates you for a decade, and it is either pushed into a neighbouring province or, if it holds land and cannot move, marked as driven off for five years. The county's trail is wiped either way, and the county still counts one refusal . And the bargain is the one where you sign its cyrograph: you are healed, de-aged and improved across every skill, and it takes your soul on a ten-, twenty- or thirty-year timer. A hunter who later learns to put demons down will refuse to pay when the bill arrives, and the demon has a war that executes soulless defenders outright.

docs.x: Two focuses, Monster Hunter and Witch-Hunter, worth +3 martial and +3 intrigue respectively, and those attribute points are the whole mechanical payload of a focus here. Everything else in a focus is the AI deciding what kind of hunter it wants to be. Two trees of eight perks each. The Monster Hunter tree has two roots that converge on The Witcher . The perk adds +35 life expectancy and grants the True Monster Hunter trait: +5 prowess, +3 martial and half a prestige a month. Stacked with Built Different's +10 and the trait's own +5, a finished monster hunter lives fifty years longer than he would have. The Witch-Hunter tree ends at the Witch-Hunter perk, which grants the True Witch Hunter trait. Several of its perks unlock things: Anti-Mage , the root, opens witch trials and the old witch-hunting decision. Combat Spells reaches the Witcher's elixirs, letting a hunter brew potions without being a witch. Protection Runes grants the witch tree's own protective perk, which more than thirty magic gates read. It did nothing at all until it was noticed that the two perks' names differ by one letter. Hunter Academy unlocks the regiment. A hunter can never take a witch, mage or warlock capstone. The perks refuse to be picked rather than failing silently, which is what they used to do.

docs.x: The hunter's regiment. Skirmishers, 50 to a stack and ten sub-regiments at the cap, needing both the Hunter trait and the Hunter Academy perk to raise or reinforce, so an heir can field an inherited regiment but cannot replace its losses until he has earned the perk himself. They do not out-fight monsters and are not meant to. One vampire sub-regiment hits for 1,850 and takes 1,750; a full trainee stack hits for 700 and takes 900. The counter is the point: a quarter against monsters and animals, and a tenth against demonic knights. A maxed hunter's guard neutralises one monster regiment, not an army of them. Fielding them is also one of the ways to bring the county's men to the door.

docs.x: Hunters have secrets too. Depending on what your rite, or a liege's above you, holds about hunters, you either carry a hidden Hunter secret or the open Known Hunter trait. The trait is +15 opinion between known hunters and −20 with vampires, werewolves and hybrids, and gives a rite that favours creatures a crime to charge you with. A rite takes the same four positions on hunters as it does on each kind of creature. What your rite thinks of you has them, and The known traits compares all five.

docs.x: The hunt gives each kind of creature a way of leaving evidence in the county it fed in, and builds a three-week activity around a hunter riding there to find out what it is and who it is. Both sides are playable. The creature gets a screen at every point the hunter does. Trails and what leaves them Everything here runs on one thing: a county that carries Something Stalks Here . The modifier is worth −5 county opinion and nothing else, and it does not suppress growth. The cost of a creature living somewhere is the drain each incident does, not a standing penalty. A county holds four facts under that modifier: who the culprit is, what kind it is, how many incidents there have been, and whether the lord has been told. The kind is shown only to a hunter who has learned to read wounds; everyone else sees a county with a problem. The first incident is usually only a whisper. It leaves no modifier, no map pin, no culprit and nothing a Trailsman can read, and it expires in a year. A second incident inside that year opens a real trail immediately. A first incident can also be noticed outright on a roll: 30 per cent for a body, 12 per cent for a prowl. Once a trail is open, every later incident escalates it without a roll, up to a cap of six. The numbers: what each incident costs the county Kind A kill A prowl Vampire −5 county control −1 control Werewolf −2 control, −1 prosperity −1 control Demon −4 control, −1 prosperity −2 control Witch −2 control, −1 prosperity −1 control A demon does not feed, it ruins, so the county pays for it twice. A witch is the quietest of the four. The county loses faith in its lord faster than it loses people. What counts as an incident. Killing on a feed, a feed somebody talks about (a witness who got away, a compulsion that did not take, or about one clean feed in ten), a werewolf's border run, a demon escaping a botched binding, a witch's plague spell, the corruption scheme, a body you chose to leave as your own, and a body you pinned on someone else. Roughly two dozen places in the game write a mark. Since 2.36 a feed nobody talks about leaves no mark at all, and the first warning that a county remembers you reads differently when what it remembers is talk rather than a body. What does not. A death in a tournament. A death in war, or with either party in an army. Killing a prisoner. And any death inside a hunt. A body that turns up inside a supernatural hunt is the hunt's business. Hunters never leave marks, because a hunter is not a creature. Since 2.35a the killer also has to be in the same province as the victim, so a murder scheme carried out from somewhere else no longer counts as a creature's kill. A murder in your own hall still does. Forgetting. There is no decay event. The modifier is added for five years and refreshed on every incident, so a trail dies five years after the last thing that happened. You can shorten it deliberately: leaving the county clears one mark, paying the lord off clears one and leaves him a debt he will remember if a hunter later proves what was living there, and a compulsion in a county carrying your own trail can bury an incident outright. And a trail whose culprit has died goes cold: no hunt can ever answer it. When the culprit dies the game looks for someone in that county who could plausibly have been doing it, whether a creature or a witch in the holder's court or the holder himself, and hands the trail to them, re-deriving the kind. If there is nobody, the trail is wiped. A census on a live 346 AC save, taken before that change, found 23 trails in the world and only four of them warm : nineteen counties carried a mark no hunter could answer, for five years each. docs.x: The activity header the mod ships for the Supernatural Hunt. The Supernatural Hunt is an activity. You need the Hunter trait, you must not be recovering from your last one, and there must be something within reach worth hunting. The button greys out and tells you which of those is missing. Since 2.35a a hunt ends if its host is not a hunter. It costs half what a vanilla activity of its size costs, an eighth for a landless adventurer, and nothing if you are riding under a contract. The cooldown is two years . There are two kinds. A Monster Hunt needs a county that carries a trail left by a living creature. A Witch Hunt can be held anywhere in your own lands, a vassal's or your liege's, and if you ride it to a county that carries a witch trail with a live culprit, it runs the whole monster spine instead of the thin version. Where you can ride. A hunt is held at a county's capital , because a trail is a fact about a county. You can reach anywhere within your court's ordinary range, or anywhere at all under your own top liege, so a duke can hunt across the kingdom, a king across the empire. A landless adventurer's reach is five times a landed hunter's radius. What you are allowed to hunt. A creature that has beaten hunters before is gated by reputation. A legend of 2 or more wants a Monster-Hunter track of 40, or two hunters riding with you. A legend of 4 or more wants a track of 75, or 40 and three hunters. The hunters counted are the ones in your court. A landless hunter, or one with fewer than two trails in his realm, is let through either gate. And a county that has been hunted in the last four years is closed while it catches its breath. What you take with you. One kit and one approach: Choice What it does Travel Light Nothing. The default. Stakes +15 at the door against a vampire or a hybrid, and neither can look you in the eye. −10 against a werewolf. Silver +15 against a werewolf or a hybrid. −10 against a vampire, and a vampire or hybrid of any rank can look you in the eye. Hire Local Guides +15 tracking. Ask Quietly No change. The creatures may still hear that a stranger is asking. Ride In Openly +10 tracking. Every creature in the county will hear of you. Read the Signs +5 tracking, +5 at the door. Against a hybrid either kit works: stakes and silver are each worth +15. An AI hunter who can read the trail picks the right kit; one who cannot, guesses. Up to four other hunters can ride with you, drawn from your friends, family, court and the hunters whose secret you keep. Each one is worth +10 on the tracking bar up to three, and another blade at the door. An apprentice who rides with their trainer can finish their training on the hunt.

docs.x: The tracking phase runs three weeks and the whole of it feeds one number, shown as a Tracking bar with its own breakdown. It starts at 35 and is clamped between 5 and 95. The numbers: every term in the tracking bar Term Value Base 35 Your Monster-Hunter track +0.5 each, up to +50 Your reputation +3 per rung. Only the first rung can be reached at present ( Known issues ). The creature's legend −3 per rung. Four rungs can be reached, so down to −12. Hunters riding with you +10 each, up to +30 Local guides +15 A county that remembers too little +8 Riding in openly +10 (reading the signs, +5, unless a local hunter rides with you) A local hunter riding with you +10 You know what the creature is +20 The creature's power −0.25 each, down to −25 The trail has gone quiet: it left the county −25 The culprit is a hide's Champion −15, and −10 more for Timber's Champion in no pack You keep a hide yourself, and the culprit is a wolf +10 What the three weeks taught you whatever the events added What fills those three weeks is a weekly pool of events. A survivor who can be listened to or pressed. What the graves say. A mob that has picked the wrong man: let him go, or let them have him for 25 prestige and two years of a county that remembers. A fellow hunter's tale. A county so crowded with creatures that you can be counted yourself. Another hunter already working the same trail, who can be ridden with, questioned, or warned off. The field events are the ones that read the kind. By the Moon tells you when a wolf will be out, worth +20 , or you can warn the county and lose ground instead. Not a Drop points a vampire hunt at the people who survived. Two Different Animals is the hybrid's tell, and getting it right is worth 15 while guessing two creatures costs you. They Are All Very Sure is a county that has been compelled, so stop asking what happened and start asking what they cannot remember. And when your bar reaches 60 on a monster hunt, the creature is told, wherever it is. He Asked About You By Name gives it three choices: run now, and the hunt ends with nothing but two years of not feeding; misdirect him on an intrigue duel, which takes 20 off everything he has built; or let him come. A demon gets It Knows Your Name instead, and argues .

docs.x: The confrontation phase opens on Cornered . If the county is crowded, you are told how many will stand with the thing before you choose how to go in: Strike now. Wait for daylight : +15 against a vampire or hybrid, nothing against a wolf. Bring the county's men : +10, if the lord likes you, you field Hunter Trainees , or the county pledged its men during the tracking. This is practically a nest : always available. You withdraw, lose 25 prestige, and the county counts a refusal against you. Then the creature answers, in Someone Is Asking Questions . There are eight answers, and most have a condition: Answer What happens Let them come The fight. Go to ground An intrigue duel. Hidden: you are gone, one mark comes off, your kin are warned, and you cannot feed for two years. Found: the hunter goes into the fight +15 up. There is worse than me in this land A diplomacy duel, available only when a neighbouring county is carrying three or more incidents from another living creature. You do not deny what you are; you tell him where the bodies are stacking higher, and it is true. He leaves and rides there instead. Refused, you have told a hunter you keep count, and the fight is harder. Look them in the eye Vampires and hybrids only, and never if he brought stakes. If he brought silver it is open at any rank. Otherwise you need a full Vampirism track and a hunter below 40 on his Monster-Hunter track. Costs 20 track experience and pays 8 to 15 back. He turns around. Let it out Werewolves and hybrids. Thirty days in full wolf form, +15 in the fight, and every hunter at the door learns what you are. For a hide's Champion it kills the hunter with no fight . Send [name] Your progeny, or failing that the one you clawed, goes instead. A player in that position gets their own screen, and can refuse. Make them an offer Needs a track of 75 and 100 gold in hand. He gets 50 gold and a stipend for five years, and you get a strong hook on him. If he refuses, he gains 25 prestige and five points in the fight. [Champion] stands over me Only while Silverback's Champion has his guard on you through Stand Over Them . He fights the hunter in your place. The numbers: how the fight is scored A prowess duel, both sides starting at 50 and floored at 10. The creature The hunter Prowess difference, up to ±25 The same, reversed Its track × 0.6, up to +60 Monster-Hunter track × 0.6, up to +60 +15 shapeshifted, or Evolved and not shifted +10 for True Monster Hunter +10 hybrid Everything he brought (kit, daylight, the county's men, a local hunter, a refused bargain) comes off the creature's side +10 forewarned −12 per kin standing with it, −6 per stranger, first three only A hide's Champion then multiplies his whole side by his Hide Strength , ×1.5 to ×3. A True Alpha with no hide multiplies his by 1.25. Losing does not have to be the end. Overmatched lets you fall back for a wound, a year recovering and some experience, or press on at a further 20-point penalty, where losing means you do not leave. Winning gives you a screen of your own, It Is Done . You can finish it, or take it alive if you hold land. Who stands with the creature # When a hunt reaches its end in a county, the game walks that county's holder, courtiers, guests and any player standing there, and asks of each one: are you a creature, are you not a demon, are you not going to ground yourself, and do you have a reason to stand. Kin qualifies, meaning anyone linked by claw or by blood, and since 2.37 a wolf of the same pack . So does the defender being a legend, and so does not disliking them. Vampires stand with werewolves under the same rule; kind does not matter at the door. Only the first three joiners change the fight, and only by a fixed amount: kin are worth 12 each, strangers 6 , so three kin take 36

docs.x: Eleven outcomes, and the conclusion screen, What the Hunt Was Worth , has its own text for each. The county's recovery is scaled to what was living in it: Outcome The county The hunter Slain or exorcised Vampire or hybrid: +5 control. Demon: +4 and a point of prosperity. Werewolf or witch: +2 and a point. The whole trail is removed. Prestige scaled by what it was, 15 to 35 Monster-Hunter, and the bounty. Guests take 5 to 15. Proxy slain +1 or +2 control, one mark cleared, the culprit still out there Three quarters of the prestige, 10 to 25 track Fled Nothing. The trail stays. +25 prestige, 5 to 10 track Withdrew A refusal counted against the county, unless you walked away in the first week, which costs nothing 3 to 8 track. Apprentices do not graduate; there was no lesson in it. Cold Nothing 5 to 10 track Compelled Nothing. The trail stays. 3 to 8 track Bought Nothing. The trail stays. The creature's gold and stipend, 5 to 10 track Hunter beaten Nothing. The trail stays. Medium stress Witch Nothing 10 to 20 Witch-Hunter track Bargained Nothing. The trail stays. Medium stress, and the bargain he signed The bounty starts at 40, adds five per point of county development and a little over one per point of the creature's power, and is floored at 40 and capped at 320. Against a hunt that costs about 45, a poor county's ordinary vampire pays around 90 and a rich city's elder pays a few hundred. A refusal is a hunter who withdraws at the door, or dies there. Three of them inside ten years and the county picks up No One Will Come for ten years: −8 county opinion and slower control growth. AI hunters then stay away unless their Monster-Hunter track is 75 or more; a player can still ride there. The creature it failed to catch gets They Stopped Coming , which adds to its dread and its legend. Killing a culprit can leave children behind, and the hunt asks what you do about them. Names the world uses # Two reputations come out of a hunt, and both are read off what the characters remember doing. A hunter's name climbs at one, two, three, five and eight creatures slain. A creature's legend climbs by besting hunters and, worth double, by killing them. Each can end in a nickname: Nickname Who How the Unhunted A creature A legend of three, checked when it beats a hunter. From then on only serious hunters are allowed to come for it. the Beastbane A hunter A name of three. It cannot be earned at present: a hunter only records his first kill, so his name stops at the first rung ( Known issues ). the Wolf A hide's Champion Ten knights killed in battle , if he has no other nickname. A fourth nickname in the files, "the Timeless", has no text and is granted by nothing.

docs.x: When a player's creature kills someone in person, the next morning brings What They Will Find , and up to four answers: Make it look like nothing. A roll on your strength and your talent for lying. Clean, and there is no mark at all. Find whoever would have had to write this down. No roll, and it costs 40 to 250 gold by the county's wealth. The lord takes your money, the county takes a mark off, and he remembers who paid. Let them look at [name]. Offered when there is someone to frame. The same roll fifteen points harder, and a success writes the mark against another creature carrying their kind , so a vampire who dresses a body as a wolf's work sends the county's next hunter to a wolf's door. You cannot frame your own maker, progeny or the one you clawed. Let them know it was me. No roll. The trail is yours and it is loud: three incidents at once, and every soul in the lord's hall is told what walked through. Hunters will come. A botched feeding has its own answers, one of which is to silence the witness. Compulsion works the other way. It is not an incident. Used in a county carrying your own trail it cleans , at 30 per cent with no power behind it and up to 80 at a full track. Used badly, and low power is the main way to be sloppy, it leaves a hole instead. Three holes inside five years and the county picks up Nobody Here Remembers , and its lord starts asking why, which is its own investigation and can end with a real trail carrying your name.

docs.x: A court position, and a camp officer version for landless adventurers. The employer does not have to be a hunter. The Trailsman walks your counties and reads what has been left in them. Bodies found at the edge of a village, herds taken in a way no wolf takes them, a road nobody will use after dark. He goes and looks, and he comes back and tells you where. A good one comes back with a name. Aptitude runs on prowess and martial, with +35 for holding the Hunter trait (the tooltip calls it "Has hunted one before"), +15 for a True Witch Hunter who lacks it, +15 for a lifestyle hunter, +10 for patience, +5 for Athletic at court, and −40 for being a creature , because a creature does not report on its own kind. The AI appoints one too, and is far keener to when a county in the realm carries a trail. Three tasks: Task What it does Chance a year Read the Countryside Finds a trail you have not been told about. Your priests only write once a county has lost three people; he goes before that. 40, up to 70 at high aptitude Follow the Trail Puts a face to a trail you already know about, and the only way short of hunting it yourself. Costs double. 20, up to 65 Beat the Bounds County opinion and faster control recovery, scaling with aptitude. Finds nothing. It is the standing answer to what a trail drains. — He will not report a trail while your hunt is on cooldown, so you are not told about a monster you cannot ride for.

docs.x: On the third incident, the county's lord is told. Something Stalks gives him five answers: look into it himself, put his spymaster on it, post a bounty, send for a hunter, or write it off as superstition and keep bleeding control. Looking into it is an intrigue duel against how well the creature hides, which scales with its power. Winning reveals the culprit to him by name. The spymaster runs the same duel with a bonus for being a schemer, and a Trailsman turns the compelled-county version into a far better one. Post a bounty creates a real task contract that any landless adventurer hunter can take off the board: the county's menace, with a purse on it. That needs the landless expansion. Send for a hunter needs nothing. Three letters go out with names on them, and the lord is shown three men in the order of what they are asking for. The roster is built nearest first: the man in your own hall, then the men who owe you, then the world. The fee starts at 60 and rises with the hunter's Monster-Hunter track, between 40 and 150 in all. It does not depend on the lord's purse. The hunter can accept, refuse, or write back naming a higher price, which doubles it. A county can only be answered once, because the first lord to write stamps it for ten years, so two lords can never both have a man on the same trail. And a hunter who holds both a bounty contract and a summons for the same county is paid twice, which is deliberate.
