docs.x: Every creature and every hunter lives behind a secret until it is known. What happens then depends on the rite: each rite takes a position on each kind, and that position decides the opinion, the crime and, since 2.36, what your own rite makes of how you live. Secrets and exposure What happens when you turn depends on what your rite thinks of you. The rule is the same for every kind; a vampire is the example here. If your rite, or a liege's above you, shuns or criminalises vampirism, you get a hidden secret , and the people who made you are told about it so your own spymaster stops rediscovering it forever. If nobody around you cares, you get nothing at all, and you go on being a vampire that the game has no public record of. There is a slow fuse as well, for every immortal. A supernatural who has been immortal more than eighty-five years and is over a hundred and twenty-five rolls three per cent a pulse that somebody finally works out why the lord has not aged. Membership of the Order of the Blue Rose is a secret of the same kind, Member of the Hermetic Order . Exposed, it marks the county the member is in for witch hunters. The known traits Each kind has an open trait for the state after the secret: Known Vampire , Known Werewolf , Known Hybrid and Known Hunter . The opinion on a known trait applies only between two holders of the same trait, and against the one enemy the trait names. What everyone else thinks comes from the rite , and is the same for every kind. Known trait With others who hold it With its enemy Baseline dread Known Vampire +20 −15 with hunters +15 Known Werewolf +25 −30 with hunters none Known Hybrid +35 −10 with hunters +20 Known Hunter +15 −20 with vampires, werewolves and hybrids none A demon No known trait. The demon traits carry −20 general opinion from everyone, known or not. Being known costs a vampire or hybrid at the table too: −15 on every feeding success roll, and an AI vampire in that position is far less willing to host one. A known Champion carries extra dread . What your rite thinks of you Each rite takes one of four positions on each kind of creature, set as a doctrine: Criminal , Shunned , Accepted or Virtuous . Since CK3 1.20 these sit on the rite rather than the faith, so two rites of one faith can disagree, and a new rite gets them too. Criminal is −30 opinion from everyone not of your kind and a legal reason to imprison or execute; Shunned is −15. Under Criminal, since 2.36, a known creature is a sin of that rite as well, which costs it another 20 with the faithful. Virtuous makes Known Vampire a virtue of the rite and costs a great deal of piety to adopt. Your rite and fulfillment Crusader Kings III 1.20 added Spiritual Fulfillment , a measure of how well a character's life fits their faith. Since 2.36 a creature's own rite weighs three of the things it does: a feed the victim lives through, a kill by fang or claw, and turning someone into your own kind. This applies to vampires, werewolves and hybrids alike, each judged by the rite's doctrine for its own kind. Your rite holds your kind What the act does Virtuous Raises fulfillment: 3 for a feed, 5 for a kill, 10 for a turning. Known or not. Criminal Lowers it by the same amounts, but only once you are known for what you are. A creature behind a secret lives as a member of its faith in good standing and is not charged. Shunned or Accepted Nothing. How hard it lands depends on how much you care. Vanilla's own multipliers apply, so a zealous character feels a loss twice over, and a cynic is never charged at all. A known creature whose rite outlaws its kind also cares less about that rite: −25 per cent on every fulfillment gain and loss, −10 per cent if the rite only shuns it. If your rite, or a liege's above you, shuns or criminalises vampirism, you get a hidden secret , and the people who made you are told about it so your own spymaster stops rediscovering it forever. If nobody around you cares, you get nothing at all, and you go on being a vampire that the game has no public record of. There is a slow fuse as well, for every immortal. A supernatural who has been immortal more than eighty-five years and is over a hundred and twenty-five rolls three per cent a pulse that somebody finally works out why the lord has not aged. Membership of the Order of the Blue Rose is a secret of the same kind, Member of the Hermetic Order . Exposed, it marks the county the member is in for witch hunters.

docs.x: Each kind has an open trait for the state after the secret: Known Vampire , Known Werewolf , Known Hybrid and Known Hunter . The opinion on a known trait applies only between two holders of the same trait, and against the one enemy the trait names. What everyone else thinks comes from the rite , and is the same for every kind. Known trait With others who hold it With its enemy Baseline dread Known Vampire +20 −15 with hunters +15 Known Werewolf +25 −30 with hunters none Known Hybrid +35 −10 with hunters +20 Known Hunter +15 −20 with vampires, werewolves and hybrids none A demon No known trait. The demon traits carry −20 general opinion from everyone, known or not. Being known costs a vampire or hybrid at the table too: −15 on every feeding success roll, and an AI vampire in that position is far less willing to host one. A known Champion carries extra dread .

docs.s: What your rite thinks of you
docs.x: Each rite takes one of four positions on each kind of creature, set as a doctrine: Criminal , Shunned , Accepted or Virtuous . Since CK3 1.20 these sit on the rite rather than the faith, so two rites of one faith can disagree, and a new rite gets them too. Criminal is −30 opinion from everyone not of your kind and a legal reason to imprison or execute; Shunned is −15. Under Criminal, since 2.36, a known creature is a sin of that rite as well, which costs it another 20 with the faithful. Virtuous makes Known Vampire a virtue of the rite and costs a great deal of piety to adopt.

docs.x: Crusader Kings III 1.20 added Spiritual Fulfillment , a measure of how well a character's life fits their faith. Since 2.36 a creature's own rite weighs three of the things it does: a feed the victim lives through, a kill by fang or claw, and turning someone into your own kind. This applies to vampires, werewolves and hybrids alike, each judged by the rite's doctrine for its own kind. Your rite holds your kind What the act does Virtuous Raises fulfillment: 3 for a feed, 5 for a kill, 10 for a turning. Known or not. Criminal Lowers it by the same amounts, but only once you are known for what you are. A creature behind a secret lives as a member of its faith in good standing and is not charged. Shunned or Accepted Nothing. How hard it lands depends on how much you care. Vanilla's own multipliers apply, so a zealous character feels a loss twice over, and a cynic is never charged at all. A known creature whose rite outlaws its kind also cares less about that rite: −25 per cent on every fulfillment gain and loss, −10 per cent if the rite only shuns it. A toast tells you why each time it happens. Hunters are weighed the other way round. Putting a creature down is righteous where its kind is outlawed and sacrilege where it is revered, 3 either way, whether or not the creature was known: a slaying is the creature unmasked. And since 1.20, choices in the mod's events count through your personality as vanilla's do, so an option that goes against a virtue of your faith costs a little fulfillment, creature or not.

docs.x: Six lifestyles, ten trees, and they are not priced the same. What a lifestyle costs per level, and how many trees it has to spend those levels on, is most of what separates the creatures in a long game. Lifestyle Per level Base gain Trees Ends at Vampire 1,500 30 Vampirism, 10 perks True Vampire Werewolf 1,100 27 Lycanthropy, 8 perks True Werewolf Hunter 1,400 25 Monster Hunter and Witch-Hunter, 8 each The Witcher / Witch-Hunter Hybrid 1,500 30 Vampirism and Lycanthropy, 9 each Both capstones, then the master focus Magic 1,000 25 Witchery 8, Arcane 7, Black Magic 6 One of True Witch, Mage or Warlock Demonic 1,000 25 Demon, 17 perks Greater Demon and Crossroad Dealmaker Magic and Demonic are the cheapest per level, at 1,000. The werewolf is the cheapest of the three blood lifestyles and has the least to buy. The vampire and the hybrid cost the most per level, and the hybrid has eighteen perks to get through ( The hybrid lifestyle ). The demon's tree is the largest single tree in the mod, and taking both its capstones closes the lifestyle behind you ( The Demonic lifestyle ). The vampire, werewolf and hybrid lifestyles each have a master focus that unlocks only when you hold the capstone: Ancient Vampirism, Indomitable Lycanthropy and The Immortal Hybrid. It grants a broad spread of attributes and no further lifestyle experience . Two problems in this area were fixed and are worth knowing about because they change how the AI behaves. Before 2.32 only the root perk of each tree carried a weight, so an AI entered a tree and stopped; every perk now carries one and the AI climbs. And a hunter holding a magic artifact used to be outbid into a magic focus, because the hunter focuses sat at a flat weight while the magic ones stacked past it. The creature focuses now all multiply themselves down for a hunter rather than zeroing, so a hunter can end up there, it simply stops being his first pick. Every perk, tree by tree All ninety perks and sixteen focuses, read from the files. "After" is the perk you need first; a perk with two parents needs both. A capstone is marked with its icon. Where a perk's tooltip promises something the mod never does, or does something the tooltip does not mention, it says so here. docs.x: Ten men-at-arms regiments: five from the Supernatural layer, five from Witchcraft. They are bought in three currencies, gold, prestige and piety, and only one of them is free to keep. Regiment Who can raise it Cost Damage / toughness Stack Wolves Any werewolf or hybrid 65 prestige 100 / 75 10 Werewolves Lycanthropy 50, or a hide's Champion 100 prestige 215 / 185 5 Bats Any vampire or hybrid Gold 5 / 5 250 Vampires Vampirism 50 100 piety 185 / 175 10 Hunter Trainees Hunter + Hunter Academy 60 gold 14 / 18 50, ten sub-regiments Cultists A coven culture, or a camp that unlocks them 50 gold 15 / 14 100 Skeleton Warriors A necromancer 200 prestige 20 / 14 100 Demonic Knights The demon tree's Infernal Guardians 1,000 prestige 300 / 80 100 Battle Golems A finished golem project 1,000 gold 250 / 100 100 Hut On The Chicken's Leg (Baba Yaga's hut) Yaga, with the house 1,000 gold 1,000 / 100 10, exactly one ever Vampires are the only thing in the game maintained in piety as well as gold ; wolves and werewolves are maintained in prestige. Skeletons cost nothing to keep at either maintenance level, so a necromancer fields a thousand free skeletons for prestige alone. Demonic Knights, Battle Golems and the hut cost nothing while they are not raised. The creature regiments cannot be borrowed through a vassal, because every one of them refuses to be raised through a subject. Two counters in the files do not work , and the files say so. Bats claim a bonus against werewolves and werewolves claim one against vampires, but a counter key has to name a regiment type , and both of those are keys whose type is Monster. They are inert. Hunter Trainees' counters are written correctly and do work. Artifacts Every artifact in the mod is created at runtime by an event or an effect. Witchcraft's artifacts share one template , marked unique and impossible to reforge, with sixteen visual keys hung off it, and there is no fixed list to collect. The six hides of 2.37 have a type and a template of their own; see The Six Hides . The relics of 2.38 and the Seal of Solomon have a type of their own, and the pages of the Vade Maecum a template. What you can end up carrying includes the Darkblade, the Crown of Shadows, a black grimoire, dragonscales, rings of life, death and power, two ancient singularities, a witch's amulet, Baba Yaga's broom, a magic orb, Hell's Scepter, a witch hunter's crossbow, Merlin's wand, and the eleven potions. Only the Darkblade and Merlin's wand have real per-culture art; the rest borrow a vanilla mesh. Darkblade Crown of Shadows Black Grimoire Dragonscales Ring Ancient Singularity Magic Catalyst Orb of Truth Hell's Scepter Amulet of Protection Baba Yaga's broom Merlin's wand Witch hunter's crossbow The Search for Magical Artifacts finds who owns these and makes your claim; Magical Research can wake the Ancient Singularity and forge the Enchanted Ring; the Demonic Invasion and the War Against the Witch both take every magical artifact the loser holds. Witchcraft's magical artifacts turn up over the years with a ruler; since 2.38 that can be a landless adventurer, and one time in four a courtier of his finds it instead. Relics and the reliquary 2.38 adds the relics : seven lesser magical items and the Seal of Solomon. Each is worn in the trinket slot, does one thing and never decays. None is one of Witchcraft's magical artifacts, so a relic does not open the Arcane focus or meet Witchcraft's other needs for a magic item, and relics do not count toward the eight a Search for Magical Artifacts allows. Each use needs the relic worn, and your own: a borrowed Glove, Necrophone or Mirror does not work, and the Powder cannot be borrowed. A borrowed Blade, Bell, Pendant or Seal works for whoever wears it. Relic Worn Use The Glove (famed) +2 intrigue Q

None is one of Witchcraft's magical artifacts, so a relic does not open the Arcane focus or meet Witchcraft's other needs for a magic item, and relics do not count toward the eight a Search for Magical Artifacts allows. Each use needs the relic worn, and your own: a borrowed Glove, Necrophone or Mirror does not work, and the Powder cannot be borrowed. A borrowed Blade, Bell, Pendant or Seal works for whoever wears it. Relic Worn Use The Glove (famed) +2 intrigue Question Under the Glove , on your own prisoner, every two years. He chooses: I will tell you the truth (you learn one of his secrets, or one he knows about someone else), I will lie (he is burned, wounded but never killed, and you gain a hook on him; he hates you for it), or, for a werewolf, Endure it . One time in four word gets out: his liege thinks less of you, and your county gets a witch mark The Necrophone (famed) +2 learning Call the Dead , once a year. Ask where a page of the Vade Maecum is, where the lost hide is, or where the Seal of Solomon is kept. The third call breaks it The Enchanted Blade (masterwork) +4 prowess On a hunt against a werewolf or hybrid it counts as silver (+15). It is the one thing that lets a hunter win against a man Bound to the Book The Echo Pendant (masterwork) Immunity to ordinary curses None Obfuscation Powder (common) Nothing Throw the Powder : the trail on the county you stand in goes cold, and the powder is used up. Only the Order makes it, with Prepare the Powder The Mirror Shard (famed) Nothing Bind Our Fates , with someone who agrees (an AI only for a lover, a best friend, or a vassal who adores you), every ten years. For ten years, if either of you is killed, the other dies the next day. A natural death only ends the bond. Break the Mirror ends it and destroys the shard The Bell of the Dead Hour (masterwork) +10% dread gain When a hunter comes for you in the county you are in, +40 to the chance you are warned The Seal of Solomon (illustrious) +2 learning, +10% piety, cannot be magically dominated See below Where they come from. With the Order on, when it first seats its temples, each temple standing then gets a relic for its head and one to three for its members, all pledged. Temples founded later get none, and on a new game there are often no temples yet when this happens. Four more go outside the Order: two to AI rulers of learning 12 or more (landless adventurers included) and two to AI courtiers of learning 14 or more. A Search for Magical Artifacts has a 10% chance each month of turning one up ( A Lesser Thing ), once a search. The rest move by war, theft, Zecchia and hunters. Powder is never seeded, and the Seal is never handed out at random. The reliquary # A temple's or coven's reliquary is everything its members have pledged to it. Pledge to the Reliquary one of your own relics or magical artifacts (not a hide, a page, the book or the Seal); a member of both a temple and a coven chooses which. The item stays yours, and while it is pledged it cannot be taken in a siege or a raid. War, Zecchia and a hunter's evidence can still take it. Take It Back unpledges it. Every member gets The Reliquary (a temple) or The Coven's Reliquary : +1% monthly magic lifestyle experience for each point, at 2 points for a relic and 3 for a magical artifact. A temple's bonus stops at +30%, a coven's at +15%. Ask to Borrow lets a Magistratus borrow an item pledged to his own temple, once in five years; an AI lender weighs his opinion and the borrower's rank, and always obeys his own Temple Magus. A loan lasts three years, the lender keeps a claim, and it comes home early if the borrower dies, is cast out

docs.x: A brass ring cut with the seal of the king who bound demons. It is a holy relic to every Abrahamic faith, and starts enshrined in Jerusalem if an Abrahamic ruler holds it and the shrine has room, else at another Abrahamic holy site that fits, else in the treasury of the greatest Abrahamic AI ruler, else it is lost for 10, 20 or 30 years. Its county carries The Seal of Solomon Is Kept Here (+2 county opinion). A Seal that is destroyed is never made again. Worn, it stops magical domination. Zecchia cannot be sent after its wearer or rob him, and a wearer who knows her name can summon her without being a Mage or spending power. The Order's master, wearing it, can make a demon kneel. It cannot be pledged, and Zecchia never takes it. To take it from its shrine: hold the county; or, as a Mage or someone who knows where it is, finish a siege of that county ( The Ring Beneath the Altar ); or go there on pilgrimage knowing it is there ( The Ring at the Shrine : an intrigue roll, 3 for each point plus 10, between 10 and 80; caught, the county's lord thinks 30 less of you). The Necrophone, Zecchia and the book can each tell you where it is.

docs.x: A new casus belli. A landed Mage, Order member or coven member (not a landless adventurer) can declare it on anyone holding at least three magical items that can move: magical artifacts, relics, pages, or the book while no Contract runs. Hides never count. A player may declare at any distance; the AI only against neighbours, and only when it is a greedy or ambitious Mage. Victory takes every relic and magical item the defender owns, pledged or not, and leaves him a claim on each. A white peace costs the attacker a little prestige. Defeat costs him gold and prestige, but nobody loses a claim over it. Witchcraft's Demonic Invasion and War Against the Witch now take relics and pages too.

docs.x: There are 26 rules across 96 settings , in two tabs: fifteen under Supernatural and eleven under Witchcraft . None of the Supernatural settings blocks achievements; seven Witchcraft ones do. These are the fifteen Supernatural rules. In game each name starts with "Supernatural:", as in Supernatural: Embrace Decisions . Rule Default Why you might change it Embrace Decisions Off Turn it on and you get the eight decisions that let you become, or stop being, a vampire, werewolf, hybrid or hunter at will. With it off there is no cure for anything. Trait Distribution Counts and below Sets the highest rank of AI adult that can be rolled into a vampire, werewolf or hunter. The roll runs at game start and again every year. On allows every rank; Off stops the rolls, which leaves the eight Mikaelsons, six of them creatures. Confer Death On Seven settings from Off through NPC Only to More Death. It governs the two hybrid turnings only. It does not reach the vampire embrace, the werewolf wound or hunter training. AI Confer On Whether AI creatures turn and train other people, and which kinds are allowed to. Set it to Off for a world where you are the only one spreading anything. Inheritance/Pregnancy Werewolf Trait Only Eight settings covering who can have children with whom and what comes out. One setting is labelled Skip this Setting and means it. Demon Inheritance/Pregnancy On Separate from the above, with four settings. Off is the original behaviour, where demon pregnancies were always lost. Events On Four settings. You can have embrace events only, everything except embrace events, or none. Paleness Vampires Whether turning lightens your skin, and whether that applies to hybrids too. How a vampire looks. Ageing Stops at portrait maturity How an immortal's portrait behaves over centuries. Visual Changes Off Turns on five cosmetic right-click options. Off by default, so most players never see them. Reset Lifetime Events Every 50 years Lets once-per-lifetime event chains come round again for immortals, who otherwise exhaust them. The Six Hides Scattered Off, Lost, Scattered or Awakened: whether the hides exist at all, and whether they start in shrines, on werewolves or lost. Detail. Packs On Off removes packs and everything between them. The Werewolf Gathering still runs, and wolves can still Challenge each other. The Blue Rose On Off means no temple of the Order is ever founded, and the Gnostic Council works as Witchcraft ships it. Relics, covens, Zecchia and the Seal of Solomon remain. Detail. The Vade Maecum Infernal Scattered Off, Scattered or Lost: whether the book's pages exist, and whether three start in treasuries or lost. Under Scattered and Lost the fourth is in Silverback's hide. Detail. These are the eleven Witchcraft rules. In game each name starts with "Witchcraft:". Rule Default Settings, and which block achievements Be a Witch Default (No) Yes, or Yes, with a source! The last blocks achievements. Scheme Adjustment Adjusted Adjusted or No Adjustment Magical Artifacts Random Distribution Random, Player's Area, or Guaranteed for the player, which blocks achievements Witch Hunters Activity Low Low, Normal or High. At Low the Grand Coalition crisis never starts. Bael (Demon) Can appear Cannot appear blocks achievements Return of the Grand Magus Can appear Cannot appear does not block achievements Ending crises At any time Delay 50, 100, 150 or 200 years, or Never, which blocks achievements. "At any time" still waits ten years. Range of spells Limited Unlimited blocks achievements. Limited means some spells need physical contact and a nearby target. Number of Mages Decreased Minimal, Decreased, Normal, Increased or Many Arena Mode Disabled Enabled blocks achievements Demonic Aggression Normal Low blocks achievements

docs.x: Ninety-seven decisions and 102 character interactions. Three of the interactions replace base-game ones, and since 2.38 so does the coven-founding decision. Almost none of it costs money. The currency in this mod is cooldowns, risk and exposure. Embrace, abandon and feeding Supernatural's own decisions, 52 in all with the hide, pack, Order, coven, relic and book ones, sit in their own group in the decisions panel, Supernatural Decisions . Eleven are older than the hides. Eight of those are a way in and a way out for each of four kinds, and all eight need the Supernatural: Embrace Decisions rule set to On. The AI can never take any of them. Kind The way in The way out Vampire Embrace Vampirism Abandon Vampirism Werewolf Embrace Lycanthropy Abandon Lycanthropy Hybrid Become a Hybrid Abandon Being a Hybrid Hunter Become a Hunter Abandon Being a Hunter The other three are the feeding decisions: Decision Who Your cooldown What it does Satiate Thirst Vampire 7 years Three days later, the feeding chain Satiate Hunger Werewolf 5 years Three days later, the hunger chain Satiate Hunger/Thirst Hybrid 7 years A coin flip between the two None of them costs anything. An AI creature runs on its own fourteen-year cadence rather than your cooldown. These were broken in instructive ways. The vampire decision was entirely commented out before 2.32, so pure vampires had no feeding decision at all, and the familiar coin-flip belonged to the hybrid. All three then had their AI check interval set to zero, which means the AI never looks at a decision: twelve years of a fresh campaign with about ninety-six vampires in it produced zero feeds and zero trails . Hides and packs Eleven decisions and seven interactions belong to the hides and the packs. The detail is in The Six Hides and Packs . Decision Who Cooldown What it does Let the Wolf Run / Hold the Wolf Back Any Champion None Whether his hide fights in your battles Vanish Timber's Champion 10 years The trail he left on the county he is standing in goes cold, if no hunt is running there Hold the Line Graybeard's Champion 5 years +10 advantage and −50% retreat losses for a year Let It Take Me Midnight's Champion, at war, with the wolf let run 3 years Twice the kills in his next battle, and major stress after it Call the Packs Alpha's Champion, no Gathering in the last five years 10 years For a year, every alpha in reach can be invited to your Gathering, and each who comes owes you a favour if it ends within that year Send for a Hide A wolf who knows where a hide is kept One errand at a time Pays someone to fetch it, about six months of your income Take the Hide from the Shrine AI werewolf lords only None What a player does from the holy site Found a Pack A wolf at Pack Standing 50 (40 born a wolf, or with Pack Leader), or any Champion None 50 prestige; you are the alpha Leave the Pack / Disband the Pack A member / the alpha None Leaving costs standing; disbanding costs nobody anything The interactions are Silverback's Stand Over Them , Tundra's Read Them (one secret of someone in reach, every five years), Ask to Unbind the Hide , and the four between wolves: Invite to the Pack , Challenge , Ask to Run With Their Pack and Lure Away . docs.x: Supernatural's own decisions, 52 in all with the hide, pack, Order, coven, relic and book ones, sit in their own group in the decisions panel, Supernatural Decisions . Eleven are older than the hides. Eight of those are a way in and a way out for each of four kinds, and all eight need the Supernatural: Embrace Decisions rule set to On. The AI can never take any of them. Kind The way in The way out Vampire Embrace Vampirism Abandon Vampirism Werewolf Embrace Lycanthropy Abandon Lycanthropy Hybrid Become a Hybrid Abandon Being a Hybrid Hunter Become a Hunter Abandon Being a Hunter The other three are the feeding decisions: Decision Who Your cooldown What it does Satiate Thirst Vampire 7 years Three days later, the feeding chain Satiate Hunger Werewolf 5 years Three days later, the hunger chain Satiate Hunger/Thirst Hybrid 7 years A coin flip between the two None of them costs anything. An AI creature runs on its own fourteen-year cadence rather than your cooldown. These were broken in instructive ways. The vampire decision was entirely commented out before 2.32, so pure vampires had no feeding decision at all, and the familiar coin-flip belonged to the hybrid. All three then had their AI check interval set to zero, which means the AI never looks at a decision: twelve years of a fresh campaign with about ninety-six vampires in it produced zero feeds and zero trails .

docs.x: Things in 2.38 that do not work the way the game's own text suggests. Each is described where it belongs; this is the list. The Beastbane cannot be earned. A hunter records only his first kill, so his name stops at the first rung. The same limit caps the reputation term on the tracking bar at +3. Names the world uses. "The Timeless" is a nickname with no text, and nothing grants it. Two regiment counters are inert. Bats against werewolves and Werewolves against vampires do nothing. Regiments. Confer Death does not cover the werewolf wound, the vampire embrace or hunter training, although its description says "turned, or trained". The bite. There are no fangs, and the "Supernatural: Visual Fangs" rule that the text files describe does not exist. How a vampire looks. The in-game notes for 2.35 mention dogs and "Hunter Academies". There is no dog kit, and the perk is Hunter Academy. 2.35. Russian players see raw keys for the hunt, 2.36, 2.37 and 2.38. Languages. The AI never shapeshifts. Shifting. The Blue Rose rule promises six temples at the start. Temples are seated around AI Mages, and Witchcraft makes none at the start of a game, so they usually appear at most one a year. Temples. Respondeo's ten-year wait starts even if you choose Not now . What members can do. A coven whose panel ends for lack of witches keeps its house modifier, and its panel never comes back. Covens. The Echo Pendant does not send a curse back , as its text says. It blocks ordinary curses and nothing more. Relics. A page a Champion chose to guard can still be found by the Necrophone, a golem, Magic Triangulation's answer and the book's voices. Finding the pages. With The Six Hides rule off, the Vade Maecum can never be bound, because its fourth page lives in Silverback's hide. The pages. A man Bound to the Book may be out of a hunter's reach. As the files read, a hunt corners only vampires, werewolves, hybrids and demons, so a bound master who is only a Mage may leave the Unmaking as the only designed way to kill him, short of taking him prisoner and executing him. The Bound to the Book text also says a Champion can kill him; nothing gives a Champion a way to. This has not been confirmed in game. Bound to the Book. Zecchia asks for "a hundred gold for each thing now" , but takes her whole fee at delivery. Zecchia. From the Witchcraft layer, which Supernatural carries as its author wrote it: Magical Experiments removes the Mage trait from anyone who already had it from an event. The magic trees. A False Mage can still take Warlock or True Witch. The one-capstone rule looks for a true Mage, so a pretender is not stopped. The magic trees. Lifestealer gives a True Witch nothing but its tooltip. Black Magic perks. The Magic Triangulation perk does not unlock triangulation. The decision needs the Mage or Warlock perk and a tower. Arcane perks. Cheat Death is out of reach for a Necromancer, though its requirement names one: the project is only offered to characters who are not. Projects. The Mage's Spire does not count as a tower for Magic Triangulation, where the Study and Laboratory below it do. Magic buildings. The Warlock trait's own Demonology and Power Saturation tracks never fill. The trait shows rewards on them, but nothing adds experience to either. The Mage Summit's Extraordinary security costs 300 gold and does nothing. Mage Summit. The expedition planner is looser than the rule. Once you know one destination, it can offer any place of power, including one you have already visited. Expeditions.

docs.x: Supernatural runs on the base game and needs nothing else. The compatibility questions that matter come from what it replaces. The mods you must not run beside it are listed under Install and load order , with the load order . What it replaces CK3 resolves mod files by path, last loaded wins. A mod file sitting at the same path as a base-game file replaces that file entirely . Anything the vanilla copy defined and the replacement does not is simply gone. Most of Supernatural is new filenames, which collide with nothing. The exceptions are the places it deliberately steps on vanilla: the birth on-actions, the death on-actions, by key, the base game's Found Witch Coven decision, several character interactions including disinheritance, some scripted relations, travel options, a handful of secret effects, and a set of portrait and accessory gene files. The mod ships its own list of these. Two mods that both replace the same vanilla file are mutually exclusive in practice. That, rather than anything specific to witches, is why Witchcraft and V&L cannot sit beside this one. Mid-save Adding it to a running campaign works, and every past release has been safe to add to a save. It is built for it in places: existing saves get a one-time repair pass for secrets nobody was told about, creatures that predate the disease-immunity flag are retro-fitted on a yearly pulse, characters stuck mid-transition are released, and the hunt's availability check is written to fail open on a continued save rather than grey the activity out forever. Two things do not carry over. Game rules are chosen when a save is created , so a campaign started without Supernatural has no values for its twenty-six rules. The ones added in 2.37 and 2.38 are read so that a save from before them gets their defaults: the hides scattered, packs on, the Order on and the Vade Maecum scattered. On such a save the Order seats its temples, and the relics, the Seal of Solomon and the pages are placed within the first year. And the mod adds portrait and accessory genes, which is the usual CK3 hazard around adding or removing a mod mid-save. Removing it from a save is not supported and there is no uninstall path. Most of what strands is mod-created and disappears with the mod. The exception worth knowing: the mod sets its four creature doctrines on every rite in the save, at game start, whenever a rite is created and once a year, and those are vanilla rite objects that persist. Nothing takes them off again. Multiplayer Every player needs the same mods at the same positions. The mod honours CK3's own multiplayer murder-scheme protections in its own scheme, and carries no other multiplayer-specific code.

The launcher does not show the mod after a manual install. Check that both supernatural_mod.mod and the supernatural_mod folder are in the CK3 mod folder, and that the .mod file's path= line is not pointing at a folder on another machine. Install and load order has the detail. Where are the decisions to become a vampire or a werewolf? Behind a game rule that is off by default. Supernatural: Embrace Decisions ships as "Default (Off)". It gates eight decisions: four to become a vampire, werewolf, hybrid or hunter, and four to stop being one, three of which are the cures. Turn it on at game setup if you want to pick what you are. The eight decisions by name. Why is there no temple of the Order in my game? The Order seats its temples around AI Mages, and Witchcraft makes none at the start of a game. Until a Mage appears, there is nobody to seat. Once there is, the Order founds at most one temple a year until six stand, so on a new campaign expect them over the first years. With no temple anywhere, a landed Mage who knows two others can use Found the Order Anew . Check also that Supernatural: The Blue Rose is on. Temples. Why can I not start Magical Research? It needs a true Mage, meaning the trait without the False Mage secret, an adult, holding at least a county, off its ten-year cooldown (five as the Gnostic Council's Keeper of the Reliquary). A Research Expedition also needs a place of power you know about and have not visited. Magical Research. The Arcane focus is greyed out. What am I missing? docs.x: The mod shows its own changelog once per save, at game start or on the next 1 January after an update. This is what it says, condensed. 2.38 — The Hermetic Order of the Blue Rose The Hermetic Order of the Blue Rose comes to Supernatural: temples of Mages that send a note and a blue rose to the people they want, and teach magic to the ones who pass. Members rise from Acolyte to Temple Magus, keep their temple's way of Silence, Subservience or Observance, work toward the Order's Prerogative, and meet in masks at the Conclave, which elects the Grand Magus of the Gnostic Council . Seven lesser relics and the Seal of Solomon join the game; most can be pledged to a temple's or coven's reliquary and lent out, and Seize Their Relics is a war for a rival's hoard. The Vade Maecum Infernal is four scattered pages, one inside Silverback's hide. Zecchia , a demon thief, answers some summonings. Covens have their own panel, can be founded with three witches, and can bring their Mages into the Order. Friendly spells and the council's interactions now sit in the Supernatural menu. Two new game rules turn the Order and the Vade Maecum on or off. Balance: one capstone each, Mage, Warlock or True Witch; the AI's nature weighs on its magic path and on necromancy; Witchcraft's magical artifacts can reach courtiers and landless adventurers; the werewolf and hybrid traits give less Martial, and the werewolf's ranks are Fledgling Werewolf, Werewolf, Seasoned Werewolf, Dread Werewolf and Elder Werewolf; hide Champions who practise magic regain power every year; packs invite lone wolves they know, and a second wolf at court lowers the bar for founding a pack to Pack Standing 25; True Witches appear again beside the Order's Mages. Fixes: healing no longer takes away the Horned God's Claws ; renouncing necromancy takes away the right to raise Skeleton Warriors; Demand Submission converts its target properly; Shadow Step out of prison runs the base game's escape; a soul-sold character's death pays the cyrograph's owner; creature lifestyle experience shows in tooltips; thousands of script errors are gone. 2.37 — The Six Hides Six ancient wolf hides are loose in the world: Silverback, Timber, Tundra, Graybeard, Midnight and Alpha. Each chooses a werewolf or hybrid who fits it, and its Champion is stronger, lives longer, never grows frail and hears magic. Most start as relics in shrines at holy sites; take one by holding the county, by siege or on pilgrimage, or pay someone to fetch it with Send for a Hide. Wolves can found and join packs, rise in Pack Standing, Challenge the alpha, and meet at the new Werewolf Gathering. AI wolves challenge an alpha only for a reason: he is too weak to lead, cruel to his pack, or their enemy. A hide an AI leaves idle for ten years slips away to find a wolf. Two new game rules control the hides and the packs. It works on a running save: the hides turn up at the next new year. Fixes: the mod's death reasons read as proper sentences; the death of a vampire who refused to feed no longer shows an error; They Stopped Coming has its icon; a broken link in Invoke the Bond is fixed; he, she and his are capitalised at the start of a sentence; a demon can have a child with a werewolf or hybrid. 2.36 — Crusader Kings III 1.20 Updated for CK3 1.20, which rebuilt religion around rites. On 1.20, 2.35a crashed as a new game loaded in; 2.36 fixes that. The vampirism, lycanthropy, hybrid and hunter doctrines belong to rites now, so every rite of a faith has them and new rites get them too, and crimes, shunning and the witch war follow the rite. Known vampires, werewolves, hybrids and hunters are sins under a rite that outlaws their kind and virtues under one that reveres it, the way 1.20 treats witches. Your own rite judges your feeding, killing

docs.s: 2.38 — The Hermetic Order of the Blue Rose
docs.x: The Hermetic Order of the Blue Rose comes to Supernatural: temples of Mages that send a note and a blue rose to the people they want, and teach magic to the ones who pass. Members rise from Acolyte to Temple Magus, keep their temple's way of Silence, Subservience or Observance, work toward the Order's Prerogative, and meet in masks at the Conclave, which elects the Grand Magus of the Gnostic Council . Seven lesser relics and the Seal of Solomon join the game; most can be pledged to a temple's or coven's reliquary and lent out, and Seize Their Relics is a war for a rival's hoard. The Vade Maecum Infernal is four scattered pages, one inside Silverback's hide. Zecchia , a demon thief, answers some summonings. Covens have their own panel, can be founded with three witches, and can bring their Mages into the Order. Friendly spells and the council's interactions now sit in the Supernatural menu. Two new game rules turn the Order and the Vade Maecum on or off. Balance: one capstone each, Mage, Warlock or True Witch; the AI's nature weighs on its magic path and on necromancy; Witchcraft's magical artifacts can reach courtiers and landless adventurers; the werewolf and hybrid traits give less Martial, and the werewolf's ranks are Fledgling Werewolf, Werewolf, Seasoned Werewolf, Dread Werewolf and Elder Werewolf; hide Champions who practise magic regain power every year; packs invite lone wolves they know, and a second wolf at court lowers the bar for founding a pack to Pack Standing 25; True Witches appear again beside the Order's Mages. Fixes: healing no longer takes away the Horned God's Claws ; renouncing necromancy takes away the right to raise Skeleton Warriors; Demand Submission converts its target properly; Shadow Step out of prison runs the base game's escape; a soul-sold character's death pays the cyrograph's owner; creature lifestyle experience shows in tooltips; thousands of script errors are gone.

docs.t: Supernatural CK3 Mod Wiki: Vampires, Werewolves and the Hunt
docs.x: Six ancient wolf hides are loose in the world: Silverback, Timber, Tundra, Graybeard, Midnight and Alpha. Each chooses a werewolf or hybrid who fits it, and its Champion is stronger, lives longer, never grows frail and hears magic. Most start as relics in shrines at holy sites; take one by holding the county, by siege or on pilgrimage, or pay someone to fetch it with Send for a Hide. Wolves can found and join packs, rise in Pack Standing, Challenge the alpha, and meet at the new Werewolf Gathering. AI wolves challenge an alpha only for a reason: he is too weak to lead, cruel to his pack, or their enemy. A hide an AI leaves idle for ten years slips away to find a wolf. Two new game rules control the hides and the packs. It works on a running save: the hides turn up at the next new year. Fixes: the mod's death reasons read as proper sentences; the death of a vampire who refused to feed no longer shows an error; They Stopped Coming has its icon; a broken link in Invoke the Bond is fixed; he, she and his are capitalised at the start of a sentence; a demon can have a child with a werewolf or hybrid.

docs.t: Supernatural CK3 Mod Wiki: Vampires, Werewolves and the Hunt
docs.x: Updated for CK3 1.20, which rebuilt religion around rites. On 1.20, 2.35a crashed as a new game loaded in; 2.36 fixes that. The vampirism, lycanthropy, hybrid and hunter doctrines belong to rites now, so every rite of a faith has them and new rites get them too, and crimes, shunning and the witch war follow the rite. Known vampires, werewolves, hybrids and hunters are sins under a rite that outlaws their kind and virtues under one that reveres it, the way 1.20 treats witches. Your own rite judges your feeding, killing and turning others through Spiritual Fulfillment, but only condemns them once you are known; the zealous feel it more and a cynic is never charged. A feed only leaves a trail when somebody talks. The Seekers camp purpose works again, and Scholar is Erudite in 1.20 and keeps the magic bonus. Fixes: the first warning that a county remembers you no longer mentions a body when there wasn't one; feeding events no longer flood the error log; the Mikaelsons no longer log hundreds of portrait errors at load; French, German, Spanish, Korean, Polish and Chinese players see English rather than raw keys for everything since the hunt. If you play with A Game of Thrones, AGOT has not been updated for 1.20 yet, and the compatibility patch follows AGOT's update.

docs.t: Supernatural CK3 Mod Wiki: Vampires, Werewolves and the Hunt
docs.x: Fixes for The Hunt, safe on a running save. Turning down a witch hunt no longer kills the witch, so witches married into other courts stop vanishing. The witch and monster sightings are fast for hunters only and back to their old rate for everyone else, which stops the world filling with new hunters and werewolves. Monster Sighting now has the same conditions as its twin, so it no longer reaches someone imprisoned, incapable, travelling or busy with an activity. An ordinary murder no longer reads as a creature's kill unless the killer was there; a murder in your own hall still can. Characters already in House Hellion stay there.

docs.t: Supernatural CK3 Mod Wiki: Vampires, Werewolves and the Hunt
docs.x: A new activity: ride out and hunt what is killing people. Kills and prowling leave trails on the counties they happen in, and trails escalate: three incidents and the lord hears about it. He can look into it himself, set his spymaster on it, post a bounty, or send for a named hunter and pay him when it is done. A new court position, the Trailsman, reads the countryside. You can hunt a creature or hunt a witch, each with their own trails and beats. Bring silver, stakes, dogs or men, and the door goes differently. Take an apprentice along and he graduates in the field. These notes follow the mod's in-game text, which has two slips: there is no dog kit, and the perk is Hunter Academy. Of the creature's answers below, "compel him" is Look them in the eye . The creature gets the other half of the scene, and real answers: stand and fight, go to ground, compel him, send your progeny, let the wolf out, or talk him onto somebody worse. Get away and you can warn your sire and your get, or sell them. Demons argue instead of running, and may offer a bargain. Hunters and creatures earn names the world starts using. A county that turns three hunters away stops attracting any. You can cover your own kills: pay it off, frame someone, or hide the body. Compel a whole town and the holes start to line up. Hunters ride at bad odds far less often, and can turn back. Fixes: witch hunts were impossible to reach and now work; two files never loaded, so no trail was ever written; the hunter migration layer never ran; hunters are told about witches and monsters far more often; secret witches leave trails, not only openly known ones; compelling someone for their secrets no longer errors; thousands of script errors a session removed; hunter regiments now need the Hunter Academies perk.

docs.t: Supernatural CK3 Mod Wiki: Vampires, Werewolves and the Hunt
docs.x: Version What it was 2.34a Your spymaster stops finding secrets you already know; makers, sires, trainers and parents know what they made; existing saves repaired once on load. 2.34 — the blood remembers who Turnings are remembered and name your maker. Six one-off events grow out of those memories. A maxed vampire can compel a hunter to go home. True Witch Hunter and True Monster Hunter capstones. Vampires can feed on tribal holdings. 2.33 — the blood remembers Fall in battle with vampire blood in you and rise. Weeks of hunger, then feed or refuse for good. Whoever gave you the blood becomes your maker. Works landed or landless, and needs no patch. 2.32 Feed in foreign cities. Vampires get their Satiate Thirst decision back. Two new vampire branches and two new werewolf branches. Surviving a hunter makes you stronger. Werewolves are named by tier, like vampires. 2.31c Dragons, wights, Others and the Night King can no longer be turned, compelled or cursed. 130 spell tooltips showed a raw key. The eight Originals use AGOT's current portrait genes. 2.31a A werewolf bite festers one to three years first. A quarter of NPC werewolves were spawning as vampires. Demon-blooded children grow into demons in their twenties.

docs.t: Download The Long Night & Azor Ahai — CK3 mod without Steam
docs.x: Manual install Download without Steam The mod is plain files, so it runs on any copy of Crusader Kings III: GOG, Epic, Game Pass, wherever you bought it. It takes about five minutes by hand, and this page walks the whole thing. Home › Mods › The Long Night › Download If your CK3 is on Steam, use the Workshop instead It's one click, it updates itself the moment I push a fix, and it handles the load order for you. Nothing on this page is better; it exists for people who can't use the Workshop at all. Subscribe on the Steam Workshop → Step zero Get the files The mod is open source. The repository is the download, with no mirror, no shortener and no waiting. Download from GitHub Browse the source current release on GitHub CK3 1.19.0.6 requires A Game of Thrones mid-save safe On the newest release, take the file named AGOT-The-Long-Night-and-Azor-Ahai- version .zip under Assets (the version number matches the release). It is about 25 MB and holds exactly the mod and nothing else. The two Source code entries below it are the whole repository, which is a much larger download you don't need. On CK3 1.20? A Game of Thrones has not been updated for 1.20 yet, so this mod needs the game on 1.19.0.6 until it is. How to stay on 1.19. Five minutes Installing it by hand Unzip it The archive unpacks straight to a single folder, the-long-night-azor-ahai , containing common , events , gfx , localization and a descriptor.mod . There's no outer wrapper folder to dig through. That folder is the whole mod. A few workshop_changelog text files sit inside it as well. They are notes from past updates; the game ignores them, so leave them be. What the archive does not include is the second file the launcher needs: a the-long-night-azor-ahai.mod that sits beside the folder rather than inside it. You'll make that in step 3, and it's a copy-paste. Move both into your CK3 mod directory The folder and the .mod file go here together, and the .mod file sits next to the folder, never inside it: Windows Documents\Paradox Interactive\Crusader Kings III\mod\ macOS ~/Documents/Paradox Interactive/Crusader Kings III/mod/ Linux ~/.local/share/Paradox Interactive/Crusader Kings III/mod/ If there's no mod folder there yet, launch CK3 once and close it, or create the folder yourself. Make the .mod file (don't skip this one) This is the step that decides whether any of the rest works, and it is not optional . The launcher does not read the descriptor.mod inside the mod folder. It reads a separate the-long-night-azor-ahai.mod file sitting in the mod directory next to the folder, and that one isn't in the archive, because it has to describe where the mod lives on your machine. So make it. In your mod folder, create a new plain text file named the-long-night-azor-ahai.mod , open it in any editor (Notepad is fine) and paste this in: copy version="1.1.3" picture="thumbnail.png" tags={ "Events" "Warfare" "Historical" "Religion" "Culture" "Gameplay" } name="AGOT: The Long Night & Azor Ahai" supported_version="1.19.0.6" path="mod/the-long-night-azor-ahai" Two details matter here. path= is relative : it says "the the-long-night-azor-ahai folder inside mod ", which is true on every machine, so use it exactly as written rather than typing a full C:\ path. And the remote_file_id line is left out by design: that line tells the launcher "this is a Steam Workshop item", which is exactly what your copy isn't, and leaving it in is a good way to have the launcher ignore your folder or replace it. If you took a Source code archive instead of the built one, it does contain a the-long-night-azor-ahai.mod , but it's the copy from my machine, with my folder path baked into it. Overwrite its contents with the block above and it'll behave. Make sure your text editor saves it as .mod and not .mod.txt . On Windows you may need to turn on file extensions to see the difference. Enable it and set the load order Open the Paradox launcher, go to All installed mods , and the mod should be listed. Add it to a playset, then order it like this: A Game of Thrones (required, and it also needs a manual install if you're not on Steam) AGOT submods: AGOT+, Valyrian Steel, Submod Core, Nobility… AGOT: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Optional: Supernatural If you run Supernatural: the Compatibility Patch, always last Before you start a game The one rule Disable every other Long Night mod AGOT: The Long Night and The Long Night+ must be unchecked in your playset . Sorting them below this one is not enough; they have to be disabled . This mod is a fork of both and ships files at the same paths, so either one loaded anywhere overrides it with older code and brings back the see-through dragon bug. If you installed those manually too, the surest fix is to delete their folders and their .mod files outright. When it goes wrong Troubleshooting "Descriptor file error" The path= line is wrong. It's the cause almost every time. Use forward slashes , never backslashes, even on Windows. The path must match your folder name exactly, including case. If the relative path won't take, use the full one instead: path="C:/Users/YourName/Documents/Paradox Interactive/Crusader Kings III/mod/the-long-night-azor-ahai" It doesn't appear at all Check the file is .mod , not .mod.txt . Check it's in the mod folder itself, not inside the mod's own folder. Check you removed the remote_file_id line. With it left in, the launcher may look for a Workshop copy instead of yours. Restart the launcher fully; it scans on start. Confirm the folder itself contains common and events , not another folder that contains them. If you're still stuck, the Long Night Discord is the fastest place to get it sorted; manual-install questions get answered there daily. Common questions Manual install FAQ Do I still need A Game of Thrones? Yes, always. This is a submod: it adds the Long Night endgame to AGOT rather than replacing it. If you're not on Steam you'll need to install AGOT manually as well, the same way, and load it above this mod. Will it update itself? No. A manual install is a snapshot of one version. When I push an update you'll want to delete the old mod folder, unzip the new one in its place, and change the version= line in your .mod file to match. Watching the repository or joining the Discord is the easiest way to know when that happens. Is this the same build as the Workshop version? It's the same source the Workshop build is cut from, and the repository is where updates land first. The one thing worth doing is checking the version number in the Paradox launcher against the version on the Workshop page . That matters in multiplayer, where everyone has to be on the same version or the game refuses to start. Which file do I take on the releases page? The one named AGOT-The-Long-Night-and-Azor-Ahai- followed by the version number. That's the built archive, around 25 MB and only the mod. The two Source code entries underneath are the entire repository including development files; they work, but they're a far bigger download for the same mod. Can I use it with an existing save? Yes, it's mid-save safe to add and to update. The one caveat is that CK3 bakes game rules in when a save is created, so an existing campaign keeps whatever rules it started with. Where's the source? The repository is public , so you can read every file, open an issue, or fork it. It's built on the work of others and it seemed only right to pass that along the same way. Does the mod work on Mac and Linux? It's script and assets rather than compiled code, so yes. Only the folder location differs, and both paths are in step 2. Standing on other people's work. This mod is a fork built on Freeholder 's original Long Night, Tehaen 's 1.19 update, and Wepo94 's The Long Night+, and on the AGOT team's total conversion underneath all of it. If you enjoy this, that's where it started. While you're here What the mod does If you landed here for the download and haven't seen it, the full breakdown is worth a look : the wights with their own realms, the playable Night's Watch, the Azor Ahai prophecy, and a riddle at the bottom for anyone who reads to the end. If you run Supernatural as well, it has its own manual install guide now, and the compatibility patch still goes last.

docs.t: AGOT: The Long Night & Azor Ahai — a CK3 Game of Thrones mod
docs.x: A CK3 mod for A Game of Thrones The Long Night & Azor Ahai "There is only one war that matters. The Great War. And it is here." Eight seasons promised us the Long Night. We got one dark episode and a knife. The best version of that story is still unwritten, and a game where you play a lord in Westeros is a very good place to write it. Subscribe on Steam Workshop Read the wiki Download without Steam Join the Discord Version 1.1.3 Updated 28 September 2026 Requires A Game of Thrones CK3 1.19.0.6 English, Russian, Spanish & French Mid-save safe Home › Mods › The Long Night & Azor Ahai 14,200+ current subscribers 27,400+ unique visitors 700+ favorites 4 phases, across a century 33,400+ views on the showcase Latest update · from the Steam change notes 1.1.3 — The Player Reports 28 September 2026 Everything you reported on the Workshop and the Discord this month, traced and fixed. Safe to add to a running game. An existing save repairs itself, most of it within a month and the rest within a year. Every change note on Steam → The showcase Watch it play out first The whole mod in one video: the invasion, the Watch, the prophecy, and what the map looks like when it's over. The Long Night & Azor Ahai — Full CK3 AGOT Mod Showcase. Plays here, or watch it on YouTube . The mod in full What this is, start to finish The Long Night & Azor Ahai is a submod for A Game of Thrones , the Crusader Kings III total conversion, and it does one thing: it builds the Long Night out into the endgame the setting always pointed at. It is free, it lives on the Steam Workshop, and it has shipped thirty-one updates since 8 August 2026, most of them built from what players reported in the Discord and the comments. The current version is 1.1.1. The invasion is a struggle in four phases that you can watch coming for decades. When it arrives, the Night King is a character with a court, a culture, a faith and a realm of his own, and every lord he beats gets back up wearing his own face, keeping his own title and answering to a new liege. Dragons that die over his ground come back on his side. The Wall comes down at Castle Black with the camera on it. His host grows with what he takes: twenty thousand beyond the Wall, fifty once the far north is his, a hundred thousand when the Wall falls, two hundred thousand when the North does, scaled by the difficulty you chose and capped at half a million, the population of King's Landing. The living have a lot to do about it. You can take the black and mean it: lay down your lands, hand the realm to your heir, and hold one of the Wall's castles or ride with one of eight ranging companies as a landless captain. As Lord Commander you can call a Great Ranging and pay two hundred brothers for the answer, or send a sworn brother down the length of Westeros asking every lord how full his dungeons are. Southern lords can send men and grain north, empty their cells onto the Wall in one order, mine dragonglass, bring a red priest into the hall, and ask him for the one blessing a priest can give once in his life. Since 1.1.0 the fight with the Night King is no longer a dice roll. Reaching him opens the Last Hour, a Trial-of-Seven melee in the snow: you and the people who were there with you against him and his White Walkers, blow by blow. Castle steel does not bite. Lightbringer, Valyrian steel and dragonglass each open their own way through the fight, and kin can take the blow meant for you. Only a bane destroys him; ordinary steel casts him down and the dark crowns another. Lose, and he keeps you: your character is raised as one of his, and a later champion may find you standing on the wrong side of the line. Underneath all of it runs the prophecy. Every character in the world is measured against nine marks, continuously, and the AI competes for the naming as hard as you do. Red priests, witches and greenseers say the name out loud; Lightbringer can be forged at the price every version of the tale agrees on; and whether the one they named was ever the prince is decided behind the curtain and revealed once, at the end. Then comes the Dawn: a scoured North, the Question of the North, colonists and free folk filling the empty land, and a record of the men who were standing there when it ended. This page is the overview. The wiki is the complete reference, every mechanic with the numbers on one page; the Workshop page is the short version, and the GitHub wiki carries the full version history. Read this part Before you play: one rule Disable every other Long Night mod AGOT: The Long Night and The Long Night+ must be unchecked in your playset . Sorting them below this one is not enough; they have to be disabled . This mod grew out of both and ships files at the same paths. Either of them loaded anywhere in your list overrides this mod with older code and brings back the see-through dragon bug. This mod replaces both, so you can unsubscribe from them entirely. What you'll play The dead get back up This is an invasion with characters, politics and a body count you recognise, and the lords you lose come back as the enemy. A risen lord, with the same face, the same title and a new liege. An Other, ruling as a character in his own right. The Night King himself, with 288K men behind him. Wights are characters, not troops Every man you lose can rise wearing his own face. Wights keep their own portraits, their own titles and their own rot, and rule their own realms under the Night King. They raise what they kill Bring a dragon down over the Haunted Forest and it comes back with the same name and the same face, the wrong colour and the wrong rider. docs.t: AGOT: The Long Night & Azor Ahai — a CK3 Game of Thrones mod
docs.s: What this is, start to finish
docs.x: The mod in full The Long Night & Azor Ahai is a submod for A Game of Thrones , the Crusader Kings III total conversion, and it does one thing: it builds the Long Night out into the endgame the setting always pointed at. It is free, it lives on the Steam Workshop, and it has shipped thirty-one updates since 8 August 2026, most of them built from what players reported in the Discord and the comments. The current version is 1.1.1. The invasion is a struggle in four phases that you can watch coming for decades. When it arrives, the Night King is a character with a court, a culture, a faith and a realm of his own, and every lord he beats gets back up wearing his own face, keeping his own title and answering to a new liege. Dragons that die over his ground come back on his side. The Wall comes down at Castle Black with the camera on it. His host grows with what he takes: twenty thousand beyond the Wall, fifty once the far north is his, a hundred thousand when the Wall falls, two hundred thousand when the North does, scaled by the difficulty you chose and capped at half a million, the population of King's Landing. The living have a lot to do about it. You can take the black and mean it: lay down your lands, hand the realm to your heir, and hold one of the Wall's castles or ride with one of eight ranging companies as a landless captain. As Lord Commander you can call a Great Ranging and pay two hundred brothers for the answer, or send a sworn brother down the length of Westeros asking every lord how full his dungeons are. Southern lords can send men and grain north, empty their cells onto the Wall in one order, mine dragonglass, bring a red priest into the hall, and ask him for the one blessing a priest can give once in his life. Since 1.1.0 the fight with the Night King is no longer a dice roll. Reaching him opens the Last Hour, a Trial-of-Seven melee in the snow: you and the people who were there with you against him and his White Walkers, blow by blow. Castle steel does not bite. Lightbringer, Valyrian steel and dragonglass each open their own way through the fight, and kin can take the blow meant for you. Only a bane destroys him; ordinary steel casts him down and the dark crowns another. Lose, and he keeps you: your character is raised as one of his, and a later champion may find you standing on the wrong side of the line. Underneath all of it runs the prophecy. Every character in the world is measured against nine marks, continuously, and the AI competes for the naming as hard as you do. Red priests, witches and greenseers say the name out loud; Lightbringer can be forged at the price every version of the tale agrees on; and whether the one they named was ever the prince is decided behind the curtain and revealed once, at the end. Then comes the Dawn: a scoured North, the Question of the North, colonists and free folk filling the empty land, and a record of the men who were standing there when it ended. This page is the overview. The wiki is the complete reference, every mechanic with the numbers on one page; the Workshop page is the short version, and the GitHub wiki carries the full version history.

docs.s: The invasion is a four-phase struggle
docs.x: The struggle Each phase changes what your counties produce and how close the dead are. Dead dragons, lost rangings and a hollowed-out Watch all move the tracker, so you can plan your preparations against something you can see. THE LONG SUMMER Peace, a +5% county modifier , and a counter you can see from day one. This is the window you get to spend. WINTER IS COMING −5% county modifier. Length is unknown, and your own losses shorten it. THE LONG NIGHT The invasion, at a −10% county modifier . Dragonglass in the cellars and men sent north is the whole difference between surviving it and being surprised by it. THE DAWN A ruined North to rebuild, and one crown-level choice that outlasts the war. The same tracker in the Long Summer, Winter Is Coming and the Long Night. The catalyst list underneath is what moved it. A quiet century still ends on schedule. A bad one ends early.

docs.t: AGOT: The Long Night & Azor Ahai — a CK3 Game of Thrones mod
docs.s: Azor Ahai has a whole system behind it
docs.x: The prophecy There is no Azor Ahai trait to tick in the ruler designer. Every character in the world is measured against the prophecy continuously, their standing moves as marks are earned and lost, and the AI is competing for it too. Nine marks, and you never need all nine Dragon dreams, and greensight Born in salt and smoke, or beneath a bleeding star Hidden blood: a Valyrian bastard raised inside a great house Walking among the dead and surviving it Carrying spellforged steel Waking dragons from stone Dying, and not staying dead Five are decided at birth and four are earned. Two of them are checked continuously: lose the sword or the dragon and the claim goes with it. Read the Signs tells you which you carry, and costs nothing. And the realm decides what it means Deeds need validating by a red priest, a witch or a greenseer, since an unwitnessed miracle counts for nothing Two deeds make you Favored of R'hllor ; four make you Chosen (a game rule can make it one and three, or three and six) Lightbringer can be forged, at the price every version of the tale agrees on The man who ends it is called the Prince That Was Promised , the Dawnbringer if he did it with a Lightbringer he forged, or, failing both, the Dawn Kill the Night King and you are Azor Ahai Reborn , marks or no marks The AI plays all of it; rival claimants meet, and sometimes ally Lightbringer, once it is finally out of the third quench. Whether the one they named was ever the prince is decided behind the curtain, and the world only finds out at the end. There are four ways that can land.

docs.x: After Surviving the invasion starts a second game: an emptied North, and decisions about it that stick for the rest of the campaign. The Question of the North Restore the Night's Watch, or open the Gift to the free folk. One choice, and it sticks for the rest of the game. By default a player in the North is asked before the AI crown. The land refills Wildling clans migrate into the empty North year by year. Landless survivors walk the Kingsroad home to rebuild their ancestral seats. Sell the ashes Sell colonisation rights to the Free Cities, and your northern vassals will remember that you did. When it ends, the game writes down who was standing there, and gets it right before the singers get it wrong.

docs.x: Your apocalypse, your rules The invasion: eight rules Chance : certain, near-certain, even odds, remote, or never Moment : a random summer, immediately, in fifty, one hundred or one hundred fifty years, historical, full random, or only when you say so Strength : weak, standard, strong or insane. Each tier sets the size of his host, his advantage, damage and toughness, how fast he re-arms between wars, and how much he takes per war War tier : duchy (a slow grind), march (recommended), or empire (a rapid onslaught) Resolution : his death ends it, or the War for the Dawn does His dragon : he raises what he kills (default), one appears on its own, or never The Iron Throne : whether it reforms afterward Recurrence : once, or The Cycle, in which the Wall is raised anew, the veterans of the first dawn are known by name, and the second night comes heavier than the first The prophecy, the Watch and the Dawn: six more Was there ever a prince? Let the flames decide (a hidden coin, tossed once at game start), there is a prince, or there is no prince and every naming is a priest reading his own hopes Naming : as the books have it (two marks to be Favored, four to be Chosen), the flames are loud (one and three), the Citadel's reading (three and six), or nobody is ever named Claimants : anyone at all, players only, or one Chosen at a time The ranging companies : the Watch fills them itself, leaves them for players, or all eight ride from day one Send the Prisoners : whether the Wall takes counts and below, or any rank The Question of the North : a player in the North is asked first (default), or the crown decides Rules are baked in when a save is created. Changing them means a new campaign.

docs.x: What's changed The newest first, each in a sentence or two. The complete notes for every release, with reporter credits, are on the Workshop change-notes page and in the GitHub wiki . 1.1.3 — The Player Reports There is one Night King. Cast down by anything but a bane, he rises again within days in the same face and name, and every player is told so; dragon battle events can no longer pick him out of the line. Every dead lord now serves him, and no living ruler can fight on his side. The invasion's stages wait only on land he can attack, and wars on the Watch and the Iron Throne need more than held ground. Fixed: the freeze when the dead reach the Wall, Take the Black breaking your council, a Valyrian goblet becoming Lightbringer, Send for a Red Priest ignoring the priest already in your hall, raw trigger text under decisions, free folk resettling as feudal, and dead courts filling with thousands of new characters a year. A new rule asks a player in the North the Question of the North first. 1.1.2 — The Cold Does Not Fall The Night King no longer dies by accident: the commander pool, a lost dragon duel and the melee's own engine could all kill him outside a scene. The Others are no longer handed to the Iron Throne after a mega-war, and the dead no longer turn up as guests in living courts. Spanish and French added, with every line in all four languages. 1.1.1 — The Watch Keeps No Land A sworn brother renounces any land he inherits outside the Wall, the Lord Commander included; the exemption was how the Watch ended up holding a random county in the North. The dead answer to nobody living. Stannis gets Melisandre when he sends for a priest, and the lord of Dragonstone usually does. The Others cannot run schemes. Every county the dead take is set to full control so their own peasants never rise against them, and their land recovers control after a siege instead of never, which also stops the invasion stalling on its own revolts. The Crown of the Others no longer refuses its own king, and a load error on the house of the Others is gone. 1.1.0b — Keeping pace with A Game of Thrones A hotfix for AGOT's 0.5.2 hotfix. An invasion war counts its goal as held once the dead occupy six tenths of it, so held ground plus a won field closes a war inside a season instead of a second winter. The seventy-two named dragons look the way AGOT now paints them, a camp with a dragon in it cannot be moved beyond an intact Wall, and dragon eggs are held by the right people. 1.1.0a — One Host A hotfix, no new content. The dead stop fighting the dead: the Others no longer declare de jure wars, a war with the dead on both sides cannot be declared on thirteen casus belli, and the Night King's own invasion can no longer be aimed at his own. Nobody keeps an alliance with the dead, and the living no longer serve them. From a full playthrough log: the Trial of Seven no longer carves one name three times, the spear card shows its portraits, and the two cards that could land on the same day no longer contradict each other. Twelve fixes. 1.1.0 — The Last Hour The Night King is fought on foot, in the snow, by you and the people who were there with you. Lose and he keeps you. White Walkers can be met during Winter Is Coming. The character page records the war. A rider can force a dragon over a standing Wall. The Wall's fall is told to everyone in their own station. His host grows with his conquest, from twenty thousand beyond the Wall to two hundred thousand once the North falls, and a field kill no longer ends the Long Night; only a bane does. Underneath it, the largest fix pass the mod has had, including three overrides that had never run at all. 1.0.16a — The Wanderer The Night King keeps his land on older saves, answers to nobody, and can pay his men again.
