docs.t: AGOT: The Long Night & Azor Ahai — a CK3 Game of Thrones mod
docs.x: Full disclosure You deserve to know what a submod touches, so here is the whole list. Every entry is a same-name override of exactly one AGOT definition: their body copied in full, one documented change, re-checked against their current version every release. It is longer than it used to be, because the mod is. Twenty definitions Six scripted rules : alliances (nothing living keeps an alliance with the dead), who may be played (a character raised as one of the dead hands off to an heir), the second chance at a natural death (the red priest's last kiss), who may be a guest, who may be regent (never a sworn brother, never for a wight), and who may move a camp (ranging captains, like the First Ranger) Eight scripted triggers : knights, court positions, councillors and commanders (the living do not serve the dead, and the Night King may lead his own host), capture (he is imprisoned rather than randomly slain in a siege), regency for personal reasons, who may become a landless adventurer (never one of the dead), and one check thirteen AGOT casus belli share (the dead cannot declare war on the dead) Four scripted effects : how rulers are named (wights, ranging captains, wardens and the Others get their titles; every other mod's titles pass straight through), what happens when a dragon dies in a dragon duel (the dead may claim it), AGOT's dragon battle events (a dragon in battle cannot pick the Night King out of the line), and the melee's scene (snow, not a tourney ground) One decision, one casus belli : Restore the Night's Watch (refounded only when there is no Watch left), and the independence war (a sworn brother cannot secede from the Lord Commander) And two that merge rather than replace The ranger-camp domicile, so a ranging captain can hold a camp at all, and the Night's Watch title-gain handler, so appointing one doesn't force a government change on him. Everything else sits alongside AGOT rather than on top of it. The mod is safe to add and to update mid-save, though game rules are baked in when a save is created, so an existing campaign keeps whatever rules it started with. Built on the work of others. This is a fork standing on Freeholder's original Long Night, Tehaen's 1.19 update, and Wepo94's The Long Night+.

docs.t: AGOT: The Long Night & Azor Ahai — a CK3 Game of Thrones mod
docs.s: There is a door in this mod
docs.x: For the ones who read this far It has no handle on the outside. It opens for one kind of lord, it is checked exactly once — at the moment your character first draws breath — and nobody has ever stumbled into it by accident. The riddle of the household ledger Three decisions sit behind it. They do not appear greyed out with their requirements listed; if you are not the one it is waiting for, they do not exist . That is how it was built. Everything you need is below. Nothing below is a lie. Found your own house — and answer to no one above you. Take the sin the septons put in the flesh, and the virtue they put in the work. Both. They sit oddly together. That is rather the point. Then set your sword-arm at three fives — not one more, and not one less. Do all of it in the ruler designer, before the first snow. The door is checked once and never again, so a build that drifts into shape later will find nothing waiting. What's behind it: a household to put in order, a house to write down, and a ship that came back from somewhere ships do not come back from. The ship is the big one. It needs no console, no save editing and no downloads, only a character sheet built a particular way.

docs.t: AGOT: The Long Night & Azor Ahai — a CK3 Game of Thrones mod
docs.x: Common questions Do I really have to disable the other Long Night mods? Yes, and it's the single most common cause of something being broken. This mod is a fork of both AGOT: The Long Night and The Long Night+, and it ships files at the same paths. Load order won't save you: either of them enabled anywhere in your playset overrides this mod with older code. They have to be disabled, not sorted lower. You can unsubscribe from them entirely. Do I need to start a new game? No. It's safe to add and to update mid-save. The one caveat is that CK3 bakes game rules in when a save is created, so an existing campaign keeps whatever rules it started with. If you want to change the invasion timing or difficulty, that needs a fresh save. Does it work with Supernatural? Yes, with the compatibility patch. Load this mod, then Supernatural, then AGOT: Supernatural & The Long Night Compatibility Patch last. Supernatural has its own page here if you haven't seen it. What if I use other dragon mods? Pick them at campaign start and keep them. Dead dragons' appearances are stored against the exact set of portrait genes loaded at the time, so adding or removing any gene-adding mod mid-save can scramble dragons that have already died. Living dragons are unaffected. What version of CK3 is it for? CK3 1.19.0.6, built against the current release of A Game of Thrones. CK3 1.20 came out on 30 September 2026, but A Game of Thrones has not been updated for it yet, so keep the game on 1.19.0.6 for now. How to stay on 1.19. How do I actually kill the Night King? Beat the dead in the field once; that opens the War for the Dawn, which only an independent ruler can declare. Reach him, and the confrontation is the Last Hour: a Trial-of-Seven melee, you and your companions against him and his Walkers. Bring a bane. Dragonglass, Valyrian steel, Lightbringer or dragonfire destroy him; anything else casts him down and the dark crowns another. Prowess counts for half against them, so a great swordsman with castle steel loses eventually. Bring companions, because losing has a worse outcome than dying: he raises you as one of his, and no priest can argue with that. What did 1.1.0 change? The ending. The Night King is fought on foot in a melee instead of rolled; lose and you are raised as an Other; White Walkers can be met during Winter Is Coming; the character page remembers the war; a rider can force a dragon over a standing Wall; and his host now grows with his conquest instead of arriving at full size. The 1.1.0a hotfix that followed stopped the dead declaring wars on each other and keeping allies among the living. The full notes are in What's changed below. Is it translated? English is complete. The Russian translation covers most of the mod; the newest events (the Last Hour, the encounter, the spear, consecration, travel danger) are still in English. Where do I report a bug or suggest something? The Long Night Discord is the fastest route: bug reports, ideas and questions all land there, and player input has driven a lot of what's in the mod. The Steam Workshop comments work too.

Tap a question to open its answer; each one links to the full section. Open all Setup Does it work on CK3 1.20? Not yet, and not because of this mod. CK3 1.20 came out on 30 September 2026, and A Game of Thrones is still built for 1.19.0.6 . The Long Night is an AGOT submod, so it follows AGOT: keep the game on 1.19.0.6 until AGOT updates. How to stay on 1.19. Do I have to disable the other Long Night mods? Yes. AGOT: The Long Night and The Long Night+ must be unchecked, not sorted below. This mod ships files at the same paths, so either of them anywhere in the playset overrides it with older code. Full section. The Night King How do I kill the Night King? Beat the dead in the field once so the War for the Dawn can be declared (independent rulers only), win a battle he is standing in, and take The Field Afterwards . Only dragonglass, Valyrian steel, Lightbringer or dragonfire destroy him; anything else casts him down, and within days he rises again, the same face and the same name. Form the line and fight the Last Hour with companions; lose it and he keeps you. Full section. Why has the Night King stalled after taking a region? The invasion moves in stages: beyond the Wall, then the Wall, then the North, then everywhere. Since 1.1.3 each stage waits only while someone he can attack still holds land in its region; before that, a lord he could not reach kept the gate shut. A stage that still cannot finish times out on its own: eight years beyond the Wall, four at the Wall, twenty in the North. He also never opens a new war while he is fighting one, and until 1.1.1 that included revolts by his own peasants. Full section. Azor Ahai and resurrection How do I get resurrected? Full section. The Night King How do I kill the Night King? Beat the dead in the field once so the War for the Dawn can be declared (independent rulers only), win a battle he is standing in, and take The Field Afterwards . Only dragonglass, Valyrian steel, Lightbringer or dragonfire destroy him; anything else casts him down, and within days he rises again, the same face and the same name. docs.s: The Night King and his host
docs.x: The Night King He is created at the Frigid Rise on the day the invasion opens: six to eight thousand years old, martial 25, intrigue 100, learning 65, prowess 30, carrying the traits Other and Great Other and the nickname the Night King . His title reads King Other 'the Night King' , with no number after the name. His culture is the Others (frostborn in the files), his faith the Cold Gods, his house the Others, his realm The Land of Always Winter , renamed The Long Night once he holds thirty counties. He takes the hegemony and fifteen counties beyond the Wall on day one, is made independent, and receives the Crown of the Others and the Crystal Sword. He leads his host in person. One of the Others is always his named heir: the best sword in his court, a man first. If he is cast down, that heir takes the crown and rises in his place with his face, his name and the whole kit, so to everyone watching the Night King has simply got back up (1.1.3), and killing him with ordinary steel does not leave the dead weaker. His culture cannot be reasoned with: the dead learn nothing (their innovations are Bronze Age and never advance), keep no mercenaries, buy nothing, and have every county opinion at +400 so nothing of theirs ever revolts. The Night King's court is sixty-two elite Others, and every ten days it is re-sacrificed: frostborn courtiers are made Others, everyone else and every prisoner dies. Since 1.1.1 the Others, the Night King and wights cannot run hostile or personal schemes at all. How big his host is Two forces. The elite host is fixed: ten thousand of The Dead (damage 38, toughness 75, siege tier 4) plus trebuchets, needing no supply. The Risen Dead horde (damage 3, toughness 25, counters peasant militia, costs him nothing to keep) is a milestone top-up, refilled every thirty days up to four regiments at a time: Milestone Standard target Weak ×0.75 Strong ×1.25 Insane ×1.5 The invasion opens 20,000 15,000 25,000 30,000 Everything beyond the Wall is his 50,000 37,500 62,500 75,000 Castle Black has fallen 100,000 75,000 125,000 150,000 The North is done 200,000 150,000 250,000 300,000 140 counties or more 250,000 187,500 312,500 375,000 The hard cap is 500,000, the population of King's Landing. Both units fight better in winter. His commanders carry The Dead Do Not Tire , which halves siege morale loss and shortens siege phases by a quarter. Under The Cycle later waves stack more on top (see After the Dawn ). The Risen Dead horde (damage 3, toughness 25, counters peasant militia, costs him nothing to keep) is a milestone top-up, refilled every thirty days up to four regiments at a time: Milestone Standard target Weak ×0.75 Strong ×1.25 Insane ×1.5 The invasion opens 20,000 15,000 25,000 30,000 Everything beyond the Wall is his 50,000 37,500 62,500 75,000 Castle Black has fallen 100,000 75,000 125,000 150,000 The North is done 200,000 150,000 250,000 300,000 140 counties or more 250,000 187,500 312,500 375,000 The hard cap is 500,000, the population of King's Landing. Both units fight better in winter.

docs.x: Every thirty days the invasion looks for a neighbouring independent ruler to attack. Small neighbours (AI, under four counties, below empire tier) are absorbed by fealty rather than war, even while he is busy; anyone bigger, or any player, gets a war. The invasion does not start a new war while it is fighting one, and it takes a pause between wars (the table above). Targets follow a ladder of stage gates, each with a clock that fails open so a gate can never stall the invasion for good: Beyond the Wall first. While the Wall stands and a neighbour he can attack still holds land beyond the Wall, or unclaimed wilderness up there is still being absorbed (one county every thirty days), only holders of land beyond the Wall qualify. Eight-year window. Then the Wall. While Castle Black stands, only a ruler seated at or holding land on the Wall. Four-year window, refilled by four years each time the Watch beats the dead from a Wall seat. The Wall is the climax, enforced. Then the North. Once Castle Black has fallen, only holders of land in the North, until no neighbour he can attack holds any of it. Twenty-year window. Then everywhere. Inside the North the front marches rather than jumps: a target outside the North is illegal while any living northern March still borders the dead, and Winterfell's crown is illegal while any other northern March stands. Every great house's seat is a Last Bastion during Winter Is Coming and the Long Night (+3 fort level, +50% garrison, +8 defender advantage), and the target picker walks around bastions until the seat's own duchy is half in dead hands; a crown's seat is admitted only once the dead hold two kingdom titles or ten counties in that empire. Until 1.1.3 a region held by someone the Night King could not reach as a top liege, such as a northern county whose lord answers to a southern king, kept that stage's gate armed until its window lapsed. That was the mechanism behind "he took the North and stopped". Since 1.1.3 each stage asks the same question the target search does, so land he cannot attack no longer holds a gate, and the host's milestones follow the same answer. The windows stay as a backstop and run once per Long Night: a Night King who is cast down and rises again does not restart them.

docs.t: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Wiki — every mechanic on one page
docs.x: The casus belli is Seize All Occupied Lands , and the war is called The Long Night . The War Tier rule picks the size of the bite: March (the default) takes one kingdom-tier March at a time, or a duchy from a smaller victim; Duchy always takes one duchy; Empire sweeps whole realms. Occupation counts for war score with the defender's capital weighted; since 1.1.0b a war counts its goal as held once the dead occupy six tenths of it, and the score climbs on its own from there so held ground plus a won field closes a war inside a season. Since 1.1.3, in a March or Empire war occupation alone can carry at most three quarters of the bar and the climb waits six months into the war, so the Watch and the Iron Throne are no longer beaten before anyone has fought. Duchy wars, which is every war beyond the Wall, are unchanged. When he wins, the war goal transfers in full and any other occupied county transfers only if it connects to land the dead already hold; the rest is given back, and allies' land is never taken. On Standard and above extra bordering duchies come with the goal (table above), never a bastion. When he loses, the invasion pauses for the re-arm period, he pays reparations, and the world remembers: the War for the Dawn can only be declared once the dead have lost a war , or once the Night King has been cast down in the field. The dead have no friends. No alliance survives with one of them on either side, no living knight, councillor, court official or commander serves them, any dead lord standing outside the Night King's realm is sworn to him (1.1.3; before that such lords were made independent, which left realms of the dead he never took back), no living ruler can fight on their side of a war (a company, a paid ally or a hired sword is removed the moment it joins, and the Night King's living tributaries are released), the dead never declare war on the dead, and every county that comes into dead hands is set to full control on the day it arrives (1.1.1), so his own peasants never rise against him.

docs.x: The Wall comes down when the dead take Castle Black: the Watch is at war with the Night King and he holds the county, or Castle Black is already in dead hands. Every player gets the cinematic The Wall Has Fallen , and the middle section of the Wall breaks on the map. A fifth of every black brother flees south; sworn brothers who held castles keep them, and the rest are released from their vows as they go and pooled at Winterfell, Karhold and the Last Hearth, so Castle Black no longer pulls them back (1.1.3). Castle Black takes The Wall Is Broken (−15 county opinion, −20% development growth, −15% supply). Thirty days later comes The Age of Heroes Is Ended , opening in your own station: sworn brother, free folk, blood of the dragon, northman, red priest, lord, or nobody. It writes the memory alive when the Wall fell . Thirty days after that Castle Black is ruined, the North stage of the invasion opens, and the horde's next milestone unlocks. The moment the dead hold any county on the Wall, the ward is gone: living dragons can fight beyond the Wall without the penalty, and the +60 the spear gets against a dragon forced over an intact Wall is removed. If the living retake the Wall, the ward returns. Under The Cycle , the Wall is raised again in the next Long Summer. Once the Long Night arrives, Black Cloaks at Your Gates can reach dukes and up across the Seven Kingdoms (never Dorne, the Reach or the Stormlands): real survivors from the Wall first, one stranger if the list is empty. Take them in and up to three join you, free of their vows, followed by What the Watch Left You , which can put Black Cloaks on the Walls on your realm for twenty years (+5% garrison, +5% reinforcement, +2 advantage).

docs.x: Who gets raised Dying is not the trigger; being taken into the dead's realm is . Anyone who gains a title from one of the dead, any vassal they gain, every courtier of an Other, and every living person in the Night King's service is converted, along with their court. Before it happens a landless noble may flee (a base 15% chance, more if craven, less if brave), and a landed lord may flee south as a refugee of the Dawn (base 10%), which is also the Flee South decision offered to any lord the dark is coming for. The dead keep no vows: a sworn brother or silent sister raised without a title of his or her own loses the vows (1.1.3). A wight keeps his face, his titles and his realm, now under the Risen Thrall government, which is unplayable by design: a player who is raised hands off to an heir. The trait Wight makes him tireless (health +50, immortal, incapacitated, cannot marry or have children, no inheritance), hated (−150 general opinion) and dreaded (+25). Every alliance, friendship, love and marriage he had is severed, and his spouse gets Death Did Us Part . Close family, friends and lovers who are players get A Face I Know when someone they knew rises. A wight is never promoted to an Other. The Night King's own kill is different. Lose the Last Hour to him and you are raised as an Other , not a wight, with the Other trait, the house of the Others and the flag that puts you on his side of the line the next time a champion reaches him. A landed champion stays landed in the dead's host. When the Night King is destroyed, every wight and every risen dragon dies where it stands, every living member of the house of the Others is gone save one (see the Cycle ), and the land the dead held is scoured. Undead dragons Under the default rule, They Raise Their Kills , the Others are given nothing. A dragon that dies during the Long Night with the dead involved, killed by one of them or dying over ground they hold, is recorded, and every three years, if the Night King has no dragon, one recorded dragon is raised: same name, same face, same size, the colour of ice, immortal, carrying the trait Risen and the nickname the Undead . Further dragons go to his lieutenants. A dragon that dies fighting another dragon over ground the dead can claim is not killed but taken in place , and its rider gets The Wrong Colour . An undead dragon that dies stays dead. One Simply Appears hands him a dragon while dragons exist anywhere; Off means never. The spear In any Long Night battle where the Night King commands or fights, if the dead have no dragon and the spear is not on cooldown, one rider on the field is drawn at random and he throws. The three-year cooldown arms on the throw, hit or miss. Dragon size Hit chance Under 30 (a hatchling) 40% 30 to 69 36% 70 to 99 32% 100 to 139 27% 140 to 179 23% 180 to 229 18% 230 to 299 13% 300 to 399 8% 400 and up (Balerion's size) 5% Add 12 beyond the Wall, and add 60 more if the rider forced the dragon over an intact Wall; the floor is 5%. On a hit the dragon is taken, and the rider rolls to live at 60/40 base, better with prowess, physique, a dragonrider's skill and a champion's traits, worse for age and bad health. Survivors are wounded, gain 200 prestige, and later get The Empty Sky . The Wall is a ward During Winter Is Coming and the Long Night a rider whose dragon approaches the Wall gets [Dragon] Will Not Cross , once. You can take her up again (+50 prestige, the dragon likes you less), stand down and let her stay behind, write to the Citadel, or ask it of her anyway , which counts the dragon as present for the bane and the Field Afterwards, at the price of that +60 on the spear while the Wall stands. The AI is likelier to force it the less it knows: never with learning of 14 or more, never if craven, often if arrog

docs.t: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Wiki — every mechanic on one page
docs.x: From the day the invasion opens until the Dawn, the travel planner shows the danger before you commit a route: The Dead Hold This Land (+60) on every county the dead hold, The Dead Are One County Away (+25) on every living county bordering them, and Past the Wall (+40) on living land beyond the Wall. On a dead road each travel step has an 8% chance of an encounter, doubled in the Long Night, with a six-month cooldown and thirty lost days either way. The Road Is Not Empty is wights: ride through them (a prowess test, 55% clean), form a line and get a fire going (80% they burn, 20% they burn and so does one of yours), or leave the wagons and ride. One of Them is a White Walker, and it only appears in the Long Night beyond the Wall or on dead ground: meet it (a very hard prowess test, 45% it comes apart, 55% it lets you live, which is worse), let someone be the slowest, or ride and do not look back. Surviving an Other on the road with dragonglass or Valyrian steel is what earns the prophecy mark for walking among the dead.

docs.t: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Wiki — every mechanic on one page
docs.x: The Watch's realm is renamed The Night's Watch . Nineteen castles on the Wall, eight ranging companies with camps on the map, a Lord Commander with decisions nobody else gets, and a set of rules that keep the Watch out of southern politics whether it likes it or not. Taking the black The decision is Take the Black . It is open to any adult man standing in the Seven Kingdoms who is not free folk, not a maester or septon, not already a sworn brother and not one of the dead, while a Lord Commander exists and a ranging company is free (vacant, or held by an AI captain he can stand down). You need somewhere for the realm to go: an heir, a liege, or nothing to give up. There is no prestige requirement. Women are refused at the gate. What it costs is the oath: every title you hold passes to your primary heir, or to your liege if you have none, with no claim kept; your marriage, betrothal, claims, debts, Iron Bank shares and Kingsguard place end at the Wall; any dragon that answers to you is unbonded; any adventurer company you led is disbanded. Your successor remembers it (+40 opinion for sixty years), your family and former vassals think better of you for it, and your close family moves to the heir's court. Since 1.1.3 your old council is dismissed, courtiers fit for the black take it with you and most of the rest go their own way, and a sworn brother joins your camp so the four ranger seats can be filled. What you get is a ranging company of your own, sworn to the Lord Commander, and you play on as the brother. The eight ranging companies The companies are The Long Ranging, The Deep Ranging, The Cold Ranging, The Silent Ranging, The Black Ranging, The Winter Ranging, The Far Ranging and The Last Ranging . Each is a landless title under the Wall with a real camp on the map, a captain titled Ranger-Captain , and its own government, Ranging Company : army upkeep −60%, men-at-arms upkeep −70%, +2 martial and +2 prowess per prestige level, +0.5 monthly dread, and no holy orders. The camp is the ranger camp AGOT gives the First Ranger, opened to all eight companies, and it can only be pitched on the Wall or beyond it, never with raised armies. From game start each company has a historical northman captain, and a new captain every generation, all the way to 8320. A captain can March the Ranging to Craster's Keep, Whitetree or Hardhome and Return to the Wall ; the camp travels, provisions are topped up at the Wall, and the arrival is quiet by design. Once a year, if the Lord Commander's court holds ten or more brothers who could be posted, each company with fewer than six ranging brothers gets one, weighted toward rangers, the brave and the strong. Captains compete for First Ranger : when the holder dies, an AI captain is chosen (martial and prowess of 12 or more, the ranger lifestyle and bravery all count) and moves to that seat; player captains are not drafted into it. Under the default rule the Watch fills companies one through five itself and holds three open for players; Leave Them for Players leaves a dead captain's seat waiting; All Eight Ride keeps every company manned. When a captain dies, the company passes to a qualifying brother of the Lord Commander's court, or a ranger is created for it, or the Lord Commander holds it himself. A ranger who has been sworn long enough (a hundred points of the Night's Watch trait; a recruit does not get given a castle) can Ask for a Castle and trade the company for a keepership. docs.t: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Wiki — every mechanic on one page
docs.x: Castle Black is the Lord Commander's own seat. The other eighteen castles are keeperships held from him: Deep Lake, Icemark, Greyguard, Stonedoor, Hoarfrost Hill, Queensgate, Oakenshield, Woodswatch-by-the-Pool, Sable Hall, Rimegate, Westwatch-by-the-Bridge, Sentinel Stand, Long Barrow, The Torches, Greenguard, and the three county seats, the Nightfort, the Shadow Tower and Eastwatch-by-the-Sea, which are granted last because each carries several baronies with it. A sworn brother without a post can Man an Empty Castle if he is worth one (500 prestige, or landed, or a knight, or a company of 200 men). When nothing is free, Ask for a Command has the Lord Commander relieve an AI keeper who is incapable, past seventy, or never swore his vows; a player's castle is never taken, and every other brother thinks a little less of you for it. A landed brother is playable, his officers are the Master-at-Arms, the Steward of the Keep, the Master Builder and the Recruiter, and he can Restore a Ruined Castle for 400 gold, once every five years, turning a ruin into a castle again. Life on the Wall has its own cards: Mole's Town , The Fist of the First Men (a hundred gold for a store of dragonglass, if you have none), and The Deserter . Petition the Realm asks the North to remember the Wall every three years: 120 gold and 25 prestige as a base, more in the cold, more if you took the black yourself, more if the realm has been feeding the Watch, and every northern ruler likes you a little less for asking.

docs.t: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Wiki — every mechanic on one page
docs.x: Election is AGOT's, and a player Lord Commander who dies passes play to a landed brother of his family, then any landed brother. Two decisions are his alone. Call the Great Ranging (Winter Is Coming or the Long Night, 100 prestige, one at a time, a year between) sends two hundred brothers north. Send them for word and the odds are 40% Word From the North (the warning that unlocks dragonglass, plus prestige and learning), 35% The Ranging Is Lost (four catalyst points, the dark a year closer), 25% They Came Back Quiet (a courtier dead of cold, the dark a year closer, but the word arrives). Lead it yourself for 150 prestige and the odds become 55/30/15. Send a Brother Recruiting rides a sworn brother of your court south. Every duke or greater in the Seven Kingdoms with three or more prisoners receives A Black Brother at the Gate in the months ahead and chooses: every unlanded man in the cells takes the black (the lord gains 100 piety and the Watch's gratitude), coin for the Wall, or nothing, which the Watch remembers.

docs.t: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Wiki — every mechanic on one page
docs.s: Helping the Watch from the south
docs.x: Send Men and Grain to the Wall is open to landed rulers who are northmen, kings, or who have heard the warning, once every five years: a cart of grain (100 gold; +25 Lord Commander opinion, +50 piety, +25 prestige), a season's stores (500; +50, +120, +60), or empty the vaults (1,500; +75, +250, +120). The gold goes straight to the Lord Commander, the realm's ledger goes up by one, two or three, and the Watch's petitions pay out more once the ledger reaches three and again at eight. Emptying the vaults is remembered if you later take the black yourself. Send the Prisoners to the Wall empties your cells in one order. Every prisoner who can take the black goes, as a sworn brother and not as an offer he can refuse, and the decision names a reason for each one who cannot: women, children, free folk, the dead, independent rulers, house heads, the last of a house, and, under the default rule, anyone above county rank. The Tier Ceiling rule can lift that last one so a king can end his days a sworn brother. You gain 100 piety and the Lord Commander's gratitude.

docs.t: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Wiki — every mechanic on one page
docs.s: What a sworn brother cannot do
docs.x: A sworn brother who inherits land outside the Wall renounces it ( The Watch Takes No Part ): the title goes to its de jure liege, or the next lawful hand, never to another brother or one of the dead. Since 1.1.1 this includes the Lord Commander, whose exemption was the bug that left the Watch holding a random county in the North. A sworn brother can only be regent for another sworn brother. Nobody declares independence from the Lord Commander. Ranging captains move camp the way the First Ranger does, and the Watch's own castles, companies and the First Ranger's title are never touched by the guard.

docs.t: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Wiki — every mechanic on one page
docs.x: Mine the Dragonglass appears in Winter Is Coming or the Long Night for any ruler, landless included, who has a reason to know: he heard the warning, looked north, is a sworn brother, has greensight, or the Long Night is simply here. It costs 200 gold plus 200 for each tier above count (a quarter off if you studied the glass, never less than 150) and gives thirty years of Dragonglass Stores , which counts as a bane at the Last Hour and opens the dragonglass option in the melee. Six sites of dragonglass lore, Castle Black and the Fist of the First Men among them, can be visited on a journey. Send for a Red Priest (150 gold) is for a landed adult who is an interloper in the struggle, a player whose faith or culture already counts as involved, or a follower of R'hllor without a priest, and who has a reason to believe: the faith, Valyrian blood, the warning, greensight, or being Stannis or the lord of Dragonstone. A priest arrives in four to thirteen months with The Priest at the Gate . Stannis gets Melisandre if she is free; a Baratheon lord of Dragonstone gets her three times in four; everyone else has a one-in-ten chance of Melisandre or Thoros of Myr, weighted by prophecy deeds, and otherwise a Myrish priest is created for you. If a red priest is already in your hall, serving in any seat or visiting as a guest, the decision becomes Hear the Red Priest instead: free, and the card comes the next day with that priest on it (1.1.3). At the gate you can take the red ( Then your god is my god , which makes an interloper involved in the Long Night, takes the priest's own faith when he follows the red god so he can serve as your chaplain afterwards, and costs 200 piety and 100 prestige), keep your steel and keep the priest, or burn him. A red priest, once he is your court chaplain, is what names you, blesses you, and brings you back.

docs.t: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Wiki — every mechanic on one page
docs.x: A red priest can spend himself on one person, once, ever. There are two roads back and both need the priest in place before you die. What you must do beforehand Have a red priest. He needs the Red Priest trait, to be an available adult, to have at least a first level of devotion or a learning of 10, and to have never given the last kiss. Get one with Send for a Red Priest , or appoint any R'hllor courtier as court chaplain and AGOT gives him the trait. Take Ask for the Lord's Blessing. It is free, has no cooldown and no faith requirement. It is shown whenever a priest who can bless you is within reach: your court chaplain, a ranging company's camp priest, or any courtier or guest. You cannot take it while imprisoned or while another priest's words already stand over you. The priest can also offer it to you himself ( Offer the Lord's Blessing ); refusing him costs him piety. Either way The Words Are Said . Keep him alive and unspent. If your priest dies, the bond is released and you can ask another. If he spends his one kiss on someone else, he is spent forever and you are free to ask again. Ask again after any change of priest. Give the fire a reason. The priest's answer is not automatic (see below). docs.x: Four things: dragonglass (mined stores, an armed knight, or having studied the glass), Valyrian steel (a Valyrian blade: a sword, axe, spear or dagger, never a bow, armour or a goblet), Lightbringer (forged or consecrated), or dragonfire (a living dragon of yours over the field, which beyond an intact Wall means one you forced across). A won melee with ordinary steel or a stray battle death casts him down, and a War for the Dawn won on score with nobody fit to face him leaves him standing (1.1.3). Cast down, he rises again within days: his named heir, always one of the Others, takes the crown, his face, his name and every bonus, and every player gets He Is Not Destroyed , which says what would have ended him. A dragon in the press of an ordinary battle does not count, and since 1.1.3 AGOT's dragon battle events cannot pick him out of the line at all. Casting him down does still count as beating the dead, so it opens the War for the Dawn. Under the War for the Dawn resolution rule even a bane is not enough until that war is won, and the Field Afterwards and the Last Hour only open while a War for the Dawn against him is running. When a bane lands, whoever landed it is Azor Ahai Reborn , marks or no marks, named or not. If a dragon did it, its rider takes the deed. An unnamed nobody can end the Long Night and prove every red priest in the world wrong.

docs.x: Six to ten days after the kill, every player gets The Dawn , and the text is the only place the hidden coin is ever read. If the prophecy was true and the slayer was named: it was prophecy, and it was always going to be. If it was false and he was named: the faith will remember this as the night it was proved right, and it was not. If it was true and nobody named him: the flames never lied, and nobody ever learned to read them. If it was false and nobody named him: he was just a man, and that will have to be enough. If a wild dragon did it and no one can be named: it ended, which is the only part anyone can prove. The trait, the modifier and the nickname do not depend on the coin. The slayer is called the Dawnbringer if he forged Lightbringer and killed with it, the Prince That Was Promised if he was named or has the blood of the dragon, and the Dawn otherwise, with 10,000 dynasty prestige, 2,000 prestige and 1,000 piety. A month later The Men Who Were There names the three who stood in the front rank, from the melee's real line: each is knighted if he was not already, gains 5,000 dynasty prestige and the memory. If you went alone, the record says so. At four months The Reckoning asks whether you write it down.

docs.x: During Winter Is Coming, before the dead have taken a single county, a player who is a sworn brother, or standing at the Wall or beyond it, or whose capital is in the North, has a 15% chance each pulse (with four years between) of Something on the Ridge (a sighting, seven times in ten) or The Snow Stands Up (three in ten): one White Walker of prowess 16 against you and a party of one to five, real men first and created rangers to fill. Win, and It Came Apart : 500 prestige, the memory slew one of the Others , and at three kills the modifier Slayer of White Walkers (+10 dread, +0.3 monthly prestige). Lose, and it is 40% You Do Not Stop Running (your companions die, you are wounded), 45% The Cold Closes (everyone dies, you are taken by the dead), 15% It Lets One Live , the Sam Tarly outcome: the weakest real companion is spared and everyone else, you included, is not.

docs.x: Under the default rule a coin is flipped at game start and hidden forever; the other two rules fix it. It is read exactly once, at the reveal, and it changes nothing but what the world believes it saw. You can do everything right, be named by every priest in Westeros, and find out you were never him.

docs.t: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Wiki — every mechanic on one page
docs.x: When the Night King is destroyed, the land the dead held is scoured : the seat of a kingdom becomes a renowned great ruin, the seat of a duchy a sizeable ruin, everything else wilderness. Only counties the mod scoured are ever touched; Harrenhal and the old ruins are left alone. Twenty, thirty or forty-five years later each scoured ruin that nobody has reclaimed becomes wilderness too, so AGOT's own settlement decision can take it. Every player gets A Dream of Spring . The Question of the North goes, under the default rule, to a player first: a player on the Iron Throne, then a player holding the North, then the highest-ranked player with land in the North. If no player qualifies, or under the rule's Crown option, it goes to the Iron Throne, or an independent King in the North, or the greatest independent crown left standing. It comes within six months: The Watch shall rise again refounds the Night's Watch under a new Lord Commander with the Wall's castles and 500 gold (or reinforces it, if it held), and the free folk are never welcomed south; Let the free folk come south renames the Wall's kingdom the Giftlands and settles it clan by clan, up to two clans a year, as vassals of the crown, and the Watch never rises again. The choice is permanent, even under the Cycle. Lords who fled south as refugees of the Dawn can Return North : a settler caravan with 1,000 provisions and 150 gold, staged up the Kingsroad through King's Landing, the Inn at the Crossroads and Moat Cailin, to their lost seat if it is empty or the nearest empty land. Free folk settle as tribal clans (1.1.3); anyone else takes his culture head's government. Rebuilding the ancestral seat is worth 200 prestige and Restored the Ancestral Seat for life. A refugee with a dragon can instead Return With Fire and settle the question of who holds his hall; there are four ways that goes and only one of them is quiet. The crown can Sell Colonization Rights to Essos , 150 gold a coastal county to a Braavosi, Pentoshi, Myrish, Tyroshi, Lyseni or Volantene lord, once every eighteen months, and every northern vassal remembers it for ten years. With Iron Throne Reformation on, every independent ruler in the Seven Kingdoms is asked The Future of the Seven Kingdoms : swear fealty to the Iron Throne, or remain independent. Under The Cycle , the Dawn lasts five years and flows back into the Long Summer with the ledger wiped, the Wall raised again and Castle Black repaired, a new summer target rolled, and one thing kept: a Night's Queen survives the cleanup to seed the next wave. Waves two and three carry The Dead Remember (+2 levy size, +3 advantage, +10% toughness), four and five Centuries of Winter (+4, +6, +20% toughness, +10% damage, four knights), six and up The Last Long Night (+7, +10, +35% toughness, +25% damage, eight knights, +25% knight effectiveness). Everyone who stood in the front rank at the last Dawn, and Azor Ahai Reborn, carries Saw the First Dawn when the next night opens, and gets You Have Seen This Before .

docs.x: Fourteen rules, all under the AGOT heading, all baked in when a save is created. Defaults are marked. Rule Options The Long Night Chance default Certain (guaranteed) · Near-Certain (75%) · Even Odds (50%) · Remote Odds (25%) · No Chance. One roll, for the first Long Night; a "no" world never accrues summer points, and under The Cycle every later wave comes regardless. The Long Night Moment default A Random Summer (never sooner than 25 years, usually 90 to 130, sometimes far later) · Immediately · In Fifty Years · In One-Hundred Years · In One Hundred-Fifty Years · Full Random (30 years to over two centuries, no cap) · Historical (from a start before 255 AC the Long Night lands between about 280 and 320 AC; from 255 AC or later the game opens in Winter Is Coming and it arrives by 300 AC; either way only if the Chance rule lets it) · Manual (only the Trigger the Long Night decision starts it, every wave is called the same way, the decision is hidden during a Dawn, and the tracker stays empty by design). The Long Night Strength Weak · default Standard · Strong · Insane. See the strength table . The Long Night Resolution default Death (the Long Night ends the moment the Night King is destroyed) · War for the Dawn (killing him is not enough; any death before the war is won casts him down, and he rises again). The Long Night War Tier Duchy (slow grind) · default March (recommended; Winterfell only once the North has gone quiet) · Empire (rapid onslaught). The Long Night Ice Dragon default They Raise Their Kills · One Simply Appears · Off. The Question of the North default A Player in the North First (a player on the Iron Throne, then a player holding the North, then the highest-ranked player with land in the North) · The Crown (the AI crown decides, as before 1.1.3). The Long Night Iron Throne Reformation default On (kingdom-tier rulers are offered fealty to the Iron Throne after the Dawn) · Off. The Long Night Recurrence default Once · The Cycle (the Long Night comes back, heavier each time; the Moment rule sets the gap). Send the Prisoners Tier Ceiling default Counts and Below · Any Rank (the King of the Iron Throne can end his days a sworn brother). Azor Ahai — Was There Ever a Prince? default Let the Flames Decide (a hidden coin) · There Is a Prince · There Is No Prince. Azor Ahai — Naming Claimants default As the Books Have It (two and four marks) · The Flames Are Loud (one and three) · The Citadel's Reading (three and six) · Nobody Is Ever Named. Azor Ahai — Who May Be Named default Anyone at All · Players Only · One at a Time (at most one living Chosen; the seat reopens when they stop breathing). The Ranging Companies default The Watch Recruits (never more than five; three companies held for players) · Leave Them for Players · All Eight Ride.

docs.x: Compatible with AGOT+, Valyrian Steel, Submod Core, Nobility of Westeros, Essos Expanded, Legacy of Valyria, AGOT Additional Models and Special Buildings, Seasons of Ice and Fire, and anything else that names its own rulers. Supernatural needs the compatibility patch, last in the list. Essos Expanded and Legacy of Valyria are untested and unsupported; keep them above this mod. Legacy of Valyria ships its own versions of three rules this mod overrides, including the one that is the whole entry point to resurrection, so this mod must load after it. Every override is one AGOT or vanilla definition, copied in full, with one documented change, re-checked against the current AGOT build every release: Six scripted rules: alliances (nothing living keeps an alliance with the dead), who may be played (a raised player hands off to an heir; a landed sworn brother is playable), the second chance at death (the last kiss), who may be a guest (not the Others), who may be regent (a sworn brother only for a sworn brother), who may move a camp (ranging captains, and no dragon beyond an intact Wall). Eight scripted triggers: knights, court positions, councillors and commanders (the living do not serve the dead; the Night King leads his own host), capture (he is imprisoned rather than slain in a siege), regency for personal reasons, who may become a landless adventurer (never the dead), and the check thirteen AGOT casus belli share (the dead do not declare war on the dead). Four scripted effects: how rulers are titled (wights, captains, the wilderness and the Others get their names; every other mod's titles pass straight through), what happens when a dragon dies in a dragon duel (the dead may claim it), AGOT's dragon battle events (a dragon in battle cannot pick the Night King out of the line), and the melee's scene. One decision, one casus belli, three files: Restore the Night's Watch (hidden once the Question has been asked), the independence war (nobody secedes from the Watch), the ranger-camp domicile (opened to eight companies), the peasant faction (never against a wight), and the portrait animations (five wight poses). Languages: English, Russian, Spanish and French, with every line present in all four. English is the author's; the Spanish and French are a first pass, and corrections are welcome. Large playsets are worth one look at logs/database_conflicts.log .

docs.x: There is a door in this mod. It has no handle on the outside, it opens for one kind of lord, it is checked exactly once, at the moment your character first draws breath, and nobody has ever stumbled into it by accident. Four decisions sit behind it. They do not appear greyed out with their requirements listed; if you are not the one it is waiting for, they do not exist. The riddle of the household ledger Everything you need is below. Nothing below is a lie. Found your own house, and answer to no one above you. Take the sin the septons put in the flesh, and the virtue they put in the work. Both. They sit oddly together. That is rather the point. Then set your sword-arm at three fives , not one more, and not one less. Do all of it in the ruler designer, before the first snow. The door is checked once and never again, so a build that drifts into shape later will find nothing waiting. What's behind it: a household to put in order, a house to write down, a physician worth the name, and a ship that came back from somewhere ships do not come back from. The ship is the big one. No console, no save editing, no downloads. Just a character sheet built a particular way.

docs.x: My priest refused to bring me back. Why? He rolls. The base is 70 to pay against 30 to refuse; if you are not worth the fire (no champion trait, no mark, not fighting in the cold) refusal gets +60, and if you are his friend refusal is cut to a fifth. Make him your friend, earn a mark, and ask again with a fresh priest next time. If the card said there was only ever one of it to give, your priest had already spent his kiss on someone else. I have a red priest but the blessing decision does not show. Check that he is an adult, available (not travelling, not imprisoned), has a first level of devotion or a learning of 10, and has never given the last kiss. Then check that nobody else's blessing already stands over you; the decision tells you if it does. I died and nothing happened. Only battle deaths as a knight or commander, and natural deaths with a red priest as your chaplain, can be argued with. Duels, executions, the Last Hour melee and scripted deaths never can. Battle deaths are also a weighted draw against the game's own, so the blessing raises your odds rather than guaranteeing the card. The Night King took the North and stopped. Before 1.1.3 the North stage waited on every northern county, including ones held by a vassal of a southern king, which he cannot target, until its twenty-year window ran out. Since 1.1.3 it waits only while someone he can attack still holds land in the North, so he moves on as soon as that stops being true. He also never opens a new war while fighting one; before 1.1.1 his own peasant revolts counted, which is fixed. Can I be Lord Commander? Election is AGOT's and the mod does not change who is eligible. A sworn brother holding a castle is playable, and a player Lord Commander who dies passes play to a landed brother of his family. Can a woman take the black? No. The Watch is brothers only, at the gate and in the dungeons order. Does killing him with ordinary steel do anything? It casts him down: within days he rises again, the same face, the same name and the same bonuses, every player gets the card He Is Not Destroyed , and the Long Night goes on. It does count as beating the dead, so it opens the War for the Dawn, and you are remembered as the Undaunted. Can I change the rules on an existing save? No. CK3 bakes game rules in when a save is created. Timing, strength, the prophecy coin and the rest need a fresh campaign. Where do I report a bug? The Long Night Discord is fastest; GitHub issues work too. Include your CK3 version, your full load order, and whether you are on the Workshop copy or a manual install.

docs.x: Version What it did 1.1.3 — The Player Reports One Night King: cast down by anything but a bane, he rises again in the same face and name, a card tells every player so, and dragon battle events can no longer take him. Every dead lord serves him and no living ruler fights on his side. The invasion's stages wait only on land he can attack, and wars on the Watch and the Iron Throne need more than held ground. The freeze at the Wall, the Take the Black council crash, a Valyrian goblet that could become Lightbringer, Send for a Red Priest missing the priest already in your hall, raw trigger text in decisions, free folk turning feudal, and dead courts filling with thousands of new characters a year are fixed. New rule: The Question of the North asks a player first. 1.1.2 — The Cold Does Not Fall He no longer dies by accident: the commander pool, a lost dragon duel and the melee's own engine could kill him outside a scene. The Others are no longer handed to the Iron Throne after a mega-war, and the dead no longer visit living courts as guests. Spanish and French added. 1.1.1 The Watch keeps no land: a sworn brother, the Lord Commander included, renounces anything he inherits outside the Wall. The dead answer to nobody living. Stannis gets Melisandre and Dragonstone usually does. The Others cannot scheme. Every county the dead take is set to full control, so their own peasants never rise, and their land recovers control after a siege instead of never. The Crown of the Others no longer refuses its own king. A load error on the house of the Others fixed. 1.1.0b Keeping pace with AGOT's 0.5.2 hotfix: an invasion war counts its goal as held once the dead occupy six tenths of it; the named dragons look the way AGOT now paints them; no camp with a dragon in it crosses an intact Wall. 1.1.0a — One Host The dead stop fighting the dead and keeping allies among the living; the Trial of Seven's roll call; the spear card's portraits; twelve fixes from a full playthrough log. 1.1.0 — The Last Hour The melee against the Night King; being raised as an Other; White Walkers in Winter Is Coming; memories; dragons over the Wall; a host that grows with his conquest; a field kill no longer ends the Long Night. 1.0.16a — The Wanderer The Night King keeps his land and pays his men; Send the Dungeons to the Wall; a limit on resurrections. 1.0.16 — The Dead That Frighten You The Others' culture; the strength rule rebuilt on advantage, damage and toughness; the Last Hour becomes a duel; the War for the Dawn gated on the dead losing a war. 1.0.15 — The Repair Release Killing him wins the war; Azor Ahai Reborn to the right man; only a bane destroys him; the Beric track; the Night King's face. 1.0.15a "Missing Title Loc" fixed for every other submod's rulers. 1.0.14 The Lord's Blessing works for players; AGOT 5.0 and 5.1; the North falls in order. 1.0.13 AGOT 0.5.1 compatibility; the mod stops shipping AGOT's rules file. 1.0.12 Lightbringer consecration; the Night King's spear; travel danger; the Great Ranging reworked. 1.0.11a The three cards that mark the turn of the age know who you are; the priest who names you has a face. 1.0.4 to 1.0.11 The struggle, the ranging companies, the Wall's castles, Send Men and Grain, the aftermath, the Russian translation. Nearly every fix since August 2026 started as a report in the Discord or the Workshop comments, and reporters are credited by name in every changelog. If the AGOT team ever ships their own Long Night, this mod will come down and point at it. If they would rather lift anything from here into the base mod, it is theirs, no strings. docs.x: Privacy policy Privacy Policy — Caffeine Break Buddy Effective July 5, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 Publisher Dlonem LLC Contact caffeinebreakbuddy@dlonem.com copy The short version. Caffeine Break Buddy is a personal caffeine-reset and habit-tracking app for Android (and for iOS, if released there later). Everything you log — your reset, intake calendar, daily check-ins, energy & sleep ratings, symptoms, badges, and the Caffeine & Sleep estimates — is stored only on your device . We run no servers and cannot see your data. The one exception is advertising : the free version shows ads through Google AdMob, which uses limited device and advertising identifiers to serve them. The one-time premium purchase removes ads. The app is an educational wellness tool — not a medical, diagnostic, or treatment service . Jump to a section 1. Who this applies to 2. What the app stores, and where 3. Advertising (free version) — Google AdMob 4. Data we process — at a glance 5. Purchases 6. What we do not do 7. Not medical advice 8. Children 9. Your choices & rights 10. Data security & retention 11. Changes to this policy 12. Contact 1 Who this applies to This policy covers the Caffeine Break Buddy mobile application published by Dlonem LLC on Google Play (and the Apple App Store , if released there later). The app is intended for a general adult audience. It is not directed to children, and we do not knowingly collect data from anyone under 13 (or the minimum age required by your region and the platform). 2 What the app stores, and where Caffeine Break Buddy is a local-first app. The information you enter is stored on your device only . Dlonem LLC operates no servers, no database, and no cloud storage of its own, and therefore has no access to this information and does not transmit it to us. What you can enter. Your onboarding profile (typical caffeine intake and delivery methods, timing, goal, and optional metabolism factors such as age range, sensitivity, smoking status, combined-pill / pregnancy status, and whether you take certain medications), your intake calendar, daily check-ins (energy, mood, headache, focus, sleep quality, cravings), milestone badges, and your bedtime/wake settings. This is used only to power the app's estimates and coaching on your device. No account, no cloud. The app has no sign-in and no server. Your data stays in this app's local storage on your device — we never receive, read, or store it, and it is not synced to any cloud by us. Optional manual backup. You can export a copy of your own data from within the app (Settings → Back up my data) and save it wherever you choose using your device's own share options, then import it later to restore. This is entirely manual and optional; the exported copy goes only where you send it. (On Android, the system's own Auto Backup may separately back up app data to your personal Google Drive under Google's terms — a platform feature we do not control or receive.) Deleting your data. You can reset your current break or erase everything from within the app (Settings → Reset this break / Start over). Uninstalling the app removes locally stored data from your device. 3 Advertising (free version) — Google AdMob The free version displays ads via Google AdMob (the Google Mobile Ads SDK). To serve and measure ads, AdMob may collect and process data such as your device's advertising identifier , IP address, general device information, and ad interactions, for advertising, analytics, and fraud-prevention purposes. Google handles this data under its own privacy policy. It is encrypted in transit and is kept separate from the personal reset data in Section 2 — AdMob does not receive your check-ins, symptoms, calendar, or profile answers. Google's handling of this data: policies.google.com/privacy and how Google uses information from partner apps . Android: you can reset or delete your advertising ID in Settings → Privacy → Ads. iOS — App Tracking Transparency (ATT): on Apple devices the app will ask for your permission before any tracking that uses your device's advertising identifier (IDFA). If you decline, ads may still be shown but will be non-personalized. You can change this any time in iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Tracking. Region consent (EU/UK and similar): where required, you will be asked for ad-consent choices through Google's consent mechanism before personalized ads are shown. Removing ads: the one-time premium purchase removes all ads, after which the ad SDK no longer serves ads in the app. 4 Data we process — at a glance This table mirrors the answers you should give in Google Play's Data safety form and Apple's App Privacy questionnaire. Data Where it lives Purpose Linked to you / used to track? Reset, intake calendar, check-ins, energy/sleep ratings, symptoms, badges, profile & metabolism inputs On your device only (plus any manual backup copy you export yourself) App functionality you asked for No — never sent to us; not used for tracking Advertising ID, IP, device info, ad interactions Processed by Google AdMob Advertising, measurement, fraud prevention Used for ads by Google; on iOS only with your ATT permission Purchase record (that you bought premium) Google Play / Apple, on-device receipt Unlock premium; restore purchases Handled by the store; no card details reach us Note on health-related inputs: some optional profile answers (e.g. sensitivity, combined-pill / pregnancy status, medications) may be considered health-related. They are used only on your device to personalize your estimates, are never transmitted to us, and are never shared with the ad SDK. 5 Purchases The optional one-time premium purchase is processed by the platform's billing system — Google Play Billing on Android and Apple In-App Purchase (StoreKit) on iOS. We do not receive or store your payment-card details; the store handles the transaction under its own terms. A Restore Purchases option lets you re-unlock premium on a new device using the same store account. 6 What we do not do To be explicit: Dlonem LLC does not sell, rent, or trade your personal information; does not build advertising or marketing profiles from your reset data, check-ins, symptoms, or health-related answers; does not require an account, email, or sign-up to use the app; and operates no server or database that receives your tracking data. The only information that leaves your device is the limited advertising data handled by Google (Section 3) and, only if you choose it, an optional backup to your own personal cloud account. 7 Not medical advice Caffeine Break Buddy is an educational wellness and habit-tracking tool . Its recovery timelines, half-life and sleep-cutoff estimates, and coaching are informational only and are not medical advice, and do not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any condition . Estimates are approximations, not guarantees. Consult a qualified professional for medical advice, especially if you have a heart condition, are pregnant, or take medications. 8 Children The app is not directed to children and we collect no personal information from anyone — including children — because the app collects no data and transmits nothing to us. There is therefore nothing on our end for us to access or delete. Any data a user enters lives only on their own device and can be erased at any time within the app (Settings → Start over) or by uninstalling. 9 Your choices & rights Because your personal reset data stays on your device, you control it directly — view, edit, or erase it in the app at any time. For rights relating to ad data processed by Google (such as access or deletion requests under the GDPR, UK GDPR, or CCPA/CPRA), see Google's privacy policy linked in Section 3; you can also exercise ad choices via your device’s ad/tracking settings, or contact us with any privacy question at caffeinebreakbuddy@dlonem.com . We will respond within a reasonable time. 10 Data security & retention Because your tracking data never leaves your device (except to a manual backup you choose to export yourself), it is protected by your device’s own operating-system security and any passcode or biometric lock you use. We retain none of it, because we never receive it — it lives only on your device for as long as you keep the app installed and is removed when you erase it in-app or uninstall. Advertising data processed by Google is retained by Google under its own policies. There is no server-side copy for us to lose, breach, or be compelled to disclose. 11 Changes to this policy We may update this policy as the app evolves or as store requirements change. Material changes will be reflected by updating the “Last updated” date above and, where appropriate, an in-app notice. Continued use of the app after an update means you accept the revised policy. 12 Contact Questions, requests, or concerns about this policy or your data: caffeinebreakbuddy@dlonem.com . We will respond within a reasonable time. Replies come from officialdlonem@gmail.com — that is us, not spam; the @dlonem.com addresses receive mail but cannot send it. © 2026 Dlonem LLC · Caffeine Break Buddy v1.0.0 · Questions? caffeinebreakbuddy@dlonem.com

docs.x: The fine print Privacy policy Short, because there isn't much to disclose. Your data stays on your device. Per-app policies Pick your app Each app has its own dedicated policy. These are the canonical documents linked from the store listings. T THC Break Buddy Support & privacy contact: thcbreakbuddy@dlonem.com Read the policy C Caffeine Break Buddy Support & privacy contact: caffeinebreakbuddy@dlonem.com Read the policy N Nicotine Break Buddy Support & privacy contact: nicotinebreakbuddy@dlonem.com Read the policy D Tiny Dragon Hoard Support & privacy contact: tinydragonhoard@dlonem.com Read the policy The studio-wide version Effective date: July 14, 2026 · Last updated: October 1, 2026 Dlonem LLC ("Dlonem," "we," "us," "our") builds the mobile applications Tiny Dragon Hoard and the Break Buddy apps (together, the "Apps"). This policy explains what information the Apps handle and how. We built our Apps to be privacy-friendly; most of them run entirely on your device. Each app has its own support and privacy address, listed on that app’s policy page above. Use it for anything specific to that app. For company-level questions, contact@dlonem.com reaches us too. Replies come from officialdlonem@gmail.com . That is us, not spam; the @dlonem.com addresses receive mail but cannot send it. Information you enter stays on your device The Break Buddy apps store what you enter (your tracking history, notes, and reminders) locally on your device. We do not collect it, send it to our servers, or have access to it. Deleting the app removes this data from your device. No accounts required You can use the Apps without creating an account or giving us your name, email, or other personal details. Advertising in the apps Some Apps display ads through Google AdMob. To serve ads, Google and its partners may collect and use certain device and usage information, including advertising identifiers, under Google's own policies. You can read more at policies.google.com/technologies/ads and manage ad personalization in your device settings. Apps that do not show ads do not collect this information. Cookies and similar technologies on this website This website (dlonem.com) sets no cookies of its own . It has no login, no shopping basket, and no first-party tracking. Where advertising is served on this site, however, advertising cookies set by third parties do apply, and the section below explains them. One page keeps something in your browser: the checklist on the Hall of Thanes guide remembers which boxes you ticked, using your browser's local storage. It stays on your device, is never sent to us or anyone else, and the page's Clear the list button removes it. Some pages show live figures: the mod subscriber and YouTube numbers, each mod's newest Steam change note, the WoW Forever headlines and Shorts on The Grey Company page and the WoW Forever guides, and a notice when the YouTube channel is live or has a stream scheduled. These are fetched through a small service we run on Cloudflare at feed.dlonem.com, which reads Steam's (including the public Workshop change-notes pages on steamcommunity.com), YouTube's, Discord's, Apple's and the news site's public data. It sets no cookies and passes nothing about you to Steam, YouTube or the news site; Cloudflare handles that request under its own privacy policy. Pages that list a Discord server may ask discord.com for that server's member count, the same figure Discord shows on its invite. Server icons load from Discord's image server (cdn.discordapp.com), and video thumbnails from YouTube's (i.ytimg.com). If you choose to play a live stream on this site, the player loads from youtube-nocookie.com, and from then on YouTube's player works as it does anywhere. The THC Break Buddy page may also ask Apple's public app lookup (itunes.apple.com) for the app's current version. The member-count and version requests are sent without cookies. Images and the player load the way they would on any site that shows them, so Discord and YouTube may see the request and any cookies your browser already holds for them, under their own privacy policies. Advertising on this website Third-party vendors, including Google, use cookies to serve ads based on a user's prior visits to this website or other websites. Google's use of advertising cookies enables it and its partners to serve ads to you based on your visit to this site and/or other sites on the internet. You can opt out of personalised advertising at any time: Turn off personalised ads from Google in Google Ads Settings (also reachable at My Ad Center ). Opt out of personalised advertising from many other vendors at aboutads.info/choices or, in Europe, youronlinechoices.eu . Block or delete cookies in your browser settings. Doing so does not stop you seeing ads; it means the ones you see are less relevant. Third-party vendors other than Google may also serve ads on this site. Where they do, you can visit their own websites to opt out of their use of cookies for personalised advertising. Google's own explanation of how it uses data from sites that use its services is at policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites . Where the law requires it (including under the GDPR in the EU and UK), you will be asked for consent before any personalised advertising cookies are set, and you can change or withdraw that choice at any time. Purchases In-app purchases are processed by Google Play Billing. We never see or store your payment details; Google handles the transaction. See Google's Privacy Policy for how that information is handled. Analytics Neither our Apps nor this website use third-party analytics tracking. We do not run Google Analytics or any equivalent, and we do not build advertising or marketing profiles from anyone's visit. (If this changes in the future, we will update this policy to disclose it.) Information sharing We do not sell your information. We do not share personal information with third parties except as needed to provide the services described above (for example, Google AdMob and Google Play Billing). Children's privacy Our Apps are not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children. Security Because your tracking data stays on your device, its security is tied to your device's own protections. We encourage you to use a device passcode and keep your software up to date. Changes to this policy We may update this policy from time to time. Material changes will be posted on this page with a new effective date. Contact For questions about this policy, email contact@dlonem.com .

docs.t: How to Quit Nicotine: Cigarettes, Vapes and Pouches
docs.x: Quitting nicotine Quitting nicotine A plan for cigarettes, vapes and pouches: pick the day, choose your support, and get through the weeks that decide it. Start here What this guide covers From Dlonem · Updated 27 September 2026 · General information, not medical advice The Nicotine Break Buddy page covers what nicotine does to your brain, the withdrawal timeline, and what the big trials say about quitting in general. This guide is the plan: choosing a day, choosing your support, what is different about vapes and pouches, and the things that catch people out in the first weeks. Quitting is much more likely to work with real support. Talk to a pharmacist or doctor about medication before your quit day. Step one Pick a quit day Smokefree.gov, run by the US National Cancer Institute, says to pick a day in the next two weeks: close enough that you do not lose your nerve, far enough away to get ready. The Institute's older quit booklet sums up the preparation in five steps, which work just as well for vapes and pouches as for cigarettes: Set a quit date. Tell family, friends and coworkers that you plan to quit. Anticipate the challenges you will face, and plan for them. Remove every product from your home, car, bag and desk: packs, pods, disposables, pouch tins, lighters. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist about help to quit. Step two Choose your medication before the day Nicotine replacement works better when you use it well, and the research is specific about what well means: Use two forms together. A patch for the steady background dose plus a fast-acting form (gum, lozenge, spray or inhaler) for cravings. Across 16 trials and more than 12,000 people, combining them raised long-term quit rates by about a quarter over using one form alone. The evidence is rated high certainty. Consider starting before quit day. Wearing the patch for a while before you stop, known as preloading, raised quit rates by about a quarter across nine trials. That evidence is moderate certainty. Ask a pharmacist how to do it. A bigger patch is not better. In the same review, a 42 or 44 mg patch did no better than the standard 21 or 22 mg one. Prescription options. Varenicline has some of the strongest evidence of any quit medication, and your doctor can say whether it suits you. Cytisine, a plant-derived medicine that works in a similar way, helped more people quit than placebo in the latest Cochrane review, and in the two trials comparing it with varenicline there was no clear difference, though that comparison is low certainty. It is prescription-only in the UK and sold over the counter in Canada and Poland. As of September 2026 it is not approved in the US: in June 2026 the FDA declined to approve it for now, citing manufacturing and labeling issues and not safety or effectiveness, and the company plans to reapply. One thing that is not a quit aid: nicotine pouches. The FDA has authorized some pouch products to be sold, which is not the same as approval, and none are approved to help people quit. Step three Line up a person, or a phone Call a quitline. In the US, 1-800-QUIT-NOW (or 1-855-DÉJELO-YA in Spanish) transfers you to your state's quitline, which is free and confidential. Coaches can help you get medication through your insurance or local programs. Among people who had already called a quitline, extra phone counselling raised the chance of quitting from about 7% to 10%. Or sign up for texts. Automated text programs raise quit rates compared with minimal support, according to a Cochrane review that rates the evidence as moderate certainty. Three free ones: SmokefreeTXT: text QUIT to 47848. It runs for six to eight weeks. CDC's texting portal: text QUITNOW to 333888. EX Program by Truth Initiative, which now includes the This is Quitting vaping program: text EXPROGRAM to 88709. It is open to anyone 13 or older. Message and data rates may apply. Not just cigarettes Vapes and pouches Quitting a vape or pouch habit starts with working out how much nicotine you actually take, and that is harder than counting cigarettes. Vapes. In US sales data, the average nicotine concentration of disposable vapes rose to 48.5 mg/mL by mid-2024, and the average amount of liquid in each device grew from 1.6 mL to 11.7 mL. One disposable can hold far more nicotine than it looks like. The UK caps e-liquid at 20 mg/mL and tanks at 2 mL. Nicotine salts, used in most disposables, let people take high levels without the harshness that would otherwise stop them. Pouches. US products tested by the CDC ranged from about 1.3 to 6.1 mg of nicotine per pouch. European products tested in another study reached 47.5 mg per pouch. Check the tin, and count pouches per day, not tins per week. What helps people quit vaping. The evidence is newer but growing: In a 2025 trial of 16 to 25-year-olds who vaped but did not smoke, 51% of those given varenicline were abstinent in weeks 9 to 12, against 14% on placebo; both groups also got counselling. By weeks 9 to 24 it was 28% against 7%. In trials of the This is Quitting text program, 24% of young adults quit, against 19% of those without it, and among teens 38% against 28%. A 2025 Cochrane review concluded that varenicline may help people stop vaping and text-message programs may help young people. For combination nicotine replacement and cytisine, the evidence on vaping is still inconclusive. The first weeks Three things that catch people out Alcohol. Smokefree.gov puts it plainly: for many people alcohol is a trigger that makes them want to smoke, and it makes you more likely to act without thinking it through. A 2023 review found drinking linked to lower quit success in 20 of 27 studies. Stay away from it for the first few weeks if you can. Coffee, if you smoked. Tobacco smoke speeds up the enzyme that clears caffeine; smokers clear it about 56% faster. When you stop smoking, that effect fades within days: in one study, caffeine clearance fell by about a third, and in another, four days off cigarettes raised the amount of caffeine in the blood over a day by 46%. Levels can stay higher for months. The result is that your usual coffee hits harder, and the jitters and poor sleep that follow are easy to mistake for nicotine withdrawal. New Zealand's medicines regulator suggests halving your caffeine when you quit. This comes from the smoke, not the nicotine. It happens when you stop smoking even if you use nicotine replacement, and it does not apply if what you are quitting is a vape or pouches. The caffeine guide shows how to count and cut back. Your other medicines, if you smoked. The same enzyme handles several prescription drugs. Doses of clozapine, olanzapine, theophylline and warfarin may need to come down when a smoker quits. If you take any of these, tell your prescriber before your quit day, not after. The target Aim for 28 days The NHS sets the first goal at 28 days without smoking, because people who reach it are five times more likely to quit for good. It turns an open-ended promise into a date on the calendar, and most of the hardest stretch is behind you well before you get there. If it happens If you slip A slip is not the end of the attempt. Smokefree.gov says it directly: you have not failed and you are not back to square one, and most people need several tries before they stop for good. What you do in the next hour matters more than the slip itself: Get rid of the rest. Do not keep the pack, the disposable or the tin "to finish it." Go back to the plan straight away, the same day. Not on Monday. Work out what set it off: the place, the time, the person, the drink. Check your medication. Are you using the patch every day and the fast-acting form when cravings hit, as directed? Under-dosing is a common reason cravings win. The app Keep count Nicotine Break Buddy is the tracker I built for this. It works for cigarettes, vapes, pouches and dip, and has a 60-second breathing timer for riding out a craving, quick daily check-ins, money saved counting up, and a Comeback badge for logging a slip instead of hiding it. It needs no account, and nothing you enter leaves your phone. It is free on Android: get it here . Taking a break from something else?
