docs.t: How to Quit Nicotine: Cigarettes, Vapes and Pouches
docs.x: Start here From Dlonem · Updated 27 September 2026 · General information, not medical advice The Nicotine Break Buddy page covers what nicotine does to your brain, the withdrawal timeline, and what the big trials say about quitting in general. This guide is the plan: choosing a day, choosing your support, what is different about vapes and pouches, and the things that catch people out in the first weeks. Quitting is much more likely to work with real support. Talk to a pharmacist or doctor about medication before your quit day.

docs.t: How to Quit Nicotine: Cigarettes, Vapes and Pouches
docs.x: Step one Smokefree.gov, run by the US National Cancer Institute, says to pick a day in the next two weeks: close enough that you do not lose your nerve, far enough away to get ready. The Institute's older quit booklet sums up the preparation in five steps, which work just as well for vapes and pouches as for cigarettes: Set a quit date. Tell family, friends and coworkers that you plan to quit. Anticipate the challenges you will face, and plan for them. Remove every product from your home, car, bag and desk: packs, pods, disposables, pouch tins, lighters. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist about help to quit.

docs.t: How to Quit Nicotine: Cigarettes, Vapes and Pouches
docs.s: Choose your medication before the day
docs.x: Step two Nicotine replacement works better when you use it well, and the research is specific about what well means: Use two forms together. A patch for the steady background dose plus a fast-acting form (gum, lozenge, spray or inhaler) for cravings. Across 16 trials and more than 12,000 people, combining them raised long-term quit rates by about a quarter over using one form alone. The evidence is rated high certainty. Consider starting before quit day. Wearing the patch for a while before you stop, known as preloading, raised quit rates by about a quarter across nine trials. That evidence is moderate certainty. Ask a pharmacist how to do it. A bigger patch is not better. In the same review, a 42 or 44 mg patch did no better than the standard 21 or 22 mg one. Prescription options. Varenicline has some of the strongest evidence of any quit medication, and your doctor can say whether it suits you. Cytisine, a plant-derived medicine that works in a similar way, helped more people quit than placebo in the latest Cochrane review, and in the two trials comparing it with varenicline there was no clear difference, though that comparison is low certainty. It is prescription-only in the UK and sold over the counter in Canada and Poland. As of September 2026 it is not approved in the US: in June 2026 the FDA declined to approve it for now, citing manufacturing and labeling issues and not safety or effectiveness, and the company plans to reapply. One thing that is not a quit aid: nicotine pouches. The FDA has authorized some pouch products to be sold, which is not the same as approval, and none are approved to help people quit.

docs.t: How to Quit Nicotine: Cigarettes, Vapes and Pouches
docs.s: Line up a person, or a phone
docs.x: Step three Call a quitline. In the US, 1-800-QUIT-NOW (or 1-855-DÉJELO-YA in Spanish) transfers you to your state's quitline, which is free and confidential. Coaches can help you get medication through your insurance or local programs. Among people who had already called a quitline, extra phone counselling raised the chance of quitting from about 7% to 10%. Or sign up for texts. Automated text programs raise quit rates compared with minimal support, according to a Cochrane review that rates the evidence as moderate certainty. Three free ones: SmokefreeTXT: text QUIT to 47848. It runs for six to eight weeks. CDC's texting portal: text QUITNOW to 333888. EX Program by Truth Initiative, which now includes the This is Quitting vaping program: text EXPROGRAM to 88709. It is open to anyone 13 or older. Message and data rates may apply.

docs.t: How to Quit Nicotine: Cigarettes, Vapes and Pouches
docs.x: Not just cigarettes Quitting a vape or pouch habit starts with working out how much nicotine you actually take, and that is harder than counting cigarettes. Vapes. In US sales data, the average nicotine concentration of disposable vapes rose to 48.5 mg/mL by mid-2024, and the average amount of liquid in each device grew from 1.6 mL to 11.7 mL. One disposable can hold far more nicotine than it looks like. The UK caps e-liquid at 20 mg/mL and tanks at 2 mL. Nicotine salts, used in most disposables, let people take high levels without the harshness that would otherwise stop them. Pouches. US products tested by the CDC ranged from about 1.3 to 6.1 mg of nicotine per pouch. European products tested in another study reached 47.5 mg per pouch. Check the tin, and count pouches per day, not tins per week. What helps people quit vaping. The evidence is newer but growing: In a 2025 trial of 16 to 25-year-olds who vaped but did not smoke, 51% of those given varenicline were abstinent in weeks 9 to 12, against 14% on placebo; both groups also got counselling. By weeks 9 to 24 it was 28% against 7%. In trials of the This is Quitting text program, 24% of young adults quit, against 19% of those without it, and among teens 38% against 28%. A 2025 Cochrane review concluded that varenicline may help people stop vaping and text-message programs may help young people. For combination nicotine replacement and cytisine, the evidence on vaping is still inconclusive.

docs.t: How to Quit Nicotine: Cigarettes, Vapes and Pouches
docs.s: Three things that catch people out
docs.x: The first weeks Alcohol. Smokefree.gov puts it plainly: for many people alcohol is a trigger that makes them want to smoke, and it makes you more likely to act without thinking it through. A 2023 review found drinking linked to lower quit success in 20 of 27 studies. Stay away from it for the first few weeks if you can. Coffee, if you smoked. Tobacco smoke speeds up the enzyme that clears caffeine; smokers clear it about 56% faster. When you stop smoking, that effect fades within days: in one study, caffeine clearance fell by about a third, and in another, four days off cigarettes raised the amount of caffeine in the blood over a day by 46%. Levels can stay higher for months. The result is that your usual coffee hits harder, and the jitters and poor sleep that follow are easy to mistake for nicotine withdrawal. New Zealand's medicines regulator suggests halving your caffeine when you quit. This comes from the smoke, not the nicotine. It happens when you stop smoking even if you use nicotine replacement, and it does not apply if what you are quitting is a vape or pouches. The caffeine guide shows how to count and cut back. Your other medicines, if you smoked. The same enzyme handles several prescription drugs. Doses of clozapine, olanzapine, theophylline and warfarin may need to come down when a smoker quits. If you take any of these, tell your prescriber before your quit day, not after.

docs.t: How to Quit Nicotine: Cigarettes, Vapes and Pouches
docs.x: The target The NHS sets the first goal at 28 days without smoking, because people who reach it are five times more likely to quit for good. It turns an open-ended promise into a date on the calendar, and most of the hardest stretch is behind you well before you get there.

docs.t: How to Quit Nicotine: Cigarettes, Vapes and Pouches
docs.x: If it happens A slip is not the end of the attempt. Smokefree.gov says it directly: you have not failed and you are not back to square one, and most people need several tries before they stop for good. What you do in the next hour matters more than the slip itself: Get rid of the rest. Do not keep the pack, the disposable or the tin "to finish it." Go back to the plan straight away, the same day. Not on Monday. Work out what set it off: the place, the time, the person, the drink. Check your medication. Are you using the patch every day and the fast-acting form when cravings hit, as directed? Under-dosing is a common reason cravings win.

It works for cigarettes, vapes, pouches and dip, and has a 60-second breathing timer for riding out a craving, quick daily check-ins, money saved counting up, and a Comeback badge for logging a slip instead of hiding it. docs.t: Support — help with Dlonem apps and CK3 mods
docs.x: Support Get help If you found a bug, hit a snag, or have a feature idea, I’d like to hear about it. Everything here reaches one person (me), so be as specific as you like. Email contact@dlonem.com Home › Support Where to write Anything sent to contact@dlonem.com reaches me, so if you are unsure, use that. If you already know which app you are writing about, its own address gets there a step faster. Each one is listed on that app’s privacy policy page , alongside the policy itself. Replies come from officialdlonem@gmail.com . That is us, not spam; the @dlonem.com addresses receive mail but cannot send it. For the Crusader Kings III mods, Discord is faster than email. Bug reports land in front of me and the rest of the community at the same time, and someone has usually hit your problem already: The Long Night Discord , for The Long Night & Azor Ahai Supernatural Discord , for the Supernatural mod Getting a faster answer I aim to respond within a few business days. To help me help you faster, include: The app or mod name , for example Tiny Dragon Hoard or The Long Night Your device model and Android/iOS version, or for a mod, your CK3 and AGOT versions What you expected to happen, and what happened instead For a mod, your load order and any other mods you are running (most mod problems turn out to be two mods disagreeing) A screenshot is worth several paragraphs. If an app crashed, telling me what you tapped immediately before it happened is usually the single most useful detail. Questions that come up a lot Where is my tracking data stored? On your device. The Break Buddy apps keep what you enter (history, notes and reminders) locally. I do not collect it, and I cannot read it. That is also why I cannot recover it for you if a phone is lost, which is what the in-app backup export is for. Do I need an account? No. None of the apps need an account. Tiny Dragon Hoard offers an optional Google Play Games sign-in for leaderboards and achievements; everything else works without signing in to anything. Is there a subscription? No. The apps are free, and where there is a paid unlock it is a one-time purchase. I am not going to charge you monthly for a habit tracker. I bought the unlock and changed phones. How do I get it back? Your unlock is tied to the store account you bought it with, so signing in to the same Google Play or App Store account restores it. Note that restoring one of the app’s own backup files will not carry the unlock across. Entitlement always comes from the store, never from an imported file, and the apps are written to keep it that way. When is the iOS version out? THC Break Buddy is on the App Store now. Caffeine Break Buddy, Nicotine Break Buddy and Tiny Dragon Hoard are Android-only for the moment. Each app page shows its current status on both stores. That is the page I keep up to date, so it will always be ahead of anything I could write here. A mod is not working. What should I check first? Load order and conflicting mods, in that order. Both mod pages carry their own FAQ covering load order, compatibility with other mods, and whether you need to start a new save; see The Long Night & Azor Ahai or Supernatural . If you are running both of my mods together, you also need the compatibility patch, which is explained on the mods page . Can I install the mods without Steam? Yes. Both mods have a manual download route with step-by-step instructions, linked from the mods page . Something in an app looks wrong or overlaps If text is colliding or a ring looks squashed, check your phone’s system font-size setting first. A very large display font can push layouts past what they were designed for. Tell me your font-size setting when you report it and it saves us both a round trip. Feature ideas Feature ideas are welcome, and a fair number of the things in these apps started as somebody’s email. I cannot promise a timeline, and I will tell you if something does not fit the app rather than leaving you waiting on it.

docs.t: The Game Center — a Discord server since 2016
docs.x: Est. May 2016 The Game Center The first server I ever made, and the one that turned into a community by accident. It is still running. How it started The real reason I made it In May 2016 my friend group was still calling each other on Skype, which meant somebody had to start the call and everybody had to be there for it. I found Discord before most people had heard of it, showed everyone, and they took to it immediately. I will be honest about the next part, because it is the real reason. I made the server because I wanted to be the one who owned it. I could see where this was going and I wanted to get there first. It is not a noble founding story, but it is a true one. It began as a room for fewer than fifty people to play Dota in, with a plain controller icon and no ambitions. Within a year there were two hundred and fifty of us. People brought friends, those friends brought friends, and at some point it stopped being a group chat. The first website Eight characters you cannot copy Here is a problem that sounds trivial and was not. You cannot copy and paste out of a video game. If you met someone in a match and wanted to invite them, you had to read eight random characters aloud and hope they typed them correctly. So I built a website. One page, one button. Go to the address, click join, you are in the room. That was the whole product, and it worked. I was not a web developer and it showed. That site is long gone, but the idea was right. This page is the same idea, built with more care, nine years later. The point of it Especially the quiet ones In 2017 I wrote myself a set of messages to send to people who had joined and then never said anything. It was not a moderation thing; I did not like the idea of somebody sitting in a server for months feeling like they were not part of it. One was written specifically for people who do not talk because they are shy, or because walking into a room where everyone already knows each other is hard. The gist of it: the regulars are good people, we post nonsense daily, and not knowing anyone yet should not be the thing that stops you. That is still the idea. I wanted the bar where everybody knows your name, with considerably more Dota. The hard part Keeping a room comfortable Wanting a place where quiet people feel welcome sounds simple until you have to enforce it. It started with slurs, which was easy; nobody serious argued the point. Then it was people telling each other to go kill themselves, and that is where I stopped treating any of it as banter. I brought in bots that caught those phrases, deleted the message, and sometimes removed the person with it. Then came the pushback: too much censorship. I never agreed and I still do not. What got removed was a short list of things whose only purpose is to make somebody feel small. Everything else was fair game. We opened an uncensored channel where anyone could say whatever they liked, and almost nobody used it, which told me the objection was never about wanting to say those things. A server where the loudest people set the rules is a server the quiet ones leave, without saying anything. What we did Game nights and Christmas mugs We ran Dota 2 in-house nights: twelve against twelve, any rank welcome, a voice channel per team, with fallbacks for when not enough people turned up. In hindsight they were held together with tape: I was organising instead of playing and the teams were assembled largely on vibes. They were also some of the best nights the server ever had. For four Decembers I ran holiday giveaways: mugs, shirts, stickers, and a pile of games bought out of my own pocket. No sponsor and no angle. People had been good to each other all year and it seemed like the right way to say so. I stopped after 2021, which felt like the right place to stop. The trade What it cost The server worked. That is also what broke it for the people who were there first. The original group slowly stopped showing up: too many people, too many strangers, too much noise. One of my oldest friends has never liked being in a room with people he does not know, and by then that is exactly what this was. I spent years pushing to get more people in, which was the same act as pushing my friends out. I did not see it that way at the time. So I made them a smaller, private one instead, and that is the one they still use. Which brings me back to owning things. I like making things I control (servers, apps, mods, this website). I hardly ever use the power, but I like having it, because I do not entirely trust other people with it. That is why it took me so long to hand anyone else the keys, and why some of the drama that eventually split the server was other people wanting exactly the same thing. Years on A tenth of a percent Someone who joined here as a teenager and left for college once told me this was the server he grew up in. You cannot design that. You can only leave the door open long enough for it to happen to somebody. I figure I own about a tenth of a percent of a lot of people's brains. Somebody mentions Discord servers, and somewhere out there a person goes: oh, The Game Center — yeah, I used to be in that. It happened almost entirely because I would not stop asking people to join. The door is still open If that invite ever stops working, this one goes to the same place. The other rooms There are four more The Game Center is the oldest of five Discord servers I run, and the rest are on the Community page . Dlonem's Den goes with the YouTube channel ; two are for my Crusader Kings III mods, The Long Night & Azor Ahai and Supernatural ; and the newest, The Grey Company , is a guild for World of Warcraft: Forever. Inviting people to it from inside the game is the same eight-characters problem all over again, so it got the same fix: a short web address instead of a code.

docs.t: How to Take a Tolerance Break That Sticks
docs.x: Cannabis tolerance break Taking a tolerance break How long to go, how to get ready, how to get through the nights, and how to come back without undoing it. Start here What this guide covers From Dlonem · Updated 27 September 2026 · General information, not medical advice The THC Break Buddy page explains why tolerance happens and what each stretch of a break feels like, day by day. This guide covers everything around a tolerance break, or T-break as most people call it: choosing a length, getting ready, getting through the nights, and what to do on the last day so you are not back here in two months. If you use cannabis for a diagnosed condition, plan any break with the clinician who knows about it. Choosing a length How long it needs to be Two brain-imaging studies have tracked what happens to cannabinoid (CB1) receptors when daily users stop. In the first, heavy users had about 20% fewer receptors than non-users in parts of the brain, and after roughly four weeks of monitored abstinence the gap was gone. The second scanned 11 cannabis-dependent men: their receptors were about 15% lower at the start, the difference was no longer significant after just two days, and it was still gone at day 28. It was a small study of men only, so read it as "recovery starts quickly," not "two days is enough." What those scans measure is receptors. How strongly you feel the effect afterwards has not been measured the same way, so the length you choose is partly a judgment call. The withdrawal timeline is the other half of it. In the study that mapped it, symptoms usually began on days one to three, peaked between days two and six, and mostly lasted four to fourteen days. Length What you get 2 to 4 days Receptor recovery has started, but you stop in the middle of the worst stretch. All of the discomfort, little of the payoff. About 2 weeks For most people the withdrawal is over and the break has stopped being hard. About 4 weeks The point at which both imaging studies found receptor levels no different from non-users. Longer than a month Worth it if the goal is to change the pattern and not only the tolerance. See the section on coming back . The week before Getting ready Count forward from your start day. Days two to six are the hard ones, so look at what falls on them. A start day that puts day four on a work deadline or a family visit is a start day worth moving. Decide what happens to what is left. Finish it before day one, give it away, or put it somewhere that takes real effort to reach. More breaks end because something was within arm's reach at 11pm than because of a craving that could not be managed. If you mix with tobacco, decide about that now. Spliffs and blunts mean a cannabis break is also a nicotine break unless you keep smoking tobacco on its own. In a small study, stopping both at once was harder than stopping either alone for the first few days, though the difference was short-lived and varied from person to person. In another, cigarette use went up by about 14 a week during a two-week cannabis break, and poor sleep predicted who smoked more. Either plan can work. Know which one you are on before day one, and if you are stopping both, the nicotine guide covers that side. Set up sleep before you need it. Pick a wake-up time you will keep every day of the break, and set a caffeine cutoff. In a sleep-lab study, 400 mg of caffeine taken six hours before bed still cut total sleep by more than an hour. The caffeine guide has a way to count what you actually drink. Know what the first week will feel like, and why. Anxiety, irritability, low mood and trouble sleeping are all on the formal list of cannabis withdrawal symptoms. If those are the reasons you use, the first week can feel like proof that you need it. It is withdrawal, and it passes on the schedule above. Not everyone's week is the same Why some breaks are harder A 2020 review of 47 studies and more than 23,000 people found cannabis withdrawal syndrome in about 47% of regular users. It was more common with daily use and with tobacco use alongside cannabis. A separate review puts it simply: the heavier and longer the use before stopping, the stronger the withdrawal. Potency matters in a related way. Frequent use of high-potency cannabis has been linked to more severe dependence, while low-potency use was not associated with dependence in the same study. Concentrate users have shown greater physiological dependence even after accounting for other factors. Neither study measured withdrawal directly, so treat it as a reason to plan for a rougher first week, not as a prediction. Women also tend to report stronger withdrawal, including physical symptoms such as nausea and stomach pain. If you use daily, use concentrates or mix with tobacco, give yourself the longer runway: a start day with a quiet week after it, and the sleep setup below in place from the first night. Sleep Getting through the nights Sleep is where most breaks are won or lost. In sleep-lab studies, heavy users slept less and spent less time in deep sleep during their first nights off. In one that recorded people across nearly two weeks of abstinence, total sleep and sleep efficiency went down while time spent awake in the night went up. Strange, vivid dreams are one of the most common complaints, and in one outpatient study sleep trouble and odd dreams were still being reported up to seven weeks in. The research does not agree on the details of what changes, but it agrees that sleep gets worse before it gets better. The techniques that work for insomnia generally work here too: Get up at the same time every day, including after a bad night. It is the single anchor the rest depends on. Go to bed when you are sleepy, not at a set time because you think you should. If you are still awake after 15 to 20 minutes, get up. Do something calm in low light and go back when you feel sleepy. Lying there trying teaches your brain that bed is where you lie awake. Keep the bed for sleep. No scrolling, no shows in bed while this is going on. Skip long naps. They take the edge off the sleep pressure you need at night. Watch the swap. Alcohol helps you fall asleep, then breaks up sleep in the second half of the night and delays dreaming sleep. In one study, people on a two-week cannabis break drank about eight more standard drinks a week. Another found the increase only in people with a past alcohol problem. If that describes you, it is the part of the break to plan for most carefully. If sleep has not started improving after a few weeks, or you are thinking about sleep medication, that is a conversation for a pharmacist or doctor. After When the break ends How a break ends matters as much as how long it lasts. A 2023 study followed 170 young adults for six months. Those who took breaks specifically to lower their tolerance were using more hazardously six months later, while those who took longer breaks for other reasons were using less. It was an observational study, so it cannot show the break caused anything. It does match the rest of the research, which consistently ties tolerance to how often you use: regular users feel less from the same amount, and more frequent use goes with a weaker high. Return to the old frequency and you are rebuilding the old tolerance. So decide the pattern before the last day, and write it down: How many days a week, and which ones. This is the number that does the most to keep tolerance down. How much, to start. Much less than you used to. Your tolerance is lower than your habits remember. What you use. Lower-potency products were not associated with dependence in the research above; high-potency ones were. One safety point. Tolerance is partial and it differs by effect. In a study of 122 users, the effect of cannabis on thinking and reaction tests was similar whether people used rarely or heavily. Feeling less high is not the same as being less impaired, and it is not a reason to drive. When it is not about tolerance Signs it is more than a tolerance problem Tolerance and withdrawal are two of the eleven criteria for cannabis use disorder. The others include using more or for longer than intended, repeated attempts to cut down that do not stick, giving up things you care about, and carrying on despite problems it is causing. A diagnosis is a clinician's call and turns on whether use is causing real problems or distress. If you have tried a break several times and never got past the first week, that is worth taking to one. Cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome is worth knowing by name. It shows up in long-term regular users as repeated bouts of severe nausea and vomiting, often with stomach pain. A strong urge to take hot showers or baths, which bring relief, is a telltale sign: in a systematic review, 92% of cases had it. docs.t: How to Take a Tolerance Break That Sticks
docs.x: Start here From Dlonem · Updated 27 September 2026 · General information, not medical advice The THC Break Buddy page explains why tolerance happens and what each stretch of a break feels like, day by day. This guide covers everything around a tolerance break, or T-break as most people call it: choosing a length, getting ready, getting through the nights, and what to do on the last day so you are not back here in two months. If you use cannabis for a diagnosed condition, plan any break with the clinician who knows about it.

docs.t: How to Take a Tolerance Break That Sticks
docs.s: How long it needs to be
docs.x: Choosing a length Two brain-imaging studies have tracked what happens to cannabinoid (CB1) receptors when daily users stop. In the first, heavy users had about 20% fewer receptors than non-users in parts of the brain, and after roughly four weeks of monitored abstinence the gap was gone. The second scanned 11 cannabis-dependent men: their receptors were about 15% lower at the start, the difference was no longer significant after just two days, and it was still gone at day 28. It was a small study of men only, so read it as "recovery starts quickly," not "two days is enough." What those scans measure is receptors. How strongly you feel the effect afterwards has not been measured the same way, so the length you choose is partly a judgment call. The withdrawal timeline is the other half of it. In the study that mapped it, symptoms usually began on days one to three, peaked between days two and six, and mostly lasted four to fourteen days. Length What you get 2 to 4 days Receptor recovery has started, but you stop in the middle of the worst stretch. All of the discomfort, little of the payoff. About 2 weeks For most people the withdrawal is over and the break has stopped being hard. About 4 weeks The point at which both imaging studies found receptor levels no different from non-users. Longer than a month Worth it if the goal is to change the pattern and not only the tolerance. See the section on coming back .

docs.t: How to Take a Tolerance Break That Sticks
docs.x: The week before Count forward from your start day. Days two to six are the hard ones, so look at what falls on them. A start day that puts day four on a work deadline or a family visit is a start day worth moving. Decide what happens to what is left. Finish it before day one, give it away, or put it somewhere that takes real effort to reach. More breaks end because something was within arm's reach at 11pm than because of a craving that could not be managed. If you mix with tobacco, decide about that now. Spliffs and blunts mean a cannabis break is also a nicotine break unless you keep smoking tobacco on its own. In a small study, stopping both at once was harder than stopping either alone for the first few days, though the difference was short-lived and varied from person to person. In another, cigarette use went up by about 14 a week during a two-week cannabis break, and poor sleep predicted who smoked more. Either plan can work. Know which one you are on before day one, and if you are stopping both, the nicotine guide covers that side. Set up sleep before you need it. Pick a wake-up time you will keep every day of the break, and set a caffeine cutoff. In a sleep-lab study, 400 mg of caffeine taken six hours before bed still cut total sleep by more than an hour. The caffeine guide has a way to count what you actually drink. Know what the first week will feel like, and why. Anxiety, irritability, low mood and trouble sleeping are all on the formal list of cannabis withdrawal symptoms. If those are the reasons you use, the first week can feel like proof that you need it. It is withdrawal, and it passes on the schedule above.

docs.x: The app THC Break Buddy is the tracker I built for this. It is a day count with the timeline built in, somewhere to note which days were hard and why, and milestones at the points that matter. It needs no account, and nothing you enter leaves your phone. It is free on Android and iPhone: get it here , and the link picks the right store for your phone. Taking a break from something else? There is a guide to cutting back on caffeine and one to quitting nicotine .

docs.t: Choosing your first class in WoW Forever: quiz, roles and races
docs.x: World of Warcraft: Forever Choosing your first class Your class matters far more than your race. Answer five questions for a starting point, then read the cards: what each class does, what Blizzard changed for Forever, and which races can play it. By Thomas, Dlonem · checked 9 October 2026 Home › WoW Forever › Classes 9 classes 10 race options, Skyborne included 6 race and class pairs that are new 10 the level talents start at If you only read one thing The short answer If you are a casual player, or new to WoW, play a Hunter. It is the easiest class to understand. THOMAS, DLONEM A Hunter's pet holds the enemy's attention while you attack from range, so most fights are forgiving. Warrior and Paladin are the other two I would point a new player at. Pick whichever race you like the look of, and play the faction your friends are on. Five questions The quiz Pick one answer for each. Your best fit appears as soon as all five are answered, and nothing is saved or sent. 1 of 5 What do you want to do in a group? Hit things Keep people alive Be the one they hit Not sure yet 2 of 5 Up close or from a distance? Up close From a distance Either 3 of 5 Do you want a pet? Yes, a companion No pet Don't mind 4 of 5 How do you mostly play? On my own With friends A bit of both 5 of 5 How much do you want to juggle? Keep it simple Lots of buttons Somewhere between Start again All nine Every class Roles are the ones Blizzard's class pages describe. Blizzard says an Enhancement Shaman can tank small groups for a while, so Shamans are not listed as tanks. Filter by the role you want, or read straight through. Can Any role Tank Heal Deal damage Hunter Damage A pet holds the enemy while you attack from range, which makes it the easiest class to understand. My pick for a casual or brand-new player. Plan for ammunition and pet taming: years ago, they were the two things that caught me out. Fights: Ranged (Survival fights up close) · Heaviest armor: Mail Specs: Beast Mastery, Marksmanship, Survival Pets gain stats from your gear, and every pet family can learn Bite or Claw. Foxes are a new pet family. Traps work in combat now, and Aimed Shot is a normal ability at level 20. No stuns or interrupts, and ranged attacks do not work within 8 yards. One of the two I would point a new player at, after the Hunter. Fights: Melee · Heaviest armor: Plate Specs: Arms, Fury, Protection Victory Rush arrives at level 20: kill something and you can hit back for a heal. Tactical Mastery is baseline at 14, so you keep 10 Rage when you switch stances. Critical hits give 75% more Rage. Blizzard's warning: few ways to recover from heavy damage. Alliance: Human, Dwarf, Night Elf, Gnome, Skyborne (High Order) Horde: Orc, Undead, Tauren, Troll, Skyborne (Windshaper) Source From the channel Paladin Tank Healer Damage Heavy armor and healing of your own, and it can tank, heal or deal damage. The other class I would point a new player at. Fights: Melee · Heaviest armor: Plate Specs: Holy, Protection, Retribution Undead Paladin is new: in Forever, Horde players can be Paladins. Blessing of Kings is now a normal Paladin spell, not a talent. Human, Dwarf and Undead are the only races that can be one. I took a Human Warlock through the beta, Hall of Thanes included. Fights: Ranged · Heaviest armor: Cloth Specs: Affliction, Demonology, Destruction Troll Warlock is new to the Horde. Cloth armor: let the pet take the hits. Alliance: Human, Gnome Horde: Orc, Undead, Troll Source My Human Warlock re-summoning his Voidwalker in Hall of Thanes. From the channel Healers Watching the Warlock Life Tap Again Mage Damage Strong single-target and area damage, Polymorph for crowd control, and you make your own food and water. Fights: Ranged · Heaviest armor: Cloth Specs: Arcane, Fire, Frost Frostfire Bolt is a new level 40 spell that counts as both Fire and Frost. Orc Mage is new to the Horde. Blizzard's warning: fragile up close. Alliance: Human, Gnome, Skyborne (High Order) Horde: Orc, Undead, Troll Source 1 · Source 2 From the channel Priest Healer Damage Blizzard calls it the most versatile healer in the game. Shadow is its damage spec. Fights: Ranged · Heaviest armor: Cloth Specs: Discipline, Holy, Shadow Fear Ward and Devouring Plague are open to every Priest at level 20. Shadow Word: Death is baseline at 32. Gnome Priest is new to the Alliance. Blizzard's warning: cloth, and few ways to escape. Alliance: Human, Dwarf, Night Elf, Gnome Horde: Undead, Troll Source 1 · Source 2 From the channel Shaman Healer Damage Melee or spell damage, or healing, in mail with a shield, and totems that help the whole group. Fights: Melee or ranged · Heaviest armor: Mail Specs: Elemental, Enhancement, Restoration Dwarf Shaman is new: the Alliance gets Shamans. Totems are on a 1-second global cooldown, and buff totems last 5 minutes. Call of the Elements (level 20) drops all four totems in one cast. Blizzard says Enhancement can tank small groups for a while. Alliance: Dwarf Horde: Orc, Tauren, Troll, Skyborne (Windshaper) Source From the channel Rogue Damage Melee damage, with stealth to pick your fights. Fights: Melee · Heaviest armor: Leather Specs: Assassination, Combat, Subtlety Damage is the only role. Every race but the Tauren can be one, including both Skyborne. Alliance: Human, Dwarf, Night Elf, Gnome, Skyborne (High Order) Horde: Orc, Undead, Troll, Skyborne (Windshaper) Source From the channel Druid Tank Healer Damage Blizzard says a Druid can fill any role with the right gear and talents. Fights: Melee or ranged · Heaviest armor: Leather Specs: Balance, Feral, Restoration All potions and almost all similar items now work in animal forms. Revive is a new out-of-combat resurrection at level 12. Tiger's Fury is gone, replaced by the Shifting Power talent. No snares, silences or interrupts. Six pairs are new to Forever: Human Hunter , Dwarf Shaman , Gnome Priest , Orc Mage , Undead Paladin and Troll Warlock . docs.t: Choosing your first class in WoW Forever: quiz, roles and races
docs.x: Once you have chosen You learn spells from your class trainer as you level, and they cost gold. Visit one every couple of levels. Talents start at level 10. Each tree has bigger talents at 11, 16, 21 and 31 points; the 16-point one is new to Forever. To change your talents, visit a class trainer in a major city. Dual specialization arrives at level 40, so you can keep two sets of talents. From Blizzard's Hunter and Druid , Mage and Shaman and Priest and Warrior deep dives.

docs.t: Choosing your first class in WoW Forever: quiz, roles and races
docs.x: Quick answers What is the easiest class in WoW Forever? For a new or casual player, the Hunter. Your pet holds the enemy while you attack from range. Watch your ammunition and your pet's level when you tame a new one. Does my race matter? Much less than your class. Pick the look you like and the faction your friends are on. Race does decide which classes you can play, so check the table . Which classes can tank? Warriors, Paladins and Druids. Blizzard also says an Enhancement Shaman can tank small groups for a while. Which classes can heal? Priests, Paladins, Shamans and Druids. What are the new race and class combinations? Human Hunter, Dwarf Shaman, Gnome Priest, Orc Mage, Undead Paladin and Troll Warlock, plus the new Skyborne race. Can I change my mind later? Not on the same character: your class is for good. Everyone starts at level 1 in Forever, and there is no character boost.

docs.x: WoW Forever dungeon guide Hall of Thanes The first new dungeon most Alliance players will see in Forever, beneath Ironforge. How to find the door, which quests to pick up first, all four bosses, and what my own beta run as a level 13 Human Warlock taught me. The pictures are from that run. By Thomas, Dlonem · checked 9 October 2026 · pictures from my own beta stream Home › WoW Forever › Dungeons › Hall of Thanes 13–18 levels, per Blizzard 5 players 4 bosses 5 quests From my beta stream Watch the run I streamed my first trip through the Hall during the Forever beta. These links jump straight to each part on YouTube. WoW Forever Beta: Hall of Thanes Dungeon + Alliance Questing (Human Warlock) Dun Morogh questing first, then the walk down from the High Seat and the dungeon itself. 29:28 The cobwebbed passage 30:28 Stairs down 33:18 Dungeon Journal at the door 51:58 Faldrim Anvilmar 1:02:58 Anvilmar's Rest 1:20:28 Magmatus Checklist Before you go Tick these off as you go. The page remembers them in this browser, and nothing is sent anywhere. Be level 13 or higher. I went in at 13. The trash hits hard if you are under the range. Start the Dun Morogh chain first. Old Ironforge Incursion, the dungeon's main quest, comes from Earthseer Farsen after you find a Dark Iron Map. The chain, step by step. Pick up the two quests at the door. Important Heirlooms and The Restless Dead start just outside the dungeon. Pick an honest playstyle in Group Finder. First time through? Choose Learning . Bring a way to cure a disease. Bloodhound Runts stack Infected Wounds . A cleanse, Simple Poultices from First Aid, or a Dwarf's Stoneform all work. Empty some bag space. You will be picking up eight heirlooms and loot. Leave yourself time. A first run can take well over an hour; mine did. Clear the list Ironforge Getting there The Hall is in Old Ironforge, the part of the city beneath the High Seat. The way in is easy to walk past. Start at the Great Forge in the middle of Ironforge and face the High Seat , where King Magni stands. Walk into the king's hall and turn left. Look for a passage covered in cobwebs. Warcraft Tavern puts it at 43.5, 52.0 ; my minimap read 46.3, 52.3 as I went through. Follow it down the stairs. I passed 38.1, 52.9 on the way. The portal is at the bottom, around 28.4, 47.8 . Mind your footing on the way down: the city is built over lava, and a fall is fatal. Step 2. The cobwebbed passage off the king's hall. Step 3. The stairs down into Old Ironforge. Step 4. The portal. In my run the minimap read 28.4, 47.8 here. Other players' names are blurred. Five quests The quests The Dungeon Journal lists five quests for the Hall. Three you can pick up at the door or inside. The main one starts out in Dun Morogh, and the last one starts at the end of the dungeon. The Dungeon Journal at the door , from my beta run: five quests, and the reward choices for Old Ironforge Incursion. The beta's journal listed the dungeon as LV 13-20; Blizzard's beta post says 13 to 18. The main quest: Old Ironforge Incursion A Visitor to Dun Morogh → Farsen's Watch → Nip 'Em in the Bud → Underground Map → Old Ironforge Incursion Beldin Steelgrill at Steelgrill's Depot sends you to Earthseer Farsen, outside Ironforge at 64.8, 58.5 . Farsen asks you to kill Dark Iron Spies around 76.7, 60.7 , and one of them drops a Dark Iron Map . Use the map and take it back to Farsen (in my quest log that step read "Deliver the Dark Iron Map to Earthseer Farsen in Dun Morogh"). He then gives you Old Ironforge Incursion : kill Durgen Dirgehammer, the last boss, and take his head to King Magni. The reward in my journal was a choice of the Calibrated Blunderbuss , the Ironforge Greathammer or Deepblaze , plus 3,200 experience and reputation with Ironforge and the Gnomeregan Exiles. Those are beta numbers and can change. The other four Important Heirlooms Thom Filch, outside, by the bridge leading in Collect 8 Dwarven Heirlooms. They sit on raised, candle-lit platforms along the corridors, and the vaults in the last room hold enough for everyone. Reward: Dwarven Tome (off-hand) The Restless Dead Afadra Dunwall, up the stairs on the way in Kill 15 Enraged Apparitions and 10 Tormented Souls, the ghosts in the first rooms. You will kill most of them anyway. An Ancient Grudge Ghostly Attendant, in the second room Kill Faldrim Anvilmar, the first boss. If you walk out instead of using your Hearthstone, you pass the Attendant again to hand it in. Reward: Catacomb Cloak The Treaty of Understanding A tablet in a vault in the last room Take it to King Magni in Ironforge. It is an experience quest. Old Ironforge Incursion goes to him too. Layout The route The Hall is small, but the corridors look alike and it can feel like a maze. This is the order most groups take, from Warcraft Tavern's map. Tap a boss to jump to its tactics. 1 The entrance Tormented Souls and Enraged Apparitions, both for The Restless Dead. Then west, down the left corridor. 2 The Ghostly Attendant Pick up An Ancient Grudge. B1 Anvilmar's Rest A big chamber around a huge tomb, full of ghosts. Faldrim Anvilmar . 3 The south-east corridor Dark Iron Dwarves: Looters, Bloodhound Runts, Engineers and Summoners, and kegs of blasting powder. B2 A natural cavern The carved tombs give way to raw rock. Magmatus . 4 Back into the Hall A pack of four Dark Iron Dwarves with two kegs beside them. B3 The hallway A stone golem on patrol. Plunder . 5 The bridge Lesser Stone Golems stand guard. Cross north. B4 The Reliquary of Kings A round room lined with vault doors. Durgen Dirgehammer , and the Treaty tablet. Anvilmar's Rest , the tomb chamber, halfway through Important Heirlooms (4 of 8). Other players' names are blurred. Four fights The bosses Tactics from Wowhead's and Warcraft Tavern's walkthroughs, checked against what I saw in my run. Pick your role to see only your part. Show tips for Everyone Tank Healer Damage 1 Faldrim Anvilmar Undead · Anvilmar's Rest My Warlock re-summoning his Voidwalker mid-fight, while Faldrim casts Mind Blast. Other players' names are blurred. Mind Blast Anvilmar's Curse Clear the ghosts in the room before you pull. He does not bring them with him, but you want the space. Anvilmar's Curse goes on you: 20% slower attacks and casts for ten minutes, and you become immune to poison and bleed effects. Wowhead calls it nasty; Warcraft Tavern says you can live with it if nobody can remove it. If you can remove curses, take Anvilmar's Curse off the tank. Mind Blast can be interrupted. It is not required, but it saves the healer some mana. Kill him for An Ancient Grudge . 2 Magmatus Elemental · the cavern (my map called it Dark Iron Ingress) Fighting Magmatus. The Dark Iron Summoner beside him is casting Fireball, with a Bloodhound Runt in the same pull. Other players' names are blurred. Fire pulses Combust (on my cast bar) Dark Iron Summoner add Kill the Dark Iron Summoner first, and clear some of the trash around him before you pull. Tank Magmatus away from the group. His fire hits everyone near him. Watch every melee player, not only the tank. The pulses hurt anyone standing close. Ranged: stand back. Melee: keep an eye on your own health. A later attempt, after we had swapped both our tank and our healer. His cast bar reads Combust. 3 Plunder Elemental · a stone golem on patrol in the hallway Knockback Patrols His knockback throws players a long way. Make sure nobody lands in a trash pack that could wipe the group. Pull him away from other enemies and keep his back to a wall, so you always know where the knockback sends people. Stand where a knockback can't throw you into another pack. 4 Durgen Dirgehammer Humanoid · leader of the Dark Iron incursion · the Reliquary of Kings Fear Lesser Stone Golems Clear the trash along the edges of the room, but leave the golems: they are linked to him, and pulling one pulls him. His fear scatters people into anything you left standing. If you do wipe, golems you killed stay dead, so the next pull is easier. When the pull starts, have the group kill the two Lesser Stone Golems first. Fear will scatter the group. A Shaman's Tremor Totem helps; without one, expect to heal people who have run out of range. Golems first, then Durgen. Loot his head for Old Ironforge Incursion . He also drops Durgen's Crescent Axe , a strong one-handed axe. Open the vaults for the Treaty tablet and the last heirlooms. Between the bosses Trash worth knowing The packs are not complicated, but they hit hard, especially if your group is low level or has no crowd control. The ones to know: Bloodhound Runts put a disease called Infected Wounds on you, which raises the physical damage you take for five minutes. Cure it with a cleanse, Simple Poultices from First Aid, or a Dwarf's Stoneform. Dark Iron Engineers throw dynamite that hits an area. Spread out a little. docs.x: Quick answers What level do I need for Hall of Thanes? Blizzard lists it for levels 13 to 18. The beta's own Dungeon Journal said 13 to 20. I went in at 13, and that was fine with a decent group. Where is the entrance? Under the High Seat in Ironforge. Go into the king's hall, turn left into the cobwebbed passage and follow the stairs down. Step by step, with coordinates. Can the Horde run it? It is built for the Alliance, as their answer to the Horde's Ragefire Chasm. Wowhead lists all five quests as Alliance-only, and Warcraft Tavern says Horde players can get in but it is hard at the right level. One thing to watch: in my beta run the Dungeon Journal showed a Horde crest next to An Ancient Grudge and Important Heirlooms, so those two may be open to both factions. How long does it take? 30 minutes to an hour with a group that knows the way. Leave more for a first run. Is it in Group Finder? Yes. You list with a playstyle (Learning, Relaxed, Competitive or Carry Offered). Group Finder does not teleport anyone, so you still walk to the portal. More on that in the beginner's guide .

docs.x: World of Warcraft: Forever WoW Forever dungeons Forever adds nine new dungeons to the original world, in places players have wondered about for years. Here is each one Blizzard has named, what changed about dungeons in general, and my guides as I write them. By Thomas, Dlonem · checked 9 October 2026 Home › WoW Forever › Dungeons 9 new dungeons 5 players a group 4 playstyles in Group Finder 2 level ranges posted by Blizzard From Blizzard's announcement The nine new dungeons Blizzard named all nine in its What's Next panel recap . It has posted level ranges for the two that opened first in the beta. The fan sites that list the rest do not agree with each other, so I will add those as Blizzard confirms them. The nine new dungeons in WoW Forever Dungeon Where Levels What it is Guide Hall of Thanes Beneath Ironforge 13–18 The dwarves' halls under the city, overrun by Dark Iron Dwarves. Read the guide Ruins of Lordaeron The ruined capital, Tirisfal Glades 15–20 Helping the Forsaken reclaim the Ruins of Lordaeron. Not yet The excavation site Above Whelgar's Excavation, Wetlands not posted yet A mysterious dig above the old excavation. Not yet City of Dalaran Dalaran not posted yet Strange magical trouble in the city of mages. Not yet The Drowned City Off the coast of Stranglethorn Vale* not posted yet Naga and pirates. Not yet Krol'dok Stronghold Riverglades* not posted yet Blizzard has not described it yet. Not yet Alcaz Prison Alcaz Island, Dustwallow Marsh not posted yet A prison on Alcaz Island. Not yet Blackmaw Hold Behind Azshara's mysterious gate* not posted yet Corruption stirring in its depths. Not yet Shaper's Terrace Un'Goro Crater not posted yet Titan mysteries in Un'Goro. Not yet * Blizzard's recap names these without saying exactly where they are; the places marked come from Icy Veins' report of the BlizzCon panel . Blizzard's roadmap adds more dungeons in later updates, alongside raids and world content. Written so far Dungeon guides Hall of Thanes : the entrance under Ironforge, the five quests, the route and all four bosses, with pictures from my own run. Read the Hall of Thanes guide Forever's rules What's different about dungeons Every dungeon drop was looked at again. Blizzard says it re-examined every item, and a boss's unique items are now blue (rare) quality. Shared appearances. When an Uncommon or Rare item that binds on pickup drops, its appearance goes to everyone eligible in the group, not only the person who wins it. Recipes from bosses. Advanced Blueprint recipes for professions drop from dungeon bosses. Crowd control matters. Blizzard wants dungeons to stay tactical, where crowd control can be the right answer to a pull. Your ruleset is your pool. You can only group with players on the same ruleset, so pick the one your friends play on. From Blizzard's Deep Dive panel recap . Finding a group Group Finder To list yourself you pick a playstyle: Learning , Relaxed , Competitive or Carry Offered . Group Finder finds the people; it does not build the group for you or teleport anyone, so everyone still walks to the entrance. If it's your first time through a dungeon, Learning is the right pick. THOMAS, DLONEM More on playstyles, and why I wish you could pick more than one, is in the beginner's guide . docs.x: Forever's rules Every dungeon drop was looked at again. Blizzard says it re-examined every item, and a boss's unique items are now blue (rare) quality. Shared appearances. Advanced Blueprint recipes for professions drop from dungeon bosses. Crowd control matters. Blizzard wants dungeons to stay tactical, where crowd control can be the right answer to a pull. Your ruleset is your pool. You can only group with players on the same ruleset, so pick the one your friends play on. From Blizzard's Deep Dive panel recap .

docs.x: World of Warcraft: Forever WoW Forever beginner's guide What to know before your first character, from someone who has played World of Warcraft for about fifteen years and leveled through the Forever beta. The facts are checked against Blizzard's own posts. The opinions are mine. By Thomas, Dlonem · facts checked 8 October 2026 · pictures from my own beta stream 4 Nov 2026 release date 1–60 levels, with no level scaling 4 rulesets to choose from 1,000+ new quests Start here What Forever actually is Blizzard describes Forever as not a mode, a season, or a new version of Classic . It is the original world, levels 1 to 60, built to keep growing instead of resetting. There is no level scaling and no flying, so a zone that is dangerous at level 20 stays dangerous at level 20. There is no WoW Token and no character boost. Everyone starts at level 1. Forever is included with a World of Warcraft subscription or Game Time. There is also no realm list. You pick a ruleset instead: Normal, PvP, Roleplaying or Hardcore. You can only group with players on your own ruleset and faction, so pick the one your friends are on. Switching later means making a new character. Every character has a first and a second name, and the full name has to be unique in your region. If you have played before What returning players get wrong The biggest mistake is assuming you already know it. Forever adds more than a thousand new quests between level 1 and 60, and in my experience nothing in the game tells you which ones are new. I have played through Northshire Valley, the human starting area, something like three dozen times over the years, and I still found a quest there I had never seen. That one is Nibbled-On Book , which starts from a book the kobolds drop and turns into a chain at the abbey library. Keep an eye out for quest givers you don't recognize. If you have only played retail , a few old rules are back: You learn spells from your class trainer as you level, and they cost gold. Visit a trainer every couple of levels. Weapon skills are trained too. Hunters use ammunition. Arrows and bullets run out, so carry plenty. Professions matter. Blizzard added over 600 new recipes, crafted food that gives a small experience bonus, and recipes that drop from dungeon bosses. Talents start at level 10, and dual spec arrives at level 40. Group Finder helps you find people, but it does not build the group for you or teleport anyone. You still travel to the dungeon entrance. Transmog is there if you want it and off if you don't. Your first character Which class to start with If you are a casual player, or new to WoW, play a Hunter. It is the easiest class to understand. You have a pet that holds attention while you attack from range. Race matters much less than class, so pick whatever you like the look of. Horde or Alliance is fine too; I play Alliance because I always have. The two things that caught me out on a Hunter, years ago, were taming a pet and ammunition. You can't tame a beast that is higher level than you. Ammunition is the one to plan for: it runs out mid-quest if you forget it, so buy a stack every time you visit town. In Forever every pet family can learn Bite or Claw, and pets scale with your gear . Warrior and Paladin are the other two I would point a new player at. Still not sure? Choosing your first class has a five-question quiz, every class card and the full race table. Forever also opens up race and class pairs that were never allowed before: Gnome Priest, Human Hunter, Dwarf Shaman, Orc Mage, Troll Warlock and Undead Paladin . There is one new race, the Skyborne. On both factions they can be Druids, Hunters, Rogues or Warriors; Horde Skyborne can also be Shamans, and Alliance Skyborne can also be Mages. They start on Zephras Isle, and access to the race comes with the Forever upgrade packs . 1 to 60 How leveling feels Leveling in Forever is faster than Classic and slower than retail. That is my read rather than a number, and Blizzard has adjusted experience more than once during testing, so I would not trust anyone quoting an exact time to 60. What helps is the usual: questing with other people, logging out in an inn or a city so you build rested experience, and eating crafted food for its small experience bonus. Dun Morogh , on my beta Warlock. The dwarf and gnome starting zone, and where the Hall of Thanes quest chain begins. My favorite new system Camping Camping is the new system I like most. You can build a campfire out in the world, and other players can add to it with their professions. A campsite can offer vendors, repairs, places to craft, and one-hour buffs. Sit by the fire for a moment and you get them. A basic campfire holds three objects, and upgraded fires hold five or ten. Objects unlock at profession skill 20. Blizzard's deep dive has the full list. If you see a campfire with people around it, stop for a minute. A campfire in Gol'Bolar Quarry , Dun Morogh, during the beta. I stopped, sat down, and checked my professions. Other players' names are blurred. Making money Professions and gold Pick up two gathering professions early. Skinning, Mining and Herbalism all pay from the first level, because you can sell what you gather. Once you have some gold and know what you want to make, drop the one that doesn't fit. If I started with Mining and Herbalism and decided to become a Blacksmith, I would keep Mining and drop Herbalism. Pick up everything and sell what you don't need. Vendor trash adds up, and early gold is what pays for your spells at the trainer. Get bags as soon as you can. Buy them, have a Tailor make them, or take them as quest rewards. Some drop at random, so you can get lucky. More bag space means fewer trips back to town. Don't buy gold. During testing Blizzard closed over 2,100 gold-buying accounts , plus around 1,600 that were selling gold or botting. I think of it like a speed limit. Everyone knows it's there, and if you get caught going over it, that's on you. Groups Dungeons and Group Finder To list yourself in Group Finder you have to pick a playstyle : Learning, Relaxed, Competitive or Carry Offered. Be honest with it. On my first Hall of Thanes run I picked Relaxed. Our tank said he was new, and he should have picked Learning. If it's your first time through a dungeon, Learning is the right pick. It is a useful tool, but I would like to be able to choose more than one. Relaxed can read as "not going to try", and Competitive can read as "on a timer". Most groups are somewhere in between. Hall of Thanes is a new dungeon in Old Ironforge, beneath the High Seat, for levels 13 to 18 . It has four bosses: Faldrim Anvilmar, Magmatus, Plunder and Durgen Dirgehammer. Its quests are for the Alliance and start in Dun Morogh. Wowhead's walkthrough covers the route. I describe it as a light warm-up for Blackrock Depths, the level 50 dungeon famous for being a maze. Hall of Thanes is much smaller, but it can feel like a maze in the same way. A group that knows the way should finish in 30 minutes to an hour. My first run took about an hour and a half, after swapping both the tank and the healer. Magmatus , the second boss of Hall of Thanes, from my run. Other players' names are blurred. Everything about the dungeon, with the route, the quests and all four bosses, is in the Hall of Thanes guide . It is one of nine new dungeons in Forever. Another is Ruins of Lordaeron, for levels 15 to 20. All nine are listed on the dungeons page. One life Hardcore Hardcore is its own ruleset, and Blizzard said it would open after the others. It is a closed community: you can't group with players on other rulesets. If a Hardcore character dies, it can transfer to another ruleset , PvP included, and keep playing. I don't plan to play Hardcore. It has never really appealed to me. That transfer rule is the closest it has come, though, because a death sends your character to the rest of the world instead of deleting it. If you try it, be careful, and never walk away from your computer while your character is somewhere dangerous. You never know what will wander past.
